sentences.zh: }}古者天子巡狩之禮，布在方策。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Son of Heaven's ritual of the inspection tour was set forth in the written records.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, the imperial tour-of-inspection rites were laid down in the canonical texts.

sentences.zh: 至秦、漢巡幸，或以厭望氣之祥，或以希神仙之應，煩擾之役，多非舊典。

translations.literal: When it came to the Qin and Han tours of the realm, sometimes they sought auspicious signs from examining the qi of the earth, sometimes they hoped for responses from immortals; such troublesome undertakings mostly departed from the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qin and Han, imperial progresses were often driven by a wish to read earthly omens or to court responses from immortals—labors that stirred up the realm and rarely matched the old canon.

sentences.zh: 唯後漢諸帝，頗有古禮焉。

translations.literal: Only the emperors of the Later Han somewhat preserved the ancient rites.
translations.idiomatic: Only among the Later Han emperors was something of the ancient practice still kept.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝值參分初創，方隅事多，皇輿亟動，略無寧歲。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Wei came to power at the beginning of the tripartite division, affairs in the regions were many; the imperial carriage moved frequently, with scarcely a peaceful year.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei took the throne just as the three realms were being carved out; troubles pressed on every frontier, and the imperial carriage was constantly on the road, with hardly a year of rest.

sentences.zh: 蓋應時之務，又非舊章也。

translations.literal: This was largely a response to the needs of the time, and again was not the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: That answered the exigencies of the age—and again was no return to the old code.

sentences.zh: 明帝凡三東巡，所過存問高年，恤人疾苦，或賜穀帛，有古巡幸之風焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming made three eastern tours in all; wherever he passed he inquired after the aged, showed concern for people's hardships, and sometimes bestowed grain and cloth—there was something of the spirit of the ancient inspection tours.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming toured the east three times in all; along the way he called on the elderly, eased the people's distress, and at times granted grain and cloth—carrying something of the ancient touring spirit.

sentences.zh: 齊王正始元年，巡洛陽，賜高年、力田各有差。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengshi of the Qi king, he toured Luoyang and bestowed gifts on the aged and on those diligent in farming, each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengshi, the Prince of Qi toured Luoyang and rewarded the aged and the diligent farmers, each in due measure.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始四年，詔刺史二千石長吏曰：「古之王者，以歲時巡狩方嶽，其次則二伯述職，不然則行人巡省，撢人誦志。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, an edict to the inspectors, the two-thousand-bushel officials, and the chief local officers said: "The ancient kings, at the proper seasons, toured the sacred mountains of the regions. Next in rank the two lords reported their duties; otherwise envoys made inspection tours, and petitioners recited the people's concerns."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taishi, Emperor Wu of Jin addressed the provincial inspectors and chief local officers: "Ancient kings toured the regional sacred peaks at the turn of the year; failing that, the two chief ministers reported their duties; failing that again, traveling envoys made the rounds and petitioners voiced the people's wishes."

sentences.zh: 故雖幽遐側微，心無壅隔。

translations.literal: Thus even in the most remote and humble places, hearts were not blocked off.
translations.idiomatic: So even in the farthest corners, no heart was shut off from the throne.

sentences.zh: 人情上通，上指遠喻。

translations.literal: Human feelings reached upward, and the ruler's intent was conveyed far abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling flowed upward, and the ruler's will was made known afar.

sentences.zh: 至于鰥寡，罔不得所。

translations.literal: As for widowers and orphans, none failed to find their place.
translations.idiomatic: Even widowers and orphans were given their due.

sentences.zh: 用垂風遺烈，休聲猶存。

translations.literal: By this they left a lasting example, and their fine reputation still endures.
translations.idiomatic: Thus a lasting example was handed down, and their good name still survives.

sentences.zh: 朕在位累載，如臨深泉，夙興夕惕，明發不寐，坐而待旦。

translations.literal: I have been on the throne for many years, as if standing over a deep spring; I rise early and remain wary into the evening, wake at dawn unable to sleep, and sit waiting for daybreak.
translations.idiomatic: Years have passed since I took the throne; I stand as over a deep abyss—rising early, staying watchful into the night, waking at first light unable to rest, sitting until dawn.

sentences.zh: 思四方水旱災眚，為之怛然。

translations.literal: When I think of flood and drought and disasters in the four quarters, I am deeply grieved.
translations.idiomatic: At the thought of flood, drought, and calamity throughout the realm, my heart is stricken.

sentences.zh: 勤躬約己，欲令事事當宜。

translations.literal: I labor in person and restrain myself, wishing that in every matter things may be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: I toil in person and keep myself in check, wanting every affair to be as it should.

sentences.zh: 常恐眾吏用情，誠心未著，萬機兼猥，慮有不周，政刑失謬，而弗獲備覽。

translations.literal: I constantly fear that the multitude of officials may act with partiality, that my sincere intent may not be made clear, that the myriad affairs together may be burdensome and that there may be oversights, that government and punishments may err, and that I may not be able to review them all.
translations.idiomatic: I live in constant fear that officials may bend affairs to private feeling, that my earnest purpose may not get through, that the press of ten thousand matters may leave gaps, and that errors in policy and law may escape my full review.

sentences.zh: 百姓有過，在予一人。

translations.literal: If the common people have faults, the blame lies with me alone.
translations.idiomatic: If the people err, the fault is mine alone.

sentences.zh: 惟歲之不易，未遑卜征巡省之事。

translations.literal: Because the years pass without ease, I have not yet had leisure to choose a day for a tour of inspection.
translations.idiomatic: The years offer no respite; I have not yet been able to set a date for touring and inspecting in person.

sentences.zh: 人之未乂，其何以恤之。

translations.literal: If the people are not yet settled, how can they be comforted?
translations.idiomatic: While the people are still unsettled, how can they be cared for?

sentences.zh: 今使使持節侍中、副給事黃門侍郎，銜命四出，周行天下，親見刺史二千石長吏，申喻朕心懇誠至意，訪求得失損益諸宜，觀省政治，問人間患苦。

translations.literal: Now I send envoys bearing credentials—the Palace Attendant with staff of authority and the Deputy Director of the Yellow Gate Attendants—to go forth in the four directions, travel throughout the realm, meet in person the inspectors, the two-thousand-bushel officials, and the chief local officers, explain my earnest and sincere intent, seek out what should be lost or gained or adjusted, observe government, and inquire into the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: I now dispatch credentialed envoys—the Palace Attendant with full powers and his deputy from the Yellow Gate—to travel the four quarters, meet the inspectors and chief local officers face to face, set forth my earnest intent, seek what should be changed for better or worse, review administration, and ask after the people's suffering.

sentences.zh: 周典有之曰：『其萬民利害為一書，其禮俗政事教治刑禁之逆順為一書，其悖逆暴亂作慝犯令為一書，其札喪凶荒厄貧為一書，其康樂和親安平為一書。

translations.literal: The Zhou canon has it: "The benefits and harms to the myriad people shall be one book; the compliance or violation of rites, customs, government, education, governance, and punishments shall be one book; those who are rebellious, violent, wicked, and who violate orders shall be one book; those afflicted by pestilence, mourning, famine, hardship, and poverty shall be one book; those in health, joy, harmony, kinship, peace, and security shall be one book."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou canon says: "Record the people's gains and losses in one book; record whether rites, customs, government, teaching, and punishments accord or conflict in another; record rebellion, violence, and violation of orders in another; record plague, mourning, famine, and want in another; record health, joy, harmony, and peace in another."

sentences.zh: 每國辨異之，以反命于王，以周知天下之故。

translations.literal: For each state they distinguished the differences and reported back to the king, so that he might thoroughly know the conditions of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Each state's report was distinguished and brought back to the king, that he might know all that happened under heaven.

sentences.zh: 』斯舊章前訓，今率由之。

translations.literal: "This is the old statute and former instruction; now follow it in full."
translations.idiomatic: That is the ancient rule and former teaching; follow it now in full.

sentences.zh: 還具條奏，俾朕昭然鑒于幽遠，若親行焉。

translations.literal: On your return present a detailed memorial, so that I may clearly discern what is far and hidden, as if I had gone in person.
translations.idiomatic: Return and submit a full report, that I may see clearly into the distant and obscure, as though I had traveled there myself.

sentences.zh: 大夫君子，其各悉乃心，各敬乃事，嘉謀令圖，苦言至戒，與使者盡之，無所隱諱。

translations.literal: Great officers and gentlemen, each give your full heart, each attend to your duties; good counsel and sound plans, bitter words and stern warnings—lay them all before the envoys without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and gentlemen of rank: give your whole hearts, do your tasks with care; offer good counsel, sound designs, and frank admonition to the envoys—hide nothing.

sentences.zh: 方將虛心以俟。

translations.literal: I shall wait with an open mind.
translations.idiomatic: I shall await your words with an open mind.

sentences.zh: 其勉哉勗之，稱朕意焉。」

translations.literal: Strive and take heart, that you may accord with my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Take heart and press on, that you may answer to my wish."

sentences.zh: 摯虞新禮議曰：「魏氏無巡狩故事，新禮則巡狩方岳，柴望告至，設壝宮，如禮諸侯之覲者。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu's discussion of the new rites says: "The house of Wei had no precedent for the inspection tour; the new rites provide for touring the sacred mountains of the regions, offering firewood and gazing toward the distance to announce arrival, and setting up an encircled palace, as in the rite for feudal lords coming to audience."
translations.idiomatic: In his discussion of the new rites, Zhi Yu wrote: "Wei had no precedent for imperial tours; the new code provides for touring the sacred peaks, offering firewood and gazing afar to announce arrival, and erecting a palisaded lodge, as when feudal lords come to audience."

sentences.zh: 擯及執贄皆如朝儀，而不建其旗。

translations.literal: The ushering aside and the bearing of gifts were all as in court ceremony, but they did not raise their banners.
translations.idiomatic: The ushering and presentation of gifts followed court ritual, but no banners were raised.

sentences.zh: 臣虞案覲禮，諸侯覲天子，各建其旗章，所以殊爵命，示等威。

translations.literal: Your subject Yu, examining the audience rite, finds that when feudal lords came to audience with the Son of Heaven, each raised his banner and insignia, thereby to distinguish rank and command and display graded majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I, Yu, have examined the audience rite: when feudal lords attended the Son of Heaven, each raised his own banner and insignia to mark rank and show graded dignity.

sentences.zh: 詩稱『君子至止，言觀其旂』。

translations.literal: The Odes say, "When the gentleman arrived, we looked upon his banners."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "When the gentleman arrived, we looked upon his banners."

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮建旗如舊禮。

translations.literal: The new rites should be fixed so that banners are raised as in the old rite.
translations.idiomatic: The new rites ought to be fixed so that banners are raised as in the old practice.

sentences.zh: 」然終晉世，巡狩廢矣。

translations.literal: "Yet through the whole Jin age, the inspection tour was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet through the entire Jin period, the inspection tour fell into disuse.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝永初元年，詔遣大使分行四方，舉善旌賢，問其疾苦。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchu of Emperor Wu of Song, an edict dispatched grand envoys to travel the four directions, to promote the good and honor the worthy, and to inquire into their hardships.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongchu, Emperor Wu of Song ordered grand envoys to travel the four quarters, commend the worthy, and ask after the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 元嘉四年二月乙卯，太祖東巡。

translations.literal: On the yimao day of the second month of the fourth year of Yuanjia, the Founder made an eastern tour.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao of the second month in the fourth year of Yuanjia, the Founder toured east.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，至丹徒。

translations.literal: On the dingmao day he reached Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao he reached Dantu.

sentences.zh: 己巳，告覲園陵。

translations.literal: On the jisi day he announced his visit at the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi he announced his visit at the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 三月甲戌，幸丹徒離宮，升京城北顧。

translations.literal: On jiaxu of the third month he visited the detached palace at Dantu and ascended to look north from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu of the third month he visited the Dantu detached palace and climbed to gaze north from the capital.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，饗父老舊勳于丹徒行宮，加賜衣裳各有差。

translations.literal: On the yihai day he feasted the elders and old meritorious men at the Dantu traveling palace and added gifts of garments, each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai he feasted the elders and veterans of merit at the Dantu traveling palace and granted additional robes, each in due measure.

sentences.zh: 蠲丹徒縣其年租布之半。

translations.literal: He remitted half of that year's grain tax and cloth levy for Dantu county.
translations.idiomatic: He remitted half of Dantu county's grain tax and cloth levy for that year.

sentences.zh: 繫囚見徒五歲刑以下，悉皆原遣。

translations.literal: Prisoners and convicts at hard labor sentenced to five years or less were all pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: All prisoners and convicts at hard labor sentenced to five years or less were pardoned and sent home.

sentences.zh: 登城三戰及先大將家并青泥關頭敗沒餘口，老疾單孤，又諸戰亡家不能自存者，並隨宜隱恤。

translations.literal: Survivors of the three battles at Dengcheng and of the households of former grand generals, together with those lost at Qingni Pass, the aged and ill, the solitary and orphaned, and all households of the war dead unable to support themselves, were all given relief as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors of the three Dengcheng battles, households of former chief generals, and those lost at Qingni Pass; the aged and sick, the alone and orphaned; and families of the war dead who could not support themselves—all received relief as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 二十六年二月己亥，上東巡。

translations.literal: On the jihai day of the second month of the twenty-sixth year, the emperor made an eastern tour.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai of the second month in the twenty-sixth year, the emperor toured east.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，幸京城。

translations.literal: On the xinchou day he visited the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou he visited the capital.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，謁二陵。

translations.literal: On the xinhai day he paid his respects at the two tombs.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai he paid his respects at the two tombs.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，會舊京故老萬餘人，往還饗勞，孤疾勤勞之家，咸蒙卹賚，發赦令，蠲徭役。

translations.literal: On the dingsi day he assembled more than ten thousand old residents of the former capital; coming and going they were feasted and rewarded, and households of the solitary, ill, and diligent poor all received relief; an amnesty was issued and corvée labor remitted.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi he gathered more than ten thousand elders of the old capital; they were feasted and rewarded on their coming and going; households of the alone, the sick, and the dutiful poor all received relief; an amnesty was proclaimed and corvée remitted.

sentences.zh: 其時皇太子監國，有司奏儀注。

translations.literal: At that time the crown prince was regent in the capital, and the relevant offices submitted the ritual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the crown prince governed in the capital, and the relevant offices submitted the ritual forms.

sentences.zh: 某曹關某事云云。

translations.literal: Such-and-such bureau forwards such-and-such matter, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: The [X] Bureau forwards the matter of [Y], and so forth.

sentences.zh: 被令，儀宜如是。

translations.literal: Having received the order, the ritual should be as follows.
translations.idiomatic: By order, the ceremony should proceed as follows.

sentences.zh: 請為牋如左。

translations.literal: Please draft a memorial as at left.
translations.idiomatic: Please draft a memorial in the form at left.

sentences.zh: 謹關。

translations.literal: Respectfully submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully submitted.

sentences.zh: :右署眾官如常儀。

translations.literal: At right: the various offices listed as in the usual form.
translations.idiomatic: At right: the various offices, as in the usual form.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射、尚書左右丞某甲，死罪死罪。

translations.literal: The Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and the Left and Right Assistants of the Masters of Writing, So-and-so—capital offense, capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and the Left and Right Assistants, So-and-so—[we deserve] death, death.

sentences.zh: 某事云云。

translations.literal: Such-and-such matter, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: The matter of [X], and so forth.

sentences.zh: 參議以為宜如是事諾。

translations.literal: Upon deliberation it is held that it should be as follows; approved.
translations.idiomatic: After deliberation, it is held that it should be as follows; approved.

sentences.zh: 奉行。

translations.literal: Carry out.
translations.idiomatic: Carry out.

translations.literal: Such-and-such year, month, and day.
translations.idiomatic: Year, month, and day.

translations.literal: Submitted by such-and-such bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Submitted by the [X] Bureau.

translations.literal: At right: the memorial form follows the memorial on the right for year and month; it is forwarded to the Gatehouse Office and the offices of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At right: the memorial form follows the opening memorial at the right for date; it is forwarded to the Gatehouse Office and the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 其言選事者，依舊不經它官。

translations.literal: Matters concerning selection of personnel, as before, do not pass through other offices.
translations.idiomatic: Matters of appointment, as before, do not pass through other offices.

sentences.zh: 太常主者寺押。

translations.literal: The chief clerk of the Ministry of Rites affixes the seal of the directorate.
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk of the Ministry of Rites affixes the directorate seal.

translations.literal: The director of such-and-such office, So-and-so, submits a petition.
translations.idiomatic: The director of the [X] Office, So-and-so, submits a petition.

sentences.zh: 言某事云云。

translations.literal: Stating such-and-such matter, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: Stating the matter of [X], and so forth.

sentences.zh: 求告報如所稱。

translations.literal: Requesting notification and reply as stated.
translations.idiomatic: Requesting notification and reply as stated.

sentences.zh: 詳檢相應。

translations.literal: Upon detailed examination it corresponds.
translations.idiomatic: Upon detailed examination it corresponds.

sentences.zh: 今聽如所上處事諾。

translations.literal: Now approved to handle the matter as submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Now approved to handle the matter as submitted.

sentences.zh: 明詳旨申勒，依承不得有虧。

translations.literal: Clearly explain the intent and issue strict orders; carry out in compliance without shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly explain the intent and issue strict orders; carry out in full compliance.

sentences.zh: 符到奉行。

translations.literal: When the warrant arrives, carry out.
translations.idiomatic: When the warrant arrives, carry out.

sentences.zh: 年月日。

translations.literal: Year, month, and day.
translations.idiomatic: Year, month, and day.

translations.idiomatic: Issued from the [X] Bureau of the Masters of Writing.

translations.idiomatic: At right: the warrant form.

translations.idiomatic: The [X] Bureau forwards the petition of the chief clerks of the Ministry of Rites, So-and-so and So-and-so.

translations.idiomatic: Seal affixed.

translations.idiomatic: The director of the [X] Office, So-and-so, submits a report.

translations.literal: Such-and-such matter, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: The matter of [X], and so forth.

translations.literal: Requesting that the central office give notification and reply as stated.
translations.idiomatic: Requesting that the central office give notification and reply as stated.

translations.literal: The responsible official, upon detailed examination, finds it corresponds.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible official, upon detailed examination, finds it corresponds.

sentences.zh: 請聽如所上事諾。

translations.literal: Request approval to handle the matter as submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Request approval to handle the matter as submitted.

translations.literal: Issue a separate warrant for enforcement and carrying out.
translations.idiomatic: Issue a separate warrant for enforcement and carrying out.

translations.literal: Respectfully submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully submitted.

translations.idiomatic: Year, month, and day.

translations.literal: At right: the forwarding form follows the yellow dossier for year, month, and day on the right; it is forwarded to the Gatehouse Office with year and month below on the left, and the various offices of the Masters of Writing are listed below.
translations.idiomatic: At right: the forwarding form follows the yellow dossier date at the right; it is forwarded to the Gatehouse Office with date below at the left, and the various Masters of Writing offices are listed below.

translations.literal: Where under the Masters of Writing it should say "memorial," it now says "forward."
translations.idiomatic: Where the Masters of Writing should say "memorial," it now says "forward."

translations.idiomatic: All the rest follow the yellow dossier form.

translations.idiomatic: The [X] Bureau forwards the opening petition of the chief clerk of the Ministry of Revenue, Wang So-and-so.

translations.idiomatic: Seal affixed.

translations.idiomatic: The inspector of [X] Province, Bing and Ding, forwards the memorial of the magistrate of [Y] County, Li Yi, stating the matter of [Z], and so forth.

translations.idiomatic: Wanqiu, though saying the headcloth should remain as before, did not clarify the absence of text on reading the earth-season ordinance.

sentences.zh: 今書舊事于左。

translations.literal: We now set down the old precedents at left.
translations.idiomatic: We now set down the old precedents at left.

sentences.zh: 魏臺雜訪曰：『前後但見讀春夏秋冬四時令，至於服黃之時，獨闕不讀。

translations.literal: The Wei Court Miscellaneous Inquiry says: 'Previously one only saw the reading of the spring, summer, autumn, and winter ordinances of the four seasons; when it was time to wear yellow, alone it was omitted and not read.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Court Miscellaneous Inquiry says: 'Previously one only saw the reading of the spring, summer, autumn, and winter ordinances of the four seasons; when it was time to wear yellow, alone it was omitted and not read.

sentences.zh: 今不解其故。

translations.literal: Now we do not understand the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Now we do not understand the reason.

sentences.zh: 』魏明帝景初元年十二月二十一日，散騎常侍領太史令高堂隆上言曰：『黃於五行，中央土也。

translations.literal: ' On the twenty-first day of the twelfth month of the first year of Jingchu of Emperor Ming of Wei, Concurrent Gentleman of the Palace Library and Director of the Grand Astrologer's Office Gao Tanglong memorialized, saying: 'Yellow in the Five Phases is central earth.
translations.idiomatic: ' On the twenty-first day of the twelfth month of the first year of Jingchu of Emperor Ming of Wei, Concurrent Gentleman of the Palace Library and Director of the Grand Astrologer's Office Gao Tanglong memorialized, saying: 'Yellow in the Five Phases is central earth.

sentences.zh: 王四季各十八日。

translations.literal: The king has eighteen days in each of the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The king has eighteen days in each of the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 土生於火，故於火用事之末服黃，三季則否。

translations.literal: Earth is born from fire; therefore at the end of fire's dominance one wears yellow; in the other three seasons, no.
translations.idiomatic: Earth is born from fire; therefore at the end of fire's dominance one wears yellow; in the other three seasons, no.

sentences.zh: 其令則隨四時，不以五行為分也。

translations.literal: The ordinances follow the four seasons and are not divided by the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: The ordinances follow the four seasons and are not divided by the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 是以服黃無令。

translations.literal: Therefore when wearing yellow there is no ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when wearing yellow there is no ordinance.

sentences.zh: 』」其後太祖常謂土令，三公郎每讀時令，皇帝臨軒，百僚備位，多震悚失常儀。

translations.literal: '" Thereafter the founding emperor commonly called it the earth-season ordinance; whenever the Three Excellencies Bureau attendant read the seasonal ordinances, the emperor faced the hall, and the hundred officials took their places—many were shaken and lost the proper ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the founding emperor habitually called it the earth-season ordinance. When the Three Excellencies Bureau attendant read the seasonal ordinances, the emperor sat upon the throne while the hundred officials took their stations—and many, shaken, botched the ritual.

sentences.zh: 宋唯世祖世劉勰、太宗世謝緯為三公郎，善於其事，人主及公卿並屬目稱歎。

translations.literal: In Song only Liu Xie in the reign of Emperor Shizu and Xie Wei in the reign of Emperor Taizong served as Three Excellencies Bureau attendants and excelled at the task; ruler and high ministers alike turned their eyes to them in praise.
translations.idiomatic: In Song only Liu Xie in the reign of Emperor Shizu and Xie Wei in the reign of Emperor Taizong served as Three Excellencies Bureau attendants and excelled at the task; ruler and high ministers alike turned their eyes to them in praise.

sentences.zh: 勰見宗室傳。

translations.literal: Liu Xie is treated in the biography of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xie is treated in the biography of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 緯，謝綜弟也。

translations.literal: Xie Wei was the younger brother of Xie Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Wei was the younger brother of Xie Zong.

sentences.zh: 舊說後漢有郭虞者，有三女。

translations.literal: Old tradition says that in Later Han there was a Guo Yu who had three daughters.
translations.idiomatic: Old tradition says that in Later Han there was a Guo Yu who had three daughters.

sentences.zh: 以三月上辰產二女，上巳產一女。

translations.literal: On the upper chen day of the third month he bore two daughters; on the shangsi day he bore one daughter.
translations.idiomatic: On the upper chen day of the third month he bore two daughters; on the shangsi day he bore one daughter.

sentences.zh: 二日之中，而三女並亡。

translations.literal: Within those two days all three daughters died.
translations.idiomatic: Within those two days all three daughters died.

sentences.zh: 俗以為大忌。

translations.literal: The common people took this as a great taboo.
translations.idiomatic: The common people took this as a great taboo.

sentences.zh: 至此月此日，不敢止家，皆於東流水上為祈禳，自潔濯，謂之禊祠。

translations.literal: When this month and this day arrived, none dared stay home; all went to flowing water in the east for prayer and purification, bathing themselves clean—this is called the Xi rite.
translations.idiomatic: On that day in that month, people did not dare remain at home. They all went to the eastern flowing waters to pray and purify themselves in washing—the ceremony known as the Xi rite.

sentences.zh: 分流行觴，遂成曲水。

translations.literal: They sent cups downstream in turn, and thus the winding stream [custom] arose.
translations.idiomatic: Wine cups were floated downstream one by one, and so the winding-stream rite took shape.

sentences.zh: 史臣案周禮女巫掌歲時祓除釁浴，如今三月上巳如水上之類也。

translations.literal: The historiographer remarks: In the Rites of Zhou the female shaman was in charge of seasonal exorcism and sin-bathing—like the present third-month shangsi on the waters.
translations.idiomatic: The historian notes that in the Rites of Zhou shamanesses oversaw seasonal purification and ritual bathing—of the same kind as today's third-month shangsi observances on the water.

sentences.zh: 釁浴謂以香薰草藥沐浴也。

translations.literal: Sin-bathing means bathing with fragrant herbs and medicinals.
translations.idiomatic: "Sin-bathing" denotes bathing with aromatic herbs and fumigated medicinals.

sentences.zh: 韓詩曰：「鄭國之俗，三月上巳，之溱、洧兩水之上，招魂續魄。

translations.literal: The Han Poetry says: "In the customs of the state of Zheng, on the third-month shangsi, [they go] to the banks of the Zhen and Wei rivers to summon the soul and renew the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Poetry says: "In Zheng country custom, on the third-month shangsi they go to the Zhen and Wei rivers to call back the soul and restore the spirit.

sentences.zh: 秉蘭草，拂不祥。

translations.literal: They take orchid-grass and brush away ill fortune."
translations.idiomatic: They take orchids in hand and brush away misfortune."

sentences.zh: 」此則其來甚久，非起郭虞之遺風、今世之度水也。

translations.literal: This custom has a very long origin; it did not arise from the legacy of Guo Yu or from today's crossing-water [practice].
translations.idiomatic: The rite is very old indeed; it did not begin with the tale of Guo Yu or with the present-day custom of crossing the water.

sentences.zh: 月令，暮春，天子始乘舟。

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances [say]: In late spring, the Son of Heaven first takes to boats.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances record that in late spring the Son of Heaven first boards his boat.

sentences.zh: 蔡邕章句曰：「陽氣和暖，鮪魚時至，將取以薦寢廟，故因是乘舟禊於名川也。

translations.literal: Cai Yong's commentary says: "When yang qi is mild and warm, sturgeon arrive in season; [the king] is about to take them to offer at the ancestral temple, and therefore takes this occasion to board boats and perform the Xi [rite] on famous rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong's commentary explains: "When the yang breath turns mild, sturgeon come in season; the king is to take them for offering at the temple of rest, and so he boards his boat and performs the Xi purification on a renowned river.

sentences.zh: 論語，暮春浴乎沂。

translations.literal: The Analects [say]: "In late spring, [to] bathe at the Yi [stream]."
translations.idiomatic: The Analects say: "In late spring, bathe at the Yi."

sentences.zh: 自上及下，古有此禮。

translations.literal: From high to low, antiquity had this rite.
translations.idiomatic: From the throne to the common people, antiquity knew this rite.

sentences.zh: 今三月上巳，祓於水濱，蓋出此也。

translations.literal: Today's third-month shangsi purification at the water's edge probably derives from this."
translations.idiomatic: Today's third-month shangsi purification beside the water surely grows from this."

sentences.zh: 」邕之言然。

translations.literal: Cai Yong's statement is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong was right.

sentences.zh: 張衡南都賦祓於陽濱又是也。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng's Rhapsody on the Southern Capital, "purified at the sunny shore," is another instance of this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng's Rhapsody on the Southern Capital—"purified on the sunny bank"—is another example.

sentences.zh: 或用秋，漢書八月祓於霸上。

translations.literal: Or it was performed in autumn; the Book of Han [records] purification at Bashang in the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes it was held in autumn; the Book of Han records an eighth-month purification at Bashang.

sentences.zh: 劉楨魯都賦：「素秋二七，天漢指隅，人胥祓除，國子水嬉。

translations.literal: Liu Zhen's Rhapsody on the Lu Capital: "In the white autumn, on the double seventh, as the Heavenly River points to the corner, all people perform exorcism and the princes' sons sport in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen's Rhapsody on the Lu Capital reads: "In pale autumn, on the double seventh, as the Milky Way turns toward the corner, all perform purification while the crown princes disport in the water.

sentences.zh: 」又是用七月十四日也。

translations.literal: This again was using the fourteenth day of the seventh month.
translations.idiomatic: That again meant the fourteenth day of the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 自魏以後但用三日，不以巳也。

translations.literal: From Wei onward only the third day was used, not the si day.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei onward only the third [of the third month] was observed, not the si day of shangsi.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝天淵池南，設流杯石溝，燕羣臣。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei south of the Heavenly Pool set up a stone channel for floating cups and feasted the assembled ministers.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Heavenly Pool, Emperor Ming of Wei had a stone channel cut for floating cups and entertained his ministers there.

sentences.zh: 晉海西鍾山後流杯曲水，延百僚，皆其事也。

translations.literal: Jin Emperor Haixi [had] winding water with floating cups behind Zhongshan, extending invitation to the hundred officers—all are instances of the same practice.
translations.idiomatic: Behind Zhongshan, Jin Emperor Haixi held a winding stream with floating cups and summoned the hundred officials—these are all of the same kind.

sentences.zh: 官人循之至今。

translations.literal: Officials have followed this down to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Court officers have kept the practice down to our own day.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝始革三年喪制。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han first reformed the three-year mourning system.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han was the first to reform the three-year mourning code.

sentences.zh: 臨終詔曰：「天下吏民臨三日，皆釋服。

translations.literal: His deathbed edict said: "Throughout the realm, officials and commoners who come to mourn for three days shall all lay aside mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he decreed: "Throughout the realm, any official or commoner who comes to mourn for three days shall lay aside mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 無禁取婦、嫁女、祠祀、飲酒、食肉。

translations.literal: None are forbidden to take wives, marry daughters, sacrifice, drink wine, or eat meat.
translations.idiomatic: No one is forbidden to marry, give daughters in marriage, sacrifice, drink wine, or eat meat.

sentences.zh: 其當給喪事者，無跣。

translations.literal: Those who should supply funeral affairs need not go barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: Those who must attend to funeral duties need not go barefoot.

sentences.zh: 絰帶無過三寸。

translations.literal: The hemp sash shall not exceed three inches.
translations.idiomatic: The mourning sash shall be no more than three inches wide.

sentences.zh: 當臨者，皆旦夕各十五舉音。

translations.literal: Those who come to mourn shall each raise lament fifteen times morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Those who come to mourn shall raise lament fifteen times each at dawn and dusk.

sentences.zh: 服大紅十五日，小紅十四日，纖七日而釋服。

translations.literal: They shall wear great red for fifteen days, lesser red for fourteen days, and fine [mourning] for seven days before laying aside mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: They shall wear deep red for fifteen days, lighter red for fourteen days, and fine mourning for seven days, then lay mourning aside.

sentences.zh: 」文帝以己亥崩，乙巳葬，其間凡七日。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen died on the jihai day and was buried on the yisi day; the interval was seven days in all.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen died on the day jihai and was buried on yisi—seven days in all.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，天下遵令，無復三年之禮。

translations.literal: From this time forward the realm obeyed the order, and there was no more three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After that the realm followed his order, and the three-year rite was no more.

sentences.zh: 案尸子，禹治水，為喪法，曰毀必杖，哀必三年。

translations.literal: Examining the Shizi: Yu in controlling the waters established mourning law, saying that when the dwelling is destroyed one must lean on a staff, and in mourning one must observe three years.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizi records that when Yu was controlling the floods he set down mourning law: if a dwelling was ruined one must lean on a staff, and mourning must last three years.

sentences.zh: 是則水不救也。

translations.literal: Thus the floods would not be remedied.
translations.idiomatic: Only then would the waters go untended.

sentences.zh: 故使死於陵者葬於陵，死於澤者葬於澤。

translations.literal: Therefore he had those who died on the hills buried on the hills, and those who died in the marshes buried in the marshes.
translations.idiomatic: So he had the dead on the hills buried on the hills, and the dead in the marshes buried in the marshes.

sentences.zh: 桐棺三寸，制喪三日。

translations.literal: Paulownia coffins three inches [thick], limiting mourning to three days.
translations.idiomatic: Paulownia coffins three inches thick, mourning limited to three days.

sentences.zh: 然則聖人之於急病，必為權制也。

translations.literal: Thus in urgent crisis the sage necessarily establishes provisional measures.
translations.idiomatic: When crisis presses, the sage must set provisional measures.

sentences.zh: 但漢文治致升平，四海寧晏，廢禮開薄，非也。

translations.literal: But Emperor Wen's rule reached ascendancy and peace, the four seas were tranquil—yet he discarded ritual and opened the way to meagerness, which was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperor Wen's reign had already reached peace and the four seas were calm; to cast off ritual and thin custom was wrong.

sentences.zh: 宣帝地節四年，詔曰：「今百姓或遭衰絰凶災，而吏徭事不得葬，傷孝子心。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dijie of Emperor Xuan, an edict said: "Now among the common people some meet with funeral mourning or calamity, yet officials on corvée service cannot bury [their dead], hurting the hearts of filial sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dijie, Emperor Xuan decreed: "Among the people today some suffer bereavement or disaster, yet officials on corvée duty cannot bury their dead—this wounds the hearts of filial sons.

sentences.zh: 自今諸有大父母、父母喪者，勿徭事，使得收斂送終，盡其子道。

translations.literal: From now on all who have mourning for great-grandparents or parents shall not be put on corvée service, so they may gather the remains and escort the dead to the end, fulfilling the way of sons.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, whoever mourns great-grandparents or parents shall not be sent on corvée, so they may lay out the dead and see them to the grave and fulfill a son's duty.

sentences.zh: 」至成帝時，丞相翟方進事父母孝謹，母終，既葬，三十六日，除服視事。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Cheng, Chancellor Zhai Fangjin served his parents with filial care; when his mother ended [her life], after burial, on the thirty-sixth day he removed mourning and took up office.
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Cheng's day, Chancellor Zhai Fangjin had served his parents with scrupulous filial piety; when his mother died and was buried, on the thirty-sixth day he laid mourning aside and returned to office.

sentences.zh: 自以為身備漢相，不敢踰國家典章。

translations.literal: He considered himself as holding the post of Han chancellor and did not dare exceed the state's statutes.
translations.idiomatic: He held himself to be Han's chancellor and did not dare overstep the state's code.

sentences.zh: 然而原涉行父喪三年，顯名天下。

translations.literal: Yet Yuan She observed three years for his father's mourning and his name shone throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yuan She kept three years for his father's death and his name rang through the realm.

sentences.zh: 河間惠王行母喪三年，詔書褒稱，以為宗室儀表。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hejian performed three years for his mother's mourning; an edict praised him, taking him as a model for the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Hejian observed three years for his mother; an imperial edict praised him as a model for the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 薛脩服母喪三年，而兄宣曰：「人少能行之。

translations.literal: Xue Xiu wore mourning for his mother three years, but his elder brother Xuan said: "Few men can do this.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xiu wore mourning for his mother three years, but his elder brother Xuan said: "Few can do as much.

sentences.zh: 」遂兄弟不同，宣卒以此獲譏於世。

translations.literal: Thus the brothers differed, and Xuan in the end for this was censured by the age.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers took different paths, and Xuan was censured by the world for it in the end.

sentences.zh: 是則喪禮見貴常存矣。

translations.literal: Thus mourning rites were held in esteem and constantly endured.
translations.idiomatic: So mourning rites were still held dear and never quite died out.

sentences.zh: 至漢平帝崩，王莽欲眩惑天下示忠孝，使六百石以上皆服喪三年。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ping of Han died, Wang Mang wished to dazzle and beguile the realm to show filial piety, making all of rank six hundred bushels and above observe three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ping died, Wang Mang wished to bedazzle the realm with a show of filial piety and ordered all officials of six hundred bushels and above to observe three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 及莽母死，但服天子弔諸侯之服，一弔再會而已。

translations.literal: When Mang's mother died, he wore only the garb with which the Son of Heaven condoles with feudal lords—one condolence visit and a second assembly, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: When Mang's own mother died, he wore only the garb the Son of Heaven uses to condole with feudal lords—one visit of mourning and a second gathering, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 而令子新都侯宇服喪三年。

translations.literal: Yet he ordered his son Xindu Marquis Yu to observe three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he made his son, Marquis Yu of Xindu, observe three years of mourning.

sentences.zh: 及元后崩，莽乃自服三年之禮。

translations.literal: When Grand Empress Dowager Wang died, Mang himself donned three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Empress Dowager Wang died, Mang himself put on three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 事皆姦妄，天下疾之。

translations.literal: All these matters were deceitful and false; the realm resented them.
translations.idiomatic: Every such act was hollow fraud, and the realm despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 漢安帝初，長吏多避事棄官。

translations.literal: Early in Emperor An of Han, chief officials often avoided duties and abandoned their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor An's reign, senior officials often shirked duty and quit their posts.

sentences.zh: 乃令自非父母服，不得去職。

translations.literal: An order was issued that except for mourning for parents, one might not leave office.
translations.idiomatic: An order went out that except for mourning one's parents, no one might leave office.

sentences.zh: 是後吏又守職居官，不行三年喪服。

translations.literal: After this officials again held their posts and did not observe three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After that officials again stayed in post and did not keep three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 其後又開長吏以下告寧，言事者或以為刺史二千石宜同此制，帝從之。

translations.literal: Later they again opened [the practice of] lower chief officials and below petitioning for leave of absence; memorialists held that inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officials should follow the same regulation, and the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: Later leave was again granted to junior chief officials and below; memorialists urged that inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officers follow the same rule, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 建光元年，尚書孟布奏宜復如建武、永平故事，絕刺史二千石告寧及父母喪服，又從之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianguang, Director of the Secretariat Meng Bu memorialized that they should return to the precedent of Jianwu and Yongping, cutting off petitioning for leave by inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officers and mourning for parents; again [the emperor] assented.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianguang, Secretariat Director Meng Bu urged a return to the Jianwu and Yongping precedent, ending leave petitions and parental mourning for inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officers—and again the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 至桓帝永興二年，復令刺史二千石行三年服。

translations.literal: By the second year of Yongxing of Emperor Huan, they again ordered inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officers to observe three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxing under Emperor Huan, inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officers were again ordered to observe three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 永壽二年，又使中常侍以下行三年服。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongshou, they again made palace attendants and below observe three-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongshou, palace attendants and those below them were again made to observe three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 至延熹元年，又皆絕之。

translations.literal: By the first year of Yanxi, all was cut off again.
translations.idiomatic: By the first year of Yanxi, all of this was abolished again.

sentences.zh: 後漢世，諸帝不豫，並告泰山、弘農、廬江、常山、潁川、南陽、河東、東郡、廣陵太守禱祠五岳四瀆，遣司徒分詣郊廟社稷。

translations.literal: In the Later Han age, when any emperor fell ill, they all notified the governors of Taishan, Hongnong, Lujiang, Changshan, Yingchuan, Nanyang, Hedong, Dongjun, and Guangling to pray and sacrifice at the Five Sacred Peaks and Four Rivers, and sent the Minister over the Masses to go separately to the suburban altars, ancestral temples, and altar of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han, whenever an emperor fell ill, notice went to the governors of Taishan, Hongnong, Lujiang, Changshan, Yingchuan, Nanyang, Hedong, Dongjun, and Guangling to pray at the Five Peaks and Four Rivers, while the Minister over the Masses was sent in turn to the suburban altars, the ancestral temples, and the altar of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 魏武臨終遺令曰：「天下尚未安定，未得遵古。

translations.literal: Cao Cao's deathbed testament said: "The realm is not yet settled; we cannot yet follow antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's deathbed command read: "The realm is not yet at peace; we cannot yet follow the ancients.

sentences.zh: 百官臨殿中者，十五舉音。

translations.literal: Officials who mourn in the palace hall shall raise lament fifteen times.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who mourn in the palace hall shall raise lament fifteen times each.

sentences.zh: 葬畢便除服。

translations.literal: When burial is complete, mourning dress is at once laid aside.
translations.idiomatic: When burial is finished, mourning dress is laid aside at once.

sentences.zh: 其將兵屯戍者，不得離部。

translations.literal: Those who command troops on garrison duty shall not leave their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders of troops on garrison duty shall not leave their posts.

sentences.zh: 」帝以正月庚子崩，辛丑即殯。

translations.literal: The emperor died on the gengzi day of the first month; on xinchou he was immediately encoffined.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died on gengzi of the first month; on xinchou he was encoffined at once.

sentences.zh: 是月丁卯葬，葬畢反吉，是為不踰月也。

translations.literal: On the dingmao day of that month he was buried; when burial was complete they returned to auspicious [dress]—thus not exceeding one month.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao of that month he was buried; when burial was done they returned to normal dress—mourning did not exceed one month.

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮受劉備遺詔，既崩，羣臣發喪，滿三日除服，到葬復如禮。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang received Liu Bei's deathbed command; when [Liu Bei] died, the ministers proclaimed mourning, laid aside mourning after the full three days, and at burial again followed the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang received Liu Bei's deathbed command; when Liu Bei died the ministers raised mourning, laid mourning aside after three full days, and at burial observed the rites again.

sentences.zh: 其郡國太守、相、尉、縣令長三日便除服。

translations.literal: The governors, chancellors, commandants, and magistrates of commanderies and kingdoms laid aside mourning after three days.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery and kingdom governors, chancellors, commandants, and county magistrates laid mourning aside after three days.

sentences.zh: 此則魏、蜀喪制，又並異於漢也。

translations.literal: Thus the mourning systems of Wei and Shu were both again different from Han.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Wei and Shu mourning customs both diverged again from Han.

sentences.zh: 孫權令諸居任遭三年之喪，皆須交代乃去，然多犯者。

translations.literal: Sun Quan ordered that all in active posts who met with three-year mourning must hand over affairs before departing—yet many violated this.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan ordered that anyone in office who faced three-year mourning must hand duties to a successor before leaving—yet many broke the rule.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾六年，使羣臣議立制，胡綜以為宜定大辟之科。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiahe he had the ministers deliberate on establishing regulations; Hu Zong held that there should be fixed the statute of death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiahe he had his ministers debate a standing regulation; Hu Zong argued that the death penalty should be fixed for violators.

sentences.zh: 又使代未至，不得告，告者抵罪。

translations.literal: He also ordered that if the replacement had not arrived, one might not petition for leave; those who petitioned were guilty of a punishable offense.
translations.idiomatic: He also ruled that if one's replacement had not arrived, one might not ask leave; whoever asked leave would be punished.

sentences.zh: 顧雍等同綜議。

translations.literal: Gu Yong and others agreed with Zong's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yong and others agreed with Zong.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [Sun Quan] followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed their advice.

sentences.zh: 其後吳令孟仁聞喪輙去，陸遜陳其素行，得減死一等，自此遂絕。

translations.literal: Thereafter Wu magistrate Meng Ren, upon hearing of a death, would immediately depart; Lu Xun stated his usual conduct, and [Ren] had his death sentence reduced by one degree—from this the [strict enforcement] ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wu magistrate Meng Ren, on hearing of a bereavement, would leave at once; Lu Xun spoke of his usual conduct, and Ren's death sentence was reduced one degree—after that the strict rule lapsed.

sentences.zh: 晉宣帝崩，文、景並從權制。

translations.literal: When the Jin founding emperor [Sima Yi] died, [Sima] Zhao and [Sima] Shi both followed provisional measures.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin's founding emperor Sima Yi died, Sima Zhao and Sima Shi both followed expedient mourning.

sentences.zh: 及文帝崩，國內行服三日。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen [Sima Zhao] died, within the state mourning was observed for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen Sima Zhao died, the realm observed mourning for three days.

sentences.zh: 武帝亦遵漢、魏之典，既葬除喪，然猶深衣素冠，降席撤膳。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu also followed Han and Wei precedents, laying aside mourning once burial was done, yet he still wore deep garments and a plain cap, lowered his mat and withdrew fine food.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu likewise followed Han and Wei precedent, laying mourning aside after burial, yet he still wore plain cap and deep garments, lowered his mat, and withdrew rich fare.

sentences.zh: 太宰司馬孚、太傅鄭沖、太保王祥、太尉何曾、司徒領中領軍司馬望、司空荀顗、車騎將軍賈充、尚書令裴秀、尚書僕射武陔、都護大將軍郭建、侍中郭綏、中書監荀勗、中軍將軍羊祜等奏曰：「臣聞禮典軌度，豐殺隨時，虞、夏、商、周，咸不相襲，蓋有由也。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Sima Fu, Grand Tutor Zheng Chong, Grand Guardian Wang Xiang, Grand Commandant He Cao, Minister over the Masses and Central Army Commander Sima Wang, Minister of Works Xun Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong, Director of the Secretariat Pei Xiu, Vice Director of the Secretariat Wu Wei, Grand Protector General Guo Jian, Attendant within Guo Sui, Director of the Central Secretariat Xun Xu, General of the Central Army Yang Hu, and others memorialized: "We your ministers have heard that ritual canons and measures, full or reduced, follow the season; Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou none simply succeeded one another—there were reasons for this.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Sima Fu, Grand Tutor Zheng Chong, Grand Guardian Wang Xiang, Grand Commandant He Cao, Minister over the Masses and Central Army Commander Sima Wang, Minister of Works Xun Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong, Director of the Secretariat Pei Xiu, Vice Director Wu Wei, Grand Protector General Guo Jian, Attendant within Guo Sui, Central Secretariat Director Xun Xu, Central Army General Yang Hu, and others submitted: "We have heard that ritual norms wax and wane with the times; Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou did not merely copy one another—and for good reason.

sentences.zh: 大晉紹承漢、魏，有革有因，期於足以興化致治而已。

translations.literal: Great Jin succeeded Han and Wei, with reforms and with continuities, aiming only at what suffices to promote transformation and achieve good government.
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin succeeded Han and Wei, reforming here and keeping there, seeking only what would raise the age and bring order.

sentences.zh: 故未皆得返情太素，同規上古也。

translations.literal: Therefore they could not all return feeling to the utmost simplicity and take the ancients of high antiquity as their single standard.
translations.idiomatic: So not everyone could return to utmost plainness and measure all things by high antiquity alone.

sentences.zh: 陛下既已俯遵漢、魏降喪之典，以濟時務；

translations.literal: Your Majesty has already humbly followed the Han and Wei lowered-mourning canon to meet the needs of the times;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has already bowed to Han and Wei's abridged mourning code to meet the needs of the age;

sentences.zh: 而躬蹈大孝，情過乎哀，素冠深衣，降席撤膳。

translations.literal: yet you personally tread the path of great filial piety, feeling beyond proper mourning—plain cap and deep garments, lowered mat and withdrawn fare.
translations.idiomatic: yet you yourself walk the way of great filial piety, grief beyond measure—plain cap and deep robes, a lowered mat, fare withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 雖武丁行之於殷世，曾閔履之於布衣，未足以喻。

translations.literal: Though King Wuding practiced it in the Yin age and Zeng Min carried it as a commoner, that is not enough as a comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Though King Wuding did this in the Yin age and Zengzi and Minzi as commoners, even they are not fit comparison.

sentences.zh: 方今荊蠻未夷，庶政未乂，萬機事殷，動勞神慮。

translations.literal: At present the Jing barbarians are not pacified, the myriad affairs of government are not ordered, the ten thousand concerns are pressing, and toil vexes the mind and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Jing tribes are not pacified, government is not set right, ten thousand matters press in, and labor wears upon your spirit.

sentences.zh: 豈遑全遂聖旨，以從至情。

translations.literal: How can there be leisure to fulfill fully the sage's intent and follow utmost feeling?
translations.idiomatic: How can there be room to fulfill the sage's aim in full and indulge utmost feeling?

sentences.zh: 加歲時變易，期運忽過，山陵彌遠，攀慕永絕。

translations.literal: Moreover the seasons change; the allotted span suddenly passes; the mountain tomb grows ever farther, and clinging admiration is cut off forever.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the seasons turn, the allotted span slips away, the hill tomb recedes, and longing is cut off forever.

sentences.zh: 臣等以為陛下宜回慮割情，以康時濟治。

translations.literal: We your ministers hold that Your Majesty should turn your thoughts and sever excessive feeling, to bring ease to the age and aid governance.
translations.idiomatic: We hold that Your Majesty should turn your mind and restrain feeling, to bring peace to the age and aid good government.

sentences.zh: 輒敕御府易服，內省改坐，太官復膳。

translations.literal: We therefore order the imperial wardrobe to change garments, the inner quarters to change seating, and the grand steward to restore fare.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore order the imperial wardrobe to change your dress, the inner quarters to change your seat, and the grand steward to restore your meals.

sentences.zh: 諸所施行，皆如舊制。

translations.literal: All measures taken shall be as the former regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Everything done shall follow the old statutes.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「每感念幽冥，而不得終苴絰於草土，以存此痛，況當食稻衣錦，誠佹然激切其心，非所以相解也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Whenever I reflect on the shades below, unable to complete the hemp mourning at the grave among grass and soil, keeping this pain—how much less when I ought to eat rice and wear brocade! Truly it abruptly stirs and cuts my heart; this is not a way to comfort me.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Whenever I think of the dead below, unable to finish hemp mourning at the grave in grass and soil, and keep this pain—how much more when I must eat grain and wear brocade! It suddenly cuts my heart; this is no comfort.

sentences.zh: 吾本諸生家，傳禮來久，何心一旦便易此情於所天。

translations.literal: I come originally from a scholar's family; ritual has been handed down a long time—what heart could suddenly alter this feeling toward him who was as heaven?
translations.idiomatic: I come from a scholar's house; ritual has been handed down long—what heart could suddenly change this feeling for him who was my heaven?

sentences.zh: 相從已多，可試省孔子答宰我之言，無事紛紜也。

translations.literal: You have remonstrated at length already; you might try reviewing what Confucius replied to Zai Wo, and need not make such turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: You have remonstrated enough; read again what Confucius answered Zai Wo, and do not stir up such clamor.

sentences.zh: 言及悲剝，奈何奈何！

translations.literal: When I speak of this grief and pain—alas, alas!
translations.idiomatic: To speak of this grief that cuts—alas, alas!

sentences.zh: 」孚等重奏：「伏讀明詔，感以悲懷。

translations.literal: Fu and the others memorialized again: "We humbly read the clear edict and are moved to mournful feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and the others submitted again: "We have read your clear edict and are moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 輙思仲尼所以抑宰我之問，聖思所以不能已已，甚深甚篤。

translations.literal: We reflect on why Zhongni restrained Zai Wo's question—the sage's thought of why he could not cease, cease—how deep, how earnest.
translations.idiomatic: We think on why Zhongni checked Zai Wo's question—on why the sage could not stop, could not stop—how deep, how earnest.

sentences.zh: 然今者干戈未戢，武事未偃，萬機至重，天下至眾。

translations.literal: Yet now arms are not laid down, military affairs are not stilled, the myriad concerns are paramount, and the realm is vast in population.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now arms are not laid aside, war is not stilled, affairs of state weigh most heavily, and the realm is vast.

sentences.zh: 陛下以萬乘之尊，履布衣之禮，服粗席藁，水飲疏食，殷憂內盈，毀悴外表，而躬勤萬機，坐而待旦，降心接下，仄不遑食，所以勞力者如斯之甚。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, in the dignity of the ten-thousand-chariot throne, yet treads the garb of a commoner—coarse mat and straw, water to drink and plain food, sorrow heaped within, wasting shown without—and still personally attends the ten thousand concerns, sits awaiting dawn, lowers your heart to receive those below, scarcely finding time to eat: the labor you take upon yourself is extreme indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, though lord of ten thousand chariots, yet keeps a commoner's mourning—coarse mat and straw bedding, water and plain food, grief within, emaciation without—and still personally tends ten thousand affairs, sits awaiting dawn, bends to those below, scarcely finding time to eat: never was labor borne so hard.

sentences.zh: 是以臣等悚息不寧，誠懼神氣用損，以疚大事。

translations.literal: Therefore we your ministers are fearful and uneasy, truly dreading that spirit and vital breath will be damaged, to the injury of great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore we are fearful and uneasy, truly afraid your spirit will be harmed and great affairs suffer for it.

sentences.zh: 輒敕有司改坐復常，率由舊典。

translations.literal: We therefore order the relevant offices to change seating back to normal, all following the old canon.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore order the offices concerned to restore your seat to normal, all according to the old code.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下察納愚款，以慰皇太后之心。

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty examine and accept our foolish sincerity, to comfort the empress dowager's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Only may Your Majesty weigh and accept our humble plea, to ease the empress dowager's heart.

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「重覽奏議，益以悲剝，不能自勝，奈何奈何！

translations.literal: Again an edict said: "Having again perused your memorial, I am all the more cut by grief; I cannot master myself—alas, alas!
translations.idiomatic: Again an edict said: "Having read your memorial again, I am all the more cut by grief; I cannot bear it—alas, alas!

sentences.zh: 三年之喪，自古達禮，誠聖人稱心立哀，明恕而行也。

translations.literal: The three-year mourning is the universal rite from antiquity; truly the sage sets forth grief according to the heart, and acts with enlightened forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: The three-year mourning has been the universal rite since antiquity—the sage gives grief its full voice in the heart and acts with enlightened forbearance.

sentences.zh: 神靈日遠，無所告訴。

translations.literal: The spirit day by day grows distant; there is none to whom to tell it.
translations.idiomatic: The departed spirit grows more distant each day, and there is no one left to whom I can speak.

sentences.zh: 雖薄於情，食旨服美，朕更所不堪也。

translations.literal: Though slight in feeling, to eat delicacies and wear finery—We are even less able to bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Even if my grief were shallow, I could not bear to eat fine food or wear beautiful robes.

sentences.zh: 不宜反覆，重傷其心，言用斷絕，奈何奈何！

translations.literal: It is not fitting to go back and forth, again wounding their hearts; let the discussion end here—what is to be done, what is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: Do not press the matter again and wound their hearts further; let this discussion end—what can I do, what can I do!

sentences.zh: 」帝遂以此禮終三年。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon observed this rite to the end of three years.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then carried that mourning through the full three years.

sentences.zh: 後居太后之喪，亦如之。

translations.literal: Later, when he observed mourning for the Empress Dowager, he did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he mourned the empress dowager, he did the same.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年八月，詔書曰：「此上旬，先帝棄天下日也。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Taishi, an edict said: "In the first ten days of this month is the day when the late emperor left the world.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Taishi 2, an edict declared: "The first ten days of this month mark the day the late emperor departed this life.

sentences.zh: 便以周年。

translations.literal: The full year has now arrived.
translations.idiomatic: A full year has now passed.

sentences.zh: 吾㷀㷀，當復何時壹得叙人子情邪？

translations.literal: I am forlorn and alone—when shall I ever once be able to give voice to a son's feelings?
translations.idiomatic: I stand bereft and alone—when will I ever be able to express a son's grief as I should?

sentences.zh: 思慕煩毒，欲詣陵瞻侍，以盡哀憤。

translations.literal: Longing and grief are tormenting; I wish to go to the tomb to look upon and attend it, to exhaust my grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Grief and longing torment me; I wish to visit the imperial tomb to look upon it and pay my respects, and pour out all my sorrow and anguish.

sentences.zh: 主者具行備。

translations.literal: The responsible officials shall fully prepare for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible officials make full preparations for the journey.

sentences.zh: 」太宰司馬孚、尚書令裴秀、尚書僕射武陔等奏：「陛下至孝蒸蒸，哀思罔極，衰麻雖除，毀顇過禮，疏食粗服，有損神和。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Sima Fu, Director of the Department of State Affairs Pei Xiu, Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Wu Gai, and others memorialized: "Your Majesty's utmost filial piety is fervent, your grieving thoughts without limit; though the hemp garments have been removed, your emaciation from grief exceeds the rites, and plain food and coarse dress are injurious to your vital harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Sima Fu, Director of the Department of State Affairs Pei Xiu, Vice Director Wu Gai, and others submitted: "Your Majesty's filial devotion burns bright and your grief knows no bound; though you have laid aside the hemp mourning dress, your wasting grief goes beyond what ritual allows, and plain food and coarse clothing are harming your health.

sentences.zh: 今雖秋節，尚有餘暑，謁見山陵，悲感摧傷，羣下竊用悚息。

translations.literal: Though it is now autumn, there is still lingering heat; to visit and look upon the mountain tomb will grievously wound you with sorrow, and your subjects venture to tremble with apprehension.
translations.idiomatic: Although autumn has come, the heat has not yet broken; a visit to the mountain tomb will only shatter you with sorrow, and we your subjects tremble at the thought.

sentences.zh: 平議以為宜惟遠體，降抑聖情，以慰萬國。

translations.literal: Those who deliberated and judged deemed it fitting that Your Majesty should only consider the distant welfare of the realm, restrain and lower your sacred feelings, to comfort the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: Those who weighed the matter judged that Your Majesty should look to the distant good of the realm, restrain your royal grief, and so bring comfort to all under heaven.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「孤煢忽爾，日月已周，痛慕摧感，永無逮及。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Orphaned and alone, suddenly thus—the days and months have completed a cycle; pain and longing crush me, and forever there is no reaching back.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Left orphaned and alone in this sudden loss—a full year has passed; grief crushes me, and there is no going back.

sentences.zh: 欲奉瞻山陵，以敍哀僨。

translations.literal: I wish to go and look upon the mountain tomb, to give voice to my grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to go to the tomb to look upon it and give full voice to my grief and anguish.

sentences.zh: 體氣自佳，其又已涼，便當行，不得如所奏也。

translations.literal: My bodily constitution is naturally good, and moreover it has already turned cool; I shall go at once and cannot act as your memorial advises.
translations.idiomatic: My health is sound, and the weather has already turned cool; I shall go at once and cannot do as you urge.

sentences.zh: 主者便具行備。

translations.literal: The responsible officials shall at once fully prepare for the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible officials prepare for the journey at once.

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「昔者哀適三十日，便為梓宮所棄，遂離衰絰，感痛豈可勝言。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "In former days, when grief had barely reached thirty days, I was abandoned to the coffin in the palace, and so parted from the hemp mourning bands; the pain—how can it be told?
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said: "In the past, grief had scarcely reached thirty days when I was left to the palace coffin and stripped of my hemp mourning bands; the pain is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 顧漢文不使天下盡哀，亦先帝至謙之志，是以自割，不以副諸君子。

translations.literal: Reflecting on how Emperor Wen of Han did not let the realm mourn fully, that too was the late emperor's utmost modest intent; therefore I cut myself off and did not follow the gentlemen in this.
translations.idiomatic: I recall that Emperor Wen of Han would not let the realm mourn fully—that too was the late emperor's deepest humility; so I restrained myself and did not do as you gentlemen urged.

sentences.zh: 有三年之愛，而身禮廓然，當見山陵，何心而無服，其以衰絰行。

translations.literal: There is a three-year love, yet the bodily rites stand empty; when I am to see the mountain tomb, how can my heart be without dress? Let me go in hemp mourning bands.
translations.idiomatic: I bear a three years' love, yet outwardly I stand almost without ritual; when I go to the tomb, how can my heart go unclothed in mourning? I shall wear the hemp bands.

sentences.zh: 」孚等重奏：「臣聞上古喪期無數，後世乃有年月之漸。

translations.literal: Fu and the others again memorialized: "Your subjects have heard that in high antiquity the mourning period had no fixed number; only in later ages did there gradually come to be years and months.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and the others memorialized again: "We have heard that in high antiquity mourning had no fixed term; only later did years and months gradually appear.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝隨時之義，制為短喪，傳之于後。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han, in the meaning of adapting to the times, established short mourning and transmitted it to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han, adapting to the needs of his age, instituted short mourning and bequeathed it to later generations.

sentences.zh: 陛下以社稷宗廟之重，萬方億兆之故，既從權制，釋降衰麻。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, for the weight of the altars of state and the ancestral temple, and for the sake of the myriad regions and the hundred million people, has already followed the expedient regulation and laid aside the hemp mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, for the sake of the altars of state and the myriad people, has already followed expedient rule and laid aside the hemp mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 羣臣庶僚吉服。

translations.literal: The host of ministers and the various officials wear auspicious dress.
translations.idiomatic: The host of ministers and officials already wear auspicious dress.

sentences.zh: 今者謁陵，以敍哀慕，若加衰絰，近臣期服，當復受制。

translations.literal: Now, in visiting the tomb to give voice to grief and longing, if hemp mourning is added, the close attendants in one-year mourning dress would again be bound by regulation.
translations.idiomatic: If you now visit the tomb in grief and again don hemp mourning, your close attendants in one-year mourning would once more be bound by regulation.

sentences.zh: 進退無當，不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: Advance and retreat would have no proper place; we dare not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Advance and retreat would have no proper rule; we dare not obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「亦知不在此麻布耳。

translations.literal: An edict said: "I also know it does not lie in this hemp cloth.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "I know as well that the matter does not lie in this hemp cloth alone.

sentences.zh: 然人子情思，為欲令哀喪之物在身，蓋近情也。

translations.literal: Yet a son's feelings wish to have the objects of grief and mourning on the body—this is, broadly, to be close to feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a son's heart wants the outward tokens of mourning on his body—that is simply to stay close to feeling.

sentences.zh: 羣臣自當案舊制。

translations.literal: The host of ministers should themselves follow the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen should yourselves follow the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 期服之義，非先帝意也。

translations.literal: The meaning of one-year mourning dress for attendants is not the late emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The rule of one-year mourning for attendants is not what the late emperor intended.

sentences.zh: 」孚等又奏：「臣聞聖人制作，必從時宜。

translations.literal: Fu and the others again memorialized: "Your subjects have heard that when the sage establishes institutions, he must follow what suits the time.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and the others memorialized again: "We have heard that when the sage makes institutions, he must follow what suits the time.

sentences.zh: 故五帝殊樂，三王異禮。

translations.literal: Therefore the Five Emperors had different music, and the Three Kings had different rites.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Five Emperors had different music, and the Three Kings had different rites.

sentences.zh: 此古今所以不同，質文所以迭用也。

translations.literal: This is why ancient and modern differ, and substance and ornament alternate in use.
translations.idiomatic: That is why antiquity and the present differ, and plainness and ornament take turns.

sentences.zh: 陛下隨時之宜，既降心克己，俯就權制，既除衰麻，而行心喪之禮。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, in what suited the time, has already lowered your heart, restrained yourself, and bowed to the expedient regulation; having removed the hemp mourning dress, you practice the rite of mourning in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, adapting to the times, has already humbled your heart, restrained yourself, and accepted expedient rule; having laid aside hemp mourning, you keep mourning in the heart.

sentences.zh: 今復制服，義無所依。

translations.literal: Now to don mourning dress again has no ground in ritual meaning.
translations.idiomatic: To don mourning dress again has no ground in ritual.

sentences.zh: 若君服而臣不服，雖先帝厚恩，亦未之敢安也。

translations.literal: If the ruler wears mourning but the ministers do not, though the late emperor's generous grace is great, we still would not dare feel at ease.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler wears mourning while his ministers do not, however great the late emperor's grace, we would not dare feel at ease.

sentences.zh: 參量平議，宜如前奏。

translations.literal: Weighing and deliberating, it should be as in the former memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing the matter, we should hold to our former memorial.

sentences.zh: 臣等敢固以請。

translations.literal: Your subjects venture to press this request firmly.
translations.idiomatic: We venture to press this request firmly.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「患情不能企及耳，衣服何在。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The trouble is that feeling cannot reach that far—what of clothes?
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "The trouble is that feeling cannot reach so far—what matter are clothes?

sentences.zh: 諸君勤勤之至，豈苟相違。」

translations.literal: You gentlemen have been diligent to the utmost—how could I casually go against you?"
translations.idiomatic: You have been so earnest—how could I lightly go against you?"

sentences.zh: 泰始四年，皇太后崩。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi, the Empress Dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi 4, the empress dowager died.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「前代故事，倚廬中施白縑帳蓐，素牀，以布巾裹凷草。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized: "In precedents of former ages, in the mourning hut white silk curtains and mats were spread, plain beds, and bolsters of coarse grass wrapped in cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials submitted: "By precedents of earlier ages, the mourning hut was furnished with white silk curtains and mats, plain beds, and bolsters of coarse grass wrapped in cloth.

sentences.zh: 軺輦板輿細犢車皆施縑裏。

translations.literal: Light carriages, plank litters, and small ox-carts were all lined with silk.
translations.idiomatic: Light carriages, plank litters, and small ox-carts were all lined with silk.

sentences.zh: 」詔不聽，但令以布衣車而已。

translations.literal: An edict did not accept this, but ordered only plain-cloth carriages.
translations.idiomatic: The edict refused this and ordered only plain-cloth carriages.

sentences.zh: 其餘居喪之制，一如禮文。

translations.literal: The rest of the regulations for dwelling in mourning followed the ritual texts.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of the regulations for dwelling in mourning followed the ritual texts.

sentences.zh: 有司又奏：「大行皇太后當以四月二十五日安厝。

translations.literal: The responsible officials again memorialized: "The late empress dowager should be laid to rest on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials submitted again: "The late empress dowager should be laid to rest on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 故事，虞著衰服，既虞而除。

translations.literal: By precedent, at the yu sacrifice one wears hemp mourning dress, and after the yu one removes it.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, at the yu sacrifice one wears hemp mourning dress and removes it after the yu.

sentences.zh: 其內外官僚，皆就朝晡臨位。

translations.literal: The inner and outer officials all take their places at morning and evening audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer officials all take their places at the morning and evening audiences.

sentences.zh: 御除服訖，各還所次除衰服。

translations.literal: When the sovereign has finished removing mourning dress, each returns to his post and removes the hemp mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign has finished removing mourning dress, each returns to his post and removes the hemp mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「夫三年之喪，天下之達禮也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The three-year mourning is the universal rite of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The three-year mourning is the universal rite of the realm.

sentences.zh: 受終身之愛，而無數年之報，奈何葬而便即吉，情所不忍也。

translations.literal: To receive a lifetime's love and have no years of requital—how can one, at burial, at once turn to auspicious dress? The feeling cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: To receive a lifetime's love and repay it with no years of mourning—how can one turn to auspicious dress as soon as burial is over? The heart cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 」有司又奏：「世有險易，道有洿隆，所遇之時異，誠有由然，非忽禮也。

translations.literal: The responsible officials again memorialized: "The age has its perils and eases, the Way has its low and high points; the times one meets are different—truly there is reason for it; it is not a sudden neglect of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials submitted again: "The age has its dangers and its ease, the Way its low points and its high; the times differ, and there is good reason for it—this is not a sudden neglect of ritual.

sentences.zh: 方今戎馬未散，王事至殷，更須聽斷，以熙庶績。

translations.literal: At present war-horses are not yet dispersed, and the king's affairs are at their most pressing; judgment must still be heard to brighten the myriad achievements.
translations.idiomatic: War-horses are not yet stilled, and the king's business presses most heavily; judgment must still be heard so that the myriad tasks may prosper.

sentences.zh: 昔周康王始登翌室，猶戴冕臨朝。

translations.literal: In former times King Kang of Zhou, when he first ascended the mourning hall, still wore the coronet and held court.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity King Kang of Zhou, when he first entered the mourning hall, still wore his coronet and held court.

sentences.zh: 降於漢、魏，既葬除釋，諒闇之禮，自遠代而廢矣。

translations.literal: Descending to Han and Wei, after burial the mourning was released; the rite of seclusion in grief has been abandoned since distant ages.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Wei downward, mourning was released after burial; the rite of seclusion in grief has been abandoned since distant ages.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下割高宗之制，從當時之宜。

translations.literal: Only Your Majesty should cut off the regulation of Gaozong and follow what suits the present time.
translations.idiomatic: Only Your Majesty should set aside Gaozong's regulation and follow what suits the present time.

sentences.zh: 敢固以請。

translations.literal: We venture to press this request firmly.
translations.idiomatic: We venture to press this request firmly.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「攬省奏事，益增感剝。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Gathering up and reviewing your memorials, my grief is only increased and torn open.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Reading your memorials over again only tears my grief open further.

sentences.zh: 夫三年之喪，所以盡情致禮。

translations.literal: The three-year mourning is what fully exhausts feeling and completes ritual.
