translations.idiomatic: The three-year mourning is what fully exhausts feeling and completes ritual.

sentences.zh: 葬已便除，所不堪也。

translations.literal: To remove it as soon as burial is done—this I cannot bear.
translations.idiomatic: To lay it aside as soon as burial is done—I cannot bear that.

sentences.zh: 當敍吾哀懷，言用斷絕，奈何奈何！

translations.literal: I shall give voice to my grief; let the discussion end here—what is to be done, what is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: I shall give voice to my grief; let this discussion end—what can I do, what can I do!

sentences.zh: 」有司又固請。

translations.literal: The responsible officials again pressed the request firmly.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials pressed their request again.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「不能篤孝，勿以毀傷為憂也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "If I cannot practice deep filial piety, do not worry on account of harm from grief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "If I cannot practice deep filial piety, do not worry that grief will harm me.

sentences.zh: 誠知衣服末事耳。

translations.literal: I truly know that clothes are the least of matters.
translations.idiomatic: I truly know that clothes are the least of matters.

sentences.zh: 然今思存草土，率常以吉物奪之，乃所以重傷至心，非見念也。

translations.literal: Yet now, thinking to keep to the grave-mound earth, I am constantly stripped of it by auspicious objects; this is what deeply wounds the utmost heart—it is not regard for me.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now, when I wish to keep to the grave-mound earth, I am constantly stripped of it by auspicious things; that is what wounds my heart most deeply—it is not regard for me.

sentences.zh: 每代禮典質文皆不同，此身何為限以近制，使達喪闕然乎。

translations.literal: In every age the ritual canon differs in substance and ornament—why should this person be bound by recent regulations, leaving the universal mourning incomplete?
translations.idiomatic: In every age ritual differs in substance and ornament—why should I be bound by recent regulations and leave the universal mourning incomplete?

sentences.zh: 」羣臣又固請，帝流涕久之乃許。

translations.literal: The host of ministers again pressed firmly; the emperor wept for a long time and then consented.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers pressed again; the emperor wept a long while and then consented.

sentences.zh: 文帝崇陽陵先開一日，遣侍臣侍梓宮，又遣將軍校尉當直尉中監各一人，將殿中將軍以下及先帝時左右常給使詣陵宿衞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen opened Chongyang Tomb one day early, he sent attendant ministers to attend the coffin, and also sent one general, colonel, duty officer, and palace inspector each, leading the palace guards from commandant of the palace guard downward and those who had regularly served the late emperor to camp and guard at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen opened Chongyang Tomb one day early, he sent attendant ministers to attend the coffin and dispatched one general, colonel, duty officer, and palace inspector each, with the palace guards from the commandant of the palace guard downward and those who had regularly served the late emperor, to camp and guard at the tomb.

sentences.zh: 文明皇后崩及武元楊后崩，天下將吏發哀三日止。

translations.literal: When Empress Wenming died and when Empress Wu-Yuan Yang died, generals and officials throughout the realm mourned for three days and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wenming died and when Empress Wu-Yuan Yang died, generals and officials throughout the realm mourned for three days and then stopped.

sentences.zh: 泰始元年，詔諸將吏二千石以下遭三年喪，聽歸終寧，庶人復除徭役。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taishi, an edict said: "All generals and officials from two-thousand-dan rank downward who encounter three-year mourning are permitted to return home to complete their mourning; commoners are exempted from corvée and levies."
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi 1, an edict declared: "All generals and officials of two-thousand-dan rank and below who face three-year mourning may return home to complete it; commoners are exempted from corvée and levies."

sentences.zh: 太康七年，大鴻臚鄭默母喪，既葬，當依舊攝職，固陳不起。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taikang, Grand Herald Zheng Mo's mother died; after burial he was to resume his former duties by precedent, but he firmly declared he would not rise to office.
translations.idiomatic: In Taikang 7, Grand Herald Zheng Mo's mother died; after burial he was to resume office by precedent, but he firmly refused to return.

sentences.zh: 於是始制大臣得終喪三年。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was first decreed that great ministers might complete mourning for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon it was first decreed that great ministers might complete the full three years of mourning.

sentences.zh: 然元康中，陳準、傅咸之徒，猶以權奪，不得終禮。

translations.literal: Yet in the Yuankang era, Chen Zhun, Fu Xian, and the like were still deprived by expedient rule and could not complete the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the Yuankang era, Chen Zhun, Fu Xian, and others were still cut short by expedient rule and could not complete the rites.

sentences.zh: 自茲至今，往往以為成比也。

translations.literal: From then until now, this has often been taken as an established parallel.
translations.idiomatic: From then until now, this has often been treated as established precedent.

sentences.zh: 晉文帝之崩也，羊祜謂傅玄曰：「三年之喪，自天子達。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Jin died, Yang Hu said to Fu Xuan: "The three-year mourning extends from the Son of Heaven down.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Jin died, Yang Hu said to Fu Xuan: "The three-year mourning extends from the Son of Heaven down.

sentences.zh: 漢文除之，毀禮傷義。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han abolished it—destroying ritual and injuring righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han abolished it—destroying ritual and injuring righteousness.

sentences.zh: 今上有曾、閔之性，實行喪禮。

translations.literal: Now the ruler above has the nature of Zeng Shen and Min Sun and truly practices mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: Now our ruler has the nature of Zeng Shen and Min Sun and truly practices mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 喪禮實行，何為除服？

translations.literal: If mourning rites are truly practiced, why remove the dress?
translations.idiomatic: If mourning rites are truly practiced, why remove the mourning dress?

sentences.zh: 若因此守先王之法，不亦善乎？

translations.literal: If by this one guards the law of the former kings, is it not good?"
translations.idiomatic: If by this we uphold the law of the former kings, would that not be good?"

sentences.zh: 」玄曰：「漢文以末世淺薄，不能復行國君之喪，故因而除之。

translations.literal: Xuan said: "Emperor Wen of Han, because the late age was shallow and thin, could not again practice the ruler's mourning, and therefore abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan said: "Emperor Wen of Han, because the age was shallow and corrupt, could not again practice a ruler's mourning, and therefore abolished it.

sentences.zh: 數百年一旦復古，恐難行也。

translations.literal: To restore antiquity after several hundred years—I fear it would be hard to carry out.
translations.idiomatic: To restore antiquity after several hundred years—I fear it would be hard to carry out.

sentences.zh: 」祜曰：「且使主上遂服，猶為善乎？

translations.literal: Hu said: "Yet if the sovereign completes the mourning dress, is it still good?"
translations.idiomatic: Hu said: "Yet if the sovereign completes the mourning dress, would that still be good?"

sentences.zh: 」玄曰：「若上不除而臣下除，此為但有父子，無復君臣，三綱之道虧矣。

translations.literal: Xuan said: "If the ruler above does not remove mourning but the ministers below remove it, this means there are only father and son and no longer ruler and minister—the way of the three bonds is impaired."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan said: "If the ruler does not remove mourning but his ministers do, then there are only father and son and no longer ruler and minister—the way of the three bonds is impaired."

sentences.zh: 」習鑿齒曰：「傅玄知無君臣之傷教，而不知兼無父子為重，豈不蔽哉。

translations.literal: Xi Zuochi said: "Fu Xuan knew the injury to teaching of having no ruler and minister, but did not know that to have neither father nor son is the heavier matter—how is he not blind?
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi said: "Fu Xuan saw the harm to teaching when ruler and minister are set aside, but did not see that to set aside father and son is the graver matter—how blind was he?

sentences.zh: 且漢廢君臣之喪，不降父子之服，故四海黎庶，莫不盡情於其親。

translations.literal: Moreover, Han abolished mourning between ruler and minister but did not lower mourning between father and son; therefore the common people of the four seas all exhausted feeling toward their kin.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Han abolished mourning between ruler and minister but did not lower mourning between father and son; therefore the common people throughout the realm all poured out feeling toward their kin.

sentences.zh: 三綱之道，二服恒用於私室，而王者獨盡廢之，豈所以孝治天下乎。

translations.literal: In the way of the three bonds, the two kinds of mourning dress were constantly used in private chambers, yet the king alone wholly abolished them—how is this governing the realm by filial piety?
translations.idiomatic: In the way of the three bonds, both kinds of mourning dress were constantly kept in private life, yet the king alone wholly set them aside—how is that governing the realm through filial piety?

sentences.zh: 詩云『猷之未遠』，其傅玄之謂也。」

translations.literal: The Odes say, 'The plan is not yet far'—is this not said of Fu Xuan?"
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, 'The plan is not yet far'—was that not said of Fu Xuan?"

sentences.zh: 泰始十年，武元楊皇后崩。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taishi, Empress Wu-Yuan Yang died.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi 10, Empress Wu-Yuan Yang died.

sentences.zh: 博士張靖議：「太子宜依漢文權制，割情除服。

translations.literal: Erudite Zhang Jing proposed: "The crown prince should follow Emperor Wen of Han's expedient regulation, cut off feeling, and remove mourning dress."
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Zhang Jing proposed: "The crown prince should follow Emperor Wen of Han's expedient regulation, restrain his grief, and remove mourning dress."

sentences.zh: 」博士陳逵議：「太子宜令服重。

translations.literal: Erudite Chen Kui proposed: "The crown prince should be ordered to wear heavy mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Chen Kui proposed: "The crown prince should be ordered to wear heavy mourning."

sentences.zh: 」尚書僕射盧欽、尚書魏舒、杜預奏：「諒闇之制，乃因自古，是以高宗無服喪之文，唯稱不言而已。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Lu Qin, Director of the Department of State Affairs Wei Shu, and Du Yu memorialized: "The regulation of seclusion in grief follows from antiquity; therefore Gaozong has no text on wearing mourning dress—he is only said not to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Lu Qin, Director Wei Shu, and Du Yu submitted: "The regulation of seclusion in grief comes down from antiquity; Gaozong has no passage on wearing mourning dress—he is only said not to speak.

sentences.zh: 漢文限三十六日，魏氏以既虞為斷。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han limited it to thirty-six days; the Wei house took the completion of the yu sacrifice as the term.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han limited it to thirty-six days; the house of Wei took the completion of the yu sacrifice as the term.

sentences.zh: 皇太子與國為體，理宜釋服。

translations.literal: The crown prince and the state are one body; by principle he should release mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and the state are one body; by principle he should release mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 」博士段暢承述預旨，推引禮傳以成其說。

translations.literal: Erudite Duan Chang, carrying on and setting forth Du Yu's intent, cited and drew upon the ritual texts to complete his argument.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Duan Chang, following Du Yu's intent, cited the ritual texts to complete his argument.

sentences.zh: 既卒哭，太子及三夫人以下皆隨御除服。

translations.literal: After the final wailing was completed, the crown prince and those below the three ladies all followed the sovereign in removing mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: After the final wailing, the crown prince and all below the three ladies followed the sovereign in removing mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 自漢文用權禮，無復□禁，歷代遵用之。

translations.literal: From the time Han Wen employed expedient mourning rites, mourning prohibitions were no longer in force, and successive dynasties followed the practice.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Emperor Wen of Han employed expedient mourning rites, the old mourning restrictions ceased to apply, and successive dynasties followed the practice.

sentences.zh: 至晉孝武崩，太傅錄尚書會稽王道子議：「山陵之後通婚嫁，不得作樂，以一朞為限。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Jin died, Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Department of State Affairs Prince Daozi of Kuaiji proposed: "After the mountain tomb, marriage may be contracted, music may not be performed, with one year as the limit."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Jin died, Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Department of State Affairs Prince Daozi of Kuaiji proposed: "After the mountain tomb, marriage may proceed and music may not be performed, for one year as the limit."

sentences.zh: 」宋高祖崩，葬畢，吏民至于宮掖，悉通樂，唯殿內禁。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Song died, after burial officials and people even to the palace quarters all had music restored; only within the halls was it forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu of Song died, after burial officials and people even within the palace quarters all had music restored; only inside the halls was it forbidden.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝永初元年，黃門侍郎王準之議：「鄭玄喪制二十七月而終，學者多云得禮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchu, Palace Attendant Wang Zhunzhi proposed: "Zheng Xuan's mourning regulation ends at twenty-seven months, and scholars mostly say it accords with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu 1, Palace Attendant Wang Zhunzhi proposed: "Zheng Xuan's mourning regulation ends at twenty-seven months, and scholars mostly say it accords with ritual.

sentences.zh: 晉初用王肅議，祥禫共月，遂以為制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin they adopted Wang Su's proposal, making the xiang and chan in the same month, and thus established it as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was founded, the court followed Wang Su's view and set the xiang and chan in the same month, and that became the standing rule.

sentences.zh: 江左以來，唯晉朝施用；

translations.literal: Since the move south of the Jiang, only the Jin dynasty applied it;
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved south of the Yangzi, only the Jin regime actually enforced it;

sentences.zh: 搢紳之士，猶多遵玄議。

translations.literal: among gentry and officials many still followed Xuan's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: yet many scholar-officials still adhered to Zheng Xuan's position.

sentences.zh: 宜使朝野一體。

translations.literal: It is fitting to make court and countryside one body.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside ought to follow a single standard.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict granted approval.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永康元年，愍懷太子薨，帝依禮服長子三年，羣臣服齊衰朞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongkang of Emperor Hui of Jin, Crown Prince Minhuai died; the Emperor wore three years for an eldest son according to ritual, and the multitude wore one-year qi-sackcloth mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongkang 1 of Emperor Hui of Jin, Crown Prince Minhuai died; the emperor observed the three-year mourning prescribed for an eldest son, and the officials wore one-year qi mourning.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武太元二十一年，孝武帝崩，李太后制三年之制。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Taiyuan of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, Emperor Xiaowu died; Empress Dowager Li adopted the three-year system.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyuan 21 of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, the emperor died, and Empress Dowager Li took up the three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝永初三年，武帝崩，蕭太后制三年之服。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu of Emperor Wu of Song, Emperor Wu died; Empress Dowager Xiao adopted three-year garments.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu 3 of Emperor Wu of Song, the emperor died, and Empress Dowager Xiao wore the three-year mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝太安元年三月，皇太孫尚薨。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Taian of Emperor Hui of Jin, Imperial Great-Grandson Shang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Taian 1 under Emperor Hui of Jin, the imperial great-grandson Shang died.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「御服齊衰朞。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: "The sovereign should wear one-year qi-sackcloth mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices reported: "The sovereign should wear one-year qi mourning.

sentences.zh: 」詔通議。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered broad discussion.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict called for a general debate.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍謝衡以為諸侯之太子，誓與未誓，尊卑體殊，喪服云，為嫡子長殤。

translations.literal: Xie Heng, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, held that for a feudal lord's crown prince, sworn and unsworn differ in the body of honor and baseness; the mourning regulations say that for a legitimate eldest son there is long shang mourning—
translations.idiomatic: Xie Heng, Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, argued that for a feudal lord's heir, sworn and unsworn status differ in rank, and that the mourning code treats a legitimate eldest son who dies young as "long shang"—

sentences.zh: 謂未誓也。

translations.literal: meaning not yet sworn.
translations.idiomatic: meaning one who had not yet taken the adulthood oath.

sentences.zh: 已誓則不殤也。

translations.literal: If already sworn, then it is not shang.
translations.idiomatic: Once the oath had been taken, the case was no longer classified as shang.

sentences.zh: 中書令卞粹曰：「太子始生，故已尊重，不待命誓。

translations.literal: Bian Cui, Director of the Central Secretariat, said: "From birth the crown prince is already honored and need not wait for the oath of adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Cui, Director of the Central Secretariat, said: "The crown prince is honored from birth and need not wait for the coming-of-age ceremony.

sentences.zh: 若衡議已誓不殤，則元服之子，當斬衰三年；

translations.literal: If one follows Heng's view that once sworn there is no shang, then a son who has received the cap should wear severest mourning for three years;
translations.idiomatic: If Heng is right that sworn heirs are not shang cases, then a son who had already capped should receive three years of severest mourning;

sentences.zh: 未誓而殤，則雖十九，當大功九月。

translations.literal: if unsworn and shang, then even at nineteen one should wear major mourning for nine months.
translations.idiomatic: but if he were unsworn and counted as shang, then even at nineteen he would wear only nine months of major mourning.

sentences.zh: 誓與未誓，其為升降也微；

translations.literal: Sworn and unsworn differ only slightly in rise and fall;
translations.idiomatic: The difference between sworn and unsworn is slight in rank;

sentences.zh: 斬與大功，其為輕重也遠。

translations.literal: severest mourning and major mourning differ far in light and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: yet severest mourning and major mourning are worlds apart in weight.

sentences.zh: 而今注云，諸侯不降嫡殤，重嫌於無服，以大功為重嫡之服。

translations.literal: Yet the commentary now says that feudal lords do not lower mourning for a legitimate shang death, being wary of no mourning at all, and take major mourning as the garment for a legitimate heir.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the commentary now says that for a lord's legitimate heir who dies young, mourning is not reduced—for fear of wearing none at all—and major mourning is prescribed.

sentences.zh: 大功為重嫡之服，則雖誓，無復有三年之理明矣。

translations.literal: If major mourning is the garment for a legitimate heir, then even if sworn, clearly there is no further ground for three years.
translations.idiomatic: If major mourning is the garment for a legitimate heir, then even after the adulthood oath there is plainly no room left for three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 男能奉衞社稷，女能奉婦道，各以可成之年，而有已成之事，故可無殤，非孩齓之謂也。

translations.literal: When a male can guard the altars of the state and a female can fulfill the wife's way, each at an age when completion is possible yet already has completed affairs, shang may be omitted—not meaning infants in swaddling clothes.
translations.idiomatic: When a son is old enough to serve the state and a daughter old enough to fulfill a wife's duties, each has already achieved what that age allows; shang may then be set aside—not meaning infants in arms.

sentences.zh: 謂殤後者，尊之如父，猶無所加，而止殤服。

translations.literal: Those called post-shang are honored as a father yet nothing more is added, and mourning stops at shang garments.
translations.idiomatic: Those called "after shang" are honored like a father, yet nothing beyond shang garments is added.

sentences.zh: 況以天子之尊，為無服之殤，行成人之制邪。

translations.literal: How, with the Son of Heaven's honor, for a shang without garments could one enact an adult's regulations?
translations.idiomatic: How could the Son of Heaven, in all his dignity, treat a death without full mourning garments as if it called for an adult's rites?

sentences.zh: 凡諸宜重之殤，皆士大夫不加服，而令至尊獨居其重，未之前聞也。

translations.literal: For all shang deaths that should be heavy, scholar-officials add no garments, yet you would have the supreme one alone bear the weight—never heard of before.
translations.idiomatic: For every shang death that ought to carry heavy mourning, ordinary officials wear nothing extra—yet the throne alone would bear the full weight? There is no precedent for that.

sentences.zh: 」博士蔡克同粹。

translations.literal: " Academician Cai Ke agreed with Cui.
translations.idiomatic: " Academician Cai Ke sided with Bian Cui.

sentences.zh: 祕書監摯虞議：「太子初生，舉以成人之禮，則殤理除矣。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu, Supervisor of the Secretariat, argued: "When the crown prince is born he is raised with adult rites, and the principle of shang is thereby removed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu, Supervisor of the Secretariat, argued: "The crown prince is invested with adult rites at birth, so the category of shang no longer applies.

sentences.zh: 太孫亦體君傳重，由位成而服全，非以年也。

translations.literal: The imperial great-grandson likewise bears the lord's succession; by the completion of his station the mourning is complete—not by age.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial great-grandson likewise carries the weight of succession; mourning is determined by office fulfilled, not by years lived.

sentences.zh: 天子無服殤之儀，絕朞故也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven has no ritual of garments for shang, because the period is cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has no shang-garment ritual, because the mourning period is cut short by rank.

sentences.zh: 」於是御史以上皆服齊衰。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the censor-in-chief and above all wore qi-sackcloth mourning.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the censor-in-chief and all ranks above him wore qi mourning.

sentences.zh: 晉康帝建元元年正月晦，成恭杜皇后周忌。

translations.literal: On the last day of the first month of the first year of Jianyuan of Emperor Kang of Jin, it was the weekly anniversary of the death of Empress Chengong Du.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the first month of Jianyuan 1 under Emperor Kang of Jin came the weekly anniversary of Empress Chengong Du's death.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「至尊朞年應改服。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: "At the one-year mark the supreme one should change garments.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices reported: "At the end of the one-year mourning period the emperor should change out of mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「君親，名教之重也。

translations.literal: " The edict said: "Ruler and parent are the weight of name-teaching.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict said: "Duty to ruler and parent lies at the heart of moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 權制出於近代耳。

translations.literal: Expedient regulations come only from recent times.
translations.idiomatic: Expedient rules are a product of recent ages alone.

sentences.zh: 」於是素服如舊。

translations.literal: " Thereupon plain garments continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore continued in plain dress as before.

sentences.zh: 非漢、魏之典。

translations.literal: This was not the canon of Han and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That was not the Han and Wei precedent.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武太元九年，崇德太后褚氏崩。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taixuan of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, Chongde Empress Dowager Chu died.
translations.idiomatic: In Taixuan 9 of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, Chongde Empress Dowager Chu died.

sentences.zh: 后於帝為從嫂，或疑其服。

translations.literal: The empress to the Emperor was his cousin's wife, and some doubted the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: To the emperor she was his elder cousin's wife, and some questioned what mourning he should wear.

sentences.zh: 太學博士徐藻議：「資父事君而敬同。

translations.literal: Xu Zao, Doctor of the Imperial Academy, argued: "Supporting the father and serving the ruler entail the same reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zao, Doctor of the Imperial Academy, argued: "Honoring one's father and serving one's ruler demand the same reverence.

sentences.zh: 又禮傳，其夫屬乎父道者，妻皆母道也。

translations.literal: The ritual texts also say that when a husband belongs to the father's way, the wife belongs to the mother's way.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual commentaries also say that when a husband stands in the father's relation, his wife stands in the mother's.

sentences.zh: 則夫屬君道，妻亦后道矣。

translations.literal: Then if the husband belongs to the lord's way, the wife also belongs to the empress's way.
translations.idiomatic: If the husband belongs to the lord's relation, the wife belongs to the empress's as well.

sentences.zh: 服后宜以資母之義。

translations.literal: Mourning for an empress should follow the meaning of honoring a foster mother.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning for an empress should follow the principle applied to a foster mother.

sentences.zh: 魯譏逆祀，以明尊尊。

translations.literal: Lu reproached inverted sacrifice to clarify honoring the honorable.
translations.idiomatic: Lu condemned improper sacrifice in order to uphold the hierarchy of honor.

sentences.zh: 今上躬奉康、穆、哀皇及靖后之祀，致敬同於所天。

translations.literal: Now the sovereign personally attends the sacrifices to Emperors Kang, Mu, and Ai and to Empress Jing, showing reverence equal to that owed Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The present emperor personally attends the sacrifices to Emperors Kang, Mu, and Ai and to Empress Jing, showing the same reverence he owes his sovereign lord.

sentences.zh: 豈可敬之以君道，而服廢於本親。

translations.literal: How could he show reverence by the lord's way yet abandon mourning for his own kin?
translations.idiomatic: How could he honor her as a lord yet set aside mourning owed to his own kin?

sentences.zh: 謂應服齊衰朞。

translations.literal: He held that one should wear one-year qi-sackcloth mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He concluded that the emperor should wear one-year qi mourning.

sentences.zh: 」於是帝制朞服。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Emperor adopted one-year mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thereupon adopted the one-year mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 晉安帝隆安四年，太皇太后李氏崩。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Longan of Emperor An of Jin, Grand Empress Dowager Li died.
translations.idiomatic: In Longan 4 of Emperor An of Jin, Grand Empress Dowager Li died.

sentences.zh: 尚書祠部郎徐廣議：「太皇太后名位允正，體同皇極，理制備盡，情禮彌申。

translations.literal: Xu Guang, Director in the Ministry of Rites of the Secretariat, argued: "The grand empress dowager's title and station are fully orthodox, her status equals the imperial pole, reason and regulation are complete, and feeling and ritual are all the more extended.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang of the Secretariat's Ministry of Rites argued: "The grand empress dowager's title and rank are fully legitimate, her status equals the imperial apex, the ritual logic is complete, and the emotional obligation is all the greater.

sentences.zh: 陽秋之義，母以子貴。

translations.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that the mother is ennobled through the son.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn principle is that a mother is honored through her son.

sentences.zh: 既稱夫人，禮服從正。

translations.literal: Once she is styled lady, ritual garments follow the orthodox rule.
translations.idiomatic: Once she bears the title of consort, ritual mourning follows the standard form.

sentences.zh: 故成風顯夫人之號，文公服三年之喪，子於父之所生，體尊義重。

translations.literal: Thus Duke Cheng displayed the title of lady, and Duke Wen wore three years of mourning; a child toward what the father bore is honored in status and heavy in obligation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Duke Cheng gave his mother the title of lady, and Duke Wen wore three years of mourning—a child owes deep obligation to the mother his father honored.

sentences.zh: 且禮祖不厭孫，宜遂服無屈。

translations.literal: Moreover, in ritual the ancestor does not weary of the grandson; mourning should therefore be worn without bending.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, ritual holds that an ancestor does not reject a grandson; mourning should be worn in full, without reduction.

sentences.zh: 而緣情立制，若嫌明文不存，則疑斯從重。

translations.literal: Yet when establishing regulations by feeling, if one doubts because no explicit text survives, then one should suspect and follow the heavier mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When regulation is shaped by affection, and no explicit text survives, the safer course is the heavier mourning.

sentences.zh: 謂應同於為祖母後齊衰朞。

translations.literal: He held that one should follow the same rule as for a paternal grandmother's widow—one-year qi-sackcloth mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He held that the emperor should follow the same rule as for a paternal grandmother who had been widowed—one-year qi mourning.

sentences.zh: 永安皇后無服，但一舉哀。

translations.literal: For the Yong'an empress there were no mourning garments, only a single outpouring of grief.
translations.idiomatic: For the Yong'an empress there was no mourning dress, only a single ritual lament.

sentences.zh: 百官亦一朞。

translations.literal: The hundred officials also mourned one year.
translations.idiomatic: The officials likewise observed one year of mourning.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉十七年七月壬子，元皇后崩。

translations.literal: On the day renzi of the seventh month of the seventeenth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, Empress Yuan died.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day of the seventh month of Yuanjia 17 under Emperor Wen of Song, Empress Yuan died.

sentences.zh: 兼司徒給事中劉溫持節監喪。

translations.literal: Liu Wen, Concurrent Minister of Education and Palace Attendant, held the staff and supervised the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wen, who held concurrent posts as Minister of Education and Palace Attendant, took the imperial staff and oversaw the funeral.

sentences.zh: 神虎門設凶門柏歷至西上閤，皇太子於東宮崇正殿及永福省並設廬。

translations.literal: At the Spirit Tiger Gate a mourning gate and cypress framework were set up to the West Upper Pavilion; at the Eastern Palace's Chongzheng Hall and the Yongfu quarter the crown prince likewise set up mourning huts.
translations.idiomatic: A mourning gate and cypress bier were erected at the Spirit Tiger Gate up to the West Upper Pavilion; the crown prince set mourning huts in the Chongzheng Hall of the Eastern Palace and in the Yongfu quarter.

sentences.zh: 諸皇子未有府第者，於西廨設廬。

translations.literal: Princes who as yet had no mansions set up huts in the west wing.
translations.idiomatic: Princes who had not yet been granted residences set up mourning huts in the west wing.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十七年，元皇后崩。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Yuanjia, Empress Yuan died.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 17, Empress Yuan died.

sentences.zh: 皇太子心喪三年。

translations.literal: The crown prince observed inner mourning for three years.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince observed inner mourning for three years.

sentences.zh: 禮心喪者，有禫無禫，禮無成文，世或兩行。

translations.literal: In ritual, for inner mourning some perform the chan and some do not; the ritual has no fixed text, and generations sometimes practice both ways.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual texts on inner mourning disagree over whether the chan is performed; no fixed rule exists, and different ages have followed different practices.

sentences.zh: 皇太子心喪畢，詔使博議。

translations.literal: When the crown prince's inner mourning was complete, an edict ordered broad discussion.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince's inner mourning ended, an edict called for a broad debate.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「喪禮有禫，以祥變有漸，不宜便除即吉，故其間服以綅縞也。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: "Mourning ritual includes the chan, because the change at xiang should be gradual and one should not immediately remove mourning and return to auspicious dress; therefore during that interval one wears pink and plain hemp.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices reported: "Mourning ritual includes the chan stage, because the transition at xiang should be gradual and one ought not to cast off mourning at once; in that interval one wears pink-trimmed plain hemp.

sentences.zh: 心喪已經十三月，大祥十五月，祥禫變除，禮畢餘一朞，不應復有禫。

translations.literal: Inner mourning has already passed thirteen months, great xiang at fifteen months; with the xiang and chan changes removed, the ritual is complete with one year remaining—there should not again be a chan.
translations.idiomatic: Inner mourning has already run thirteen months, and great xiang at fifteen; once xiang and chan are past, only one year of the rite remains—there should be no further chan.

sentences.zh: 宣下以為永制。

translations.literal: Proclaim this below as a permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Let this be proclaimed as the permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 孝武孝建三年三月，有司奏：「故散騎常侍、右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司義陽王師王偃喪逝。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Xiaojian of Emperor Xiaowu, the relevant offices memorialized: "The late Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, Right Director of the Imperial Household, and Commander Equal to the Three Dukes, Tutor to the Prince of Yiyang, Wang Yan, has died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Xiaojian 3 under Emperor Xiaowu, the responsible offices reported: "Wang Yan, former Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, Right Director of the Imperial Household, Commander Equal to the Three Dukes, and tutor to the Prince of Yiyang, has died.

sentences.zh: 至尊為服緦三月，成服，仍即公除。

translations.literal: The supreme one wore finest hemp for three months, completed the garments, and immediately undertook public removal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore finest-grade hemp mourning for three months, completed the initial mourning garments, and at once undertook public removal.

sentences.zh: 至三月竟，未詳當除服與不？

translations.literal: When the three months were finished, it was unclear whether he should remove the garments or not.
translations.idiomatic: When the three months ended, it was unclear whether he should fully lay the mourning aside.

sentences.zh: 又皇后依朝制服心喪，行喪三十日公除。

translations.literal: Moreover, the empress, following court regulations, observed inner mourning and, after thirty days of mourning, undertook public removal.
translations.idiomatic: The empress, following court regulations, also observed inner mourning and undertook public removal after thirty days.

sentences.zh: 至祖葬日，臨喪當著何服？

translations.literal: On the day of the grandfather's burial, what garments should she wear when attending the mourning?
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the grandfather's burial, what dress should she wear when attending the funeral?

sentences.zh: 又舊事，皇后心喪，服終除之日，更還著未公除時服，然後就除。

translations.literal: According to old practice, when the empress's inner mourning reached the day of final removal, she again put on the garments worn before public removal, and only then completed the removal.
translations.idiomatic: By former practice, when an empress ended inner mourning, on the day of final removal she put on again the dress she had worn before public removal, and only then completed the mourning.

sentences.zh: 未詳今皇后除心制日，當依舊更服？

translations.literal: It is unclear whether today, on the day the empress ends inner mourning, she should follow the old rule and change garments again—
translations.idiomatic: It is unclear whether, on the day the empress ends inner mourning today, she should follow the old custom and don mourning dress again—

sentences.zh: 為但釋心制中所著布素而已？

translations.literal: or only set aside the plain cloth worn during inner mourning?
translations.idiomatic: or simply set aside the plain cloth she wore during inner mourning?

sentences.zh: 勒禮官處正。

translations.literal: Order the ritual officials to decide correctly.
translations.idiomatic: Let the ritual officials determine the correct practice.

sentences.zh: 」太學博士王膺之議：「尊卑殊制，輕重有級，五服雖同，降厭則異。

translations.literal: " Wang Yingzhi, Doctor of the Imperial Academy, argued: "Honor and baseness have different systems; light and heavy have their grades; though the five garments are the same in kind, lowering and reduction differ.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Yingzhi, Doctor of the Imperial Academy, argued: "High and low follow different rules; lighter and heavier mourning have their grades; though the five garments share a common scheme, reduction by rank differs.

sentences.zh: 禮，天子止降旁親，外舅緦麻，本在服例，但衰絰不可以臨朝饗，故有公除之議。

translations.literal: In ritual the Son of Heaven only lowers mourning for collateral kin; a maternal uncle wears finest hemp and is within the garment canon, but hemp bands and headcloth cannot attend court or feasts—hence the proposal of public removal.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual the Son of Heaven reduces mourning only for collateral kin. A maternal uncle wears finest hemp and falls within the mourning canon, but hemp bands cannot be worn at court or at feasts—hence the institution of public removal.

sentences.zh: 雖釋衰襲冕，尚有緦麻之制。

translations.literal: Although one removes the hemp and dons the cap and gown, the rule of finest hemp still remains.
translations.idiomatic: Even after shedding hemp for court dress, the rule of finest-grade mourning still applies in private.

sentences.zh: 愚謂至尊服三月既竟，猶宜除釋。

translations.literal: I hold that once the supreme one's three months are finished, he should still fully remove and release the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that once the emperor's three months are complete, he should fully lay the mourning aside.

sentences.zh: 」又議：「吉凶異容，情禮相稱。

translations.literal: " He argued further: "Auspicious and inauspicious occasions require different appearance; feeling and ritual must match.
translations.idiomatic: " He argued further: "Joyous and mournful occasions require different dress; emotion and ritual must correspond.

sentences.zh: 皇后一月之限雖過，二功之服已釋，哀情所極，莫深於尸柩，親見之重，不可以無服。

translations.literal: Though the empress has passed the one-month limit and released the two-grade mourning garments, nowhere is grief deeper than before the coffin; the weight of seeing the deceased in person cannot be met without garments.
translations.idiomatic: Though the empress has passed the one-month limit and set aside her second-grade mourning dress, grief reaches its depth at the coffin; the obligation of seeing the deceased face to face cannot be met without mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 案周禮，為兄弟既除喪已，及其葬也，反服其服。

translations.literal: According to the Rites of Zhou, for a brother, once mourning has been removed, at the burial one returns to those garments.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou provide that for a brother, once mourning has been removed, one puts the mourning garments back on for the burial.

sentences.zh: 輕喪雖除，猶齊衰以臨葬。

translations.literal: Though light mourning has been removed, one still wears qi-sackcloth to attend the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Even after lighter mourning has been set aside, one still wears qi mourning for the burial.

sentences.zh: 舉輕明重，則其理可知也。

translations.literal: Inferring the heavy from the light, the principle may be known.
translations.idiomatic: If the lighter case requires this, the heavier case follows by analogy.

sentences.zh: 愚謂王右光祿祖葬之日，皇后宜反齊衰。

translations.literal: I hold that on the day of the burial of Wang Guanglu's grandfather, the empress should return to qi-sackcloth mourning.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that on the day of the burial of Wang Yan's grandfather, the empress should return to qi mourning.

sentences.zh: 」又議：「喪禮即遠，變除漸輕，情與日殺，服隨時改。

translations.literal: " He argued further: "As mourning recedes, each change of removal grows lighter; feeling diminishes day by day, and garments change with the time.
translations.idiomatic: " He argued further: "As mourning recedes, each stage of removal grows lighter; grief fades day by day, and dress changes with the calendar.

sentences.zh: 權禮既行，服制已變，豈容終除之日，而更重服乎？

translations.literal: Once expedient ritual has been performed and the garment system changed, how at the day of final removal could one again wear heavy garments?
translations.idiomatic: Once expedient mourning has been observed and the dress code altered, how on the day of final removal could one put on heavy mourning again?

sentences.zh: 案晉泰始三年，武帝以朞除之月，欲反重服拜陵，頻詔勤勤，思申棘心。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi of Jin, Emperor Wu, in the month of one-year removal, wished to return to heavy garments to visit the tomb; repeated edicts urged diligence, seeking to express a thorn-pierced heart.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Taishi 3, Emperor Wu, in the month when one-year mourning was ending, wished to resume heavy dress to visit his father's tomb; edict after edict urged the court on, seeking to express his anguished heart.

sentences.zh: 于時朝議譬執，亦遂不果。

translations.literal: At that time court debate was obstinate, and in the end it did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion was stubbornly divided, and in the end the plan failed.

sentences.zh: 愚謂皇后終除之日，不宜還著重服，直當釋除布素而已。

translations.literal: I hold that on the empress's day of final removal she should not again wear heavy garments, but should simply set aside the plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that on the empress's day of final removal she should not resume heavy mourning, but simply lay aside the plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 」太常丞朱膺之議：「凡云公除，非全除之稱。

translations.literal: " Zhu Yingzhi, Director under the Minister of Ceremonies, argued: "Whenever one speaks of public removal, it is not a term for complete removal.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhu Yingzhi, Director under the Minister of Ceremonies, argued: "Whenever one speaks of gongchu—public removal—it does not mean complete removal.

sentences.zh: 今朝臣私服，亦有公除，猶自窮其本制。

translations.literal: Today when court ministers wear private garments, they too have public removal, yet still exhaust the root regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Today when court ministers observe private mourning, they too undergo public removal, yet still fulfill the full mourning term in private.

sentences.zh: 膺之云，晉武拜陵不遂反服，此時是權制，既除衰麻，不可以重制耳。

translations.literal: Yingzhi said that when Jin Wu visited the tomb he did not succeed in returning to garments—that was an expedient regulation; once hemp had been removed, one could not impose the heavy system again.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yingzhi noted that when Emperor Wu of Jin tried to revisit the tomb in mourning dress he did not succeed—that was an expedient rule; once hemp had been set aside, the heavy mourning could not be imposed again.

sentences.zh: 與公除不同。

translations.literal: That differs from public removal.
translations.idiomatic: That case differs from public removal.

sentences.zh: 愚謂皇后除心制日，宜如舊反服未公除時服，以申創巨之情。

translations.literal: I hold that on the day the empress ends inner mourning she should, as in the old practice, return to the garments worn before public removal, in order to express the wound of a great bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that on the day the empress ends inner mourning she should, following old practice, return to the dress worn before public removal, so as to express the depth of her grief.

sentences.zh: 」餘同膺之議。

translations.literal: " The rest agreed with Yingzhi's discussion.
translations.idiomatic: " On the remaining points the court followed Zhu Yingzhi's view.

sentences.zh: 國子助教蘇瑋生議：「案三日成服即除，及皇后行喪三十日，禮無其文。

translations.literal: National University assistant instructor Su Weisheng submitted a discussion: "According to the case of completing mourning garments in three days and then removing them, and of the empress observing mourning for thirty days, the ritual texts provide no such wording.
translations.idiomatic: Su Weisheng, an assistant instructor at the National University, argued: "The rites nowhere prescribe completing mourning dress in three days and then laying it aside, nor an empress mourning for only thirty days."

sentences.zh: 若並謂之公除，則可粗相依准。

translations.literal: If both are to be called public removal of mourning, then one may roughly take them as parallel standards.
translations.idiomatic: If both are treated as public removal of mourning, they can be aligned only in the roughest sense.

sentences.zh: 凡諸公除之設，蓋以王制奪禮。

translations.literal: As for the institution of all such public removals, it is broadly because royal affairs override the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Every provision for public removal exists because state business overrides normal mourning.

sentences.zh: 葬及祥除，皆宜反服。

translations.literal: At burial and at the removal of mourning at the subduing year, one should alike put mourning garments back on.
translations.idiomatic: At burial and at the subduing-year release from mourning, mourners should again don mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 未有服之於前，不除於後。

translations.literal: There is no precedent for wearing mourning beforehand and not removing it afterward.
translations.idiomatic: One does not wear mourning earlier only to refuse to lay it aside later.

sentences.zh: 雖有齊斬重制，猶為功緦除喪。

translations.literal: Even where there are heavy regulations of qi and zhan mourning, removal of mourning still follows the grades of gong and si.
translations.idiomatic: Even the heaviest qi and zhan mourning is still ended according to the lighter gong and si grades.

sentences.zh: 夫公除暫奪，豈可遂以即吉邪。

translations.literal: Public removal is a temporary dispossession—how can one straightway take up auspicious dress?
translations.idiomatic: Public removal is only a temporary suspension; how can one immediately resume festive dress?

sentences.zh: 愚謂至尊三月服竟，故應依禮除釋。

translations.literal: In my humble view, when the Son of Heaven's three-month mourning is finished, he should accordingly remove and release mourning according to the rites.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that once the emperor's three-month mourning is complete, he should end it in the proper ritual manner.

sentences.zh: 皇后臨祖，及一周祥除，並宜反服齊衰。

translations.literal: When the empress attends the grandfather's burial, and at the removal of mourning at the first year's subduing period, she should alike put back on qi mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress attends her grandfather-in-law's burial, and at the first-year subduing release, she should again wear qi mourning.

sentences.zh: 」尚書令、中軍將軍建平王宏議謂：「至尊緦制終，止舉哀而已。

translations.literal: The Minister Over the Masses, General of the Central Army, Prince of Pingping Hong submitted a discussion saying: "When the Son of Heaven's si mourning is finished, he need only perform the lamentation.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hong of Pingping, Minister Over the Masses and General of the Central Army, argued: "Once the emperor's three-month si mourning ends, he need only offer lamentation."

sentences.zh: 不須釋服。

translations.literal: There is no need to remove mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: He need not lay aside mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 」餘同朱膺之議。

translations.literal: The rest accords with Zhu Yingzhi's discussion.
translations.idiomatic: On all other points he agreed with Zhu Yingzhi.

sentences.zh: 前祠部郎中周景遠議：「權事變禮，五服俱革，緦麻輕制，不容獨異。

translations.literal: Former Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices Zhou Jingyuan submitted a discussion: "When affairs of the time alter the rites, all five grades of mourning are changed together; the light si grade cannot alone be treated differently.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jingyuan, formerly of the Sacrifices Bureau, wrote: "When exigency alters ritual, every grade of mourning changes together; the lightest si grade cannot stand apart."

sentences.zh: 」謂：「至尊既已公除，至三月竟，不復有除釋之義。

translations.literal: He said: "Since the Son of Heaven has already undergone public removal, when the three months are finished there is no longer any meaning of removal and release.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Once the emperor has undergone public removal, the end of three months no longer calls for a further ritual release."

sentences.zh: 」其餘同朱膺之議。

translations.literal: On the rest he agreed with Zhu Yingzhi's discussion.
translations.idiomatic: On the remaining points he followed Zhu Yingzhi.

sentences.zh: 重加研詳，以宏議為允。

translations.literal: After further careful study, Hong's discussion was held acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: After further review, Hong's opinion was accepted.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 大明二年正月，有司奏：「故右光祿大夫王偃喪，依格皇后服朞，心喪三年，應再周來二月晦。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Daming, the relevant offices memorialized: "The former Right Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan has died; according to the regulations the empress wears the one-year mourning grade, with heart-mourning for three years; the second full cycle should end on the last day of the second month to come.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Daming 2, officials reported: "The late Right Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan has died. By regulation the empress wears one-year mourning with three years of heart-mourning; the second full cycle should end on the last day of the coming second month.

sentences.zh: 檢元嘉十九年舊事，武康公主出適，二十五月心制終盡，從禮即吉。

translations.literal: Checking the old precedent of the nineteenth year of Yuanjia, when Princess Wukang married out, her heart-mourning was fully completed in the twenty-fifth month and she followed the rites in immediately taking up auspicious dress.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanjia 19 precedent shows Princess Wukang, after marrying out, completing heart-mourning in the twenty-fifth month and then resuming normal dress as the rites allow.

sentences.zh: 昔國哀再周，孝建二年二月，其月末，諸公主心制終，則應從吉。

translations.literal: Formerly, at the national mourning's second full cycle, in the second month of the second year of Xiaojian, at the end of that month the heart-mourning of all the princesses was finished, and they should accordingly have taken up auspicious dress.
translations.idiomatic: At the second cycle of national mourning, in Xiaojian 2, the princesses' heart-mourning ended at the close of the second month and they should have resumed normal dress.

sentences.zh: 于時猶心禫素衣，二十七月乃除，二事不同。

translations.literal: At that time they still wore plain dress in the final period of heart-mourning; only in the twenty-seventh month was mourning removed—the two cases differ.
translations.idiomatic: On that occasion they still wore plain dress for the final period of heart-mourning and did not leave mourning until the twenty-seventh month—the two cases differ.

sentences.zh: 」領儀曹郎朱膺之議：「詳尋禮文，心喪不應有禫，皇代考檢，已為定制。

translations.literal: Zhu Yingzhi, Director of the Bureau of Ceremonies, submitted a discussion: "On careful examination of the ritual texts, heart-mourning should not have a final chan period; our dynasty has investigated this and already fixed it as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yingzhi of the Ceremonies Bureau argued: "The classics do not prescribe a final mourning period for heart-mourning; the court has long since fixed the rule.

sentences.zh: 元嘉季年，禍難深酷，聖心天至，喪紀過哀。

translations.literal: In the closing years of Yuanjia, calamity was deep and cruel; the sage heart reached heaven's utmost, and the mourning observance exceeded what sorrow required.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Yuanjia years catastrophe was severe; the emperor's grief was boundless and mourning observances went beyond the norm.

sentences.zh: 是以出適公主，還同在室，即情變禮，非革舊章。

translations.literal: Therefore princesses who had married out were treated like those still in the paternal home—altering the rites to suit feeling, not changing the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses who had married out were therefore treated like unmarried daughters—a concession to feeling, not a revision of statute.

sentences.zh: 今皇后二月晦，宜依元嘉十九年制，釋素即吉。

translations.literal: Now at the end of the empress's second month, she should follow the regulation of the nineteenth year of Yuanjia, lay aside plain dress, and take up auspicious dress.
translations.idiomatic: The empress should now, at the end of the second month, follow Yuanjia 19: lay aside plain dress and resume normal clothing.

sentences.zh: 以為永準。

translations.literal: Let this be the permanent standard.
translations.idiomatic: Let this stand as the permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉十五年，皇太子妃祖父右光祿大夫殷和喪，變除之禮，儀同皇后。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen, the crown prince's consort's grandfather, the Right Director of the Masters of Writing Yin He, died; the ritual for changing and removing mourning was the same as for the empress.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 15 of Emperor Wen, when the crown prince's consort's grandfather Yin He died, the rules for changing and ending mourning matched those for the empress.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武太元十五年，淑媛陳氏卒，皇太子所生也。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Taiyuan of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, the Shuyuan Chen died—she was the birth mother of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Taiyuan 15, Shuyuan Chen died; she was the crown prince's birth mother.

sentences.zh: 有司參詳母以子貴，贈淑媛為夫人，置家令典喪事。

translations.literal: The relevant offices, after consultation, held that when a mother is ennobled through her son, Shuyuan was posthumously made Lady and a Household Steward was appointed to manage the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Officials ruled that, as a mother is ennobled through her son, Shuyuan was posthumously made a Lady and a household steward was appointed for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 太子前衞率徐邈議：「喪服傳稱，與尊者為體，則不服其私親。

translations.literal: Xu Miao, former Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, submitted a discussion: "The Mourning Garments commentary says that when one forms a single body with a person of higher rank, one does not wear mourning for one's private kin.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao argued: "The Mourning Garments commentary says that one who shares a single body with a superior does not mourn private kin.

sentences.zh: 又君父所不服，子亦不敢服。

translations.literal: Again, what the lord and father do not wear, the son also dare not wear.
translations.idiomatic: What lord and father do not observe, the son likewise may not observe.

sentences.zh: 故王公妾子服其所生母，練冠麻衣，既葬而除。

translations.literal: Therefore the sons of kings and dukes by concubines wore mourning for the mothers who bore them: a practice cap and hemp garments, removed after burial.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of kings and dukes by concubines therefore mourned their birth mothers in a practice cap and hemp, laying these aside after burial.

sentences.zh: 非五服之常，則謂之無服。

translations.literal: What is not among the regular five grades of mourning is called no mourning.
translations.idiomatic: What falls outside the regular five grades is treated as no mourning.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: His view was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his view.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武大明五年閏月，皇太子妃薨。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month of the fifth year of Daming of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, the crown prince's consort died.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month of Daming, Emperor Xiaowu's crown prince's consort died.

sentences.zh: 樟木為櫬，號曰樟宮。

translations.literal: Camphor wood was made into the outer coffin, and it was styled the Camphor Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Her outer coffin was of camphor wood and was called the Camphor Palace.

sentences.zh: 載以龍輴。

translations.literal: She was carried on the dragon hearse.
translations.idiomatic: She was borne on the dragon hearse.

sentences.zh: 造陵於龍山，置大匠卿斷草，司空告后土。

translations.literal: A tomb was built on Dragon Mountain; the Director of Great Works cut the grass, and the Minister of Works reported to the earth spirit.
translations.idiomatic: A tomb was raised on Dragon Mountain; the Director of Great Works cleared the ground and the Minister of Works reported to the earth spirit.

sentences.zh: 謂葬曰山塋。

translations.literal: Burial was called a mountain tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Burial was termed a "mountain tomb.

sentences.zh: 祔文元皇后廟之陰室，在正堂後壁之外，北向。

translations.literal: She was enshrined in the side chamber of Empress Wenyuan's temple, behind the wall at the rear of the main hall, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: She was enshrined in the side chamber of Empress Wenyuan's temple, in the space behind the main hall's rear wall, facing north.

sentences.zh: 御服大功九月，設位太極東宮堂殿。

translations.literal: Imperial mourning dress of da gong for nine months was worn; a place was set in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The court wore da gong mourning for nine months, and a mourning station was set in the Eastern Palace hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 中監、黃門侍郎、僕射並從服。

translations.literal: The Supervisor of the Palace, Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate, and the Steward all followed in mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: The palace supervisor, Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate, and the Steward all wore following mourning.

sentences.zh: 從服者，御服衰乃從服，他日則否。

translations.literal: Those who follow in mourning wear it only when the court wears mourning; on other days they do not.
translations.idiomatic: Follow-mourning is worn only on days when the court is in mourning; otherwise normal dress applies.

sentences.zh: 宮臣服齊衰三月，其居宮者處寧假。

translations.literal: Palace attendants wore qi mourning for three months; those residing in the palace observed the period of repose in the mourning lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Palace officers wore qi mourning for three months; those living in the palace kept to the mourning lodge.

sentences.zh: 大明五年閏月，有司奏：「依禮皇太后服太子妃小功五月，皇后大功九月。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month of the fifth year of Daming, the relevant offices memorialized: "According to the rites, the empress dowager wears xiao gong for the crown prince's consort for five months, and the empress wears da gong for nine months.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month of Daming, officials reported: "By the rites the empress dowager wears xiao gong for five months for the crown prince's consort, and the empress wears da gong for nine months.

sentences.zh: 」右丞徐爰參議：「宮人從服者，若二御哭臨應著衰時，從服者悉著衰，非其日如常儀。

translations.literal: The Right Assistant Director Xu Yuan joined in discussion: "Among palace personnel who follow in mourning, if at the time the two consorts come to wail and attend they should wear mourning, then all who follow in mourning should wear mourning; on other days the usual protocol applies.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan added: "When the two consorts attend a wailing ceremony in mourning, all follow-mourners should wear mourning; on other days ordinary dress applies.

sentences.zh: 太子既有妃朞服，詔見之日，還著公服。

translations.literal: The crown prince, having the consort's one-year mourning grade, on days when he is summoned to audience should again wear court dress.
translations.idiomatic: While the crown prince is in one-year mourning for his consort, on days when he is summoned to audience he should wear court dress.

sentences.zh: 若至尊非哭臨日幸東宮，太子見亦如之。

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven, on a day that is not one of wailing attendance, visits the Eastern Palace, the crown prince on seeing him should do likewise.
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor visits the Eastern Palace on a day other than a wailing day, the crown prince should receive him in court dress as well.

sentences.zh: 宮臣見至尊，皆著朱衣。」

translations.literal: Palace officers on seeing the Son of Heaven all wore vermilion robes.
translations.idiomatic: Palace officers appearing before the emperor all wore vermilion robes.

sentences.zh: 大明五年閏月，有司奏：「皇太子妃薨，至尊、皇后並服大功九月，皇太后小功五月。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month of the fifth year of Daming, the relevant offices memorialized: "The crown prince's consort has died; the Son of Heaven and the empress both wear da gong for nine months, and the empress dowager wears xiao gong for five months.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month of Daming, officials reported: "With the crown prince's consort dead, the emperor and empress wear da gong for nine months and the empress dowager xiao gong for five.

sentences.zh: 未詳二御何當得作鼓吹及樂？

translations.literal: It is not clear when the two consorts may perform drum music and ordinary music.
translations.idiomatic: It was unclear when the two consorts might resume drum music and ordinary music.

sentences.zh: 」博士司馬興之議：「案禮，『齊衰大功之喪，三月不從政』。

translations.literal: Erudite Sima Xingzhi submitted a discussion: "According to the rites, 'In qi and da gong mourning, for three months one does not attend to government.'"
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Sima Xingzhi cited the rites: "In qi and da gong mourning one does not handle government for three months."

sentences.zh: 今臨軒拜授，則人君之大典，今古既異，賒促不同。

translations.literal: Now to ascend the hall and confer appointments is the great ceremony of the ruler; ancient and modern differ, and the periods allowed are not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ascending the hall to confer office is a ruler's greatest public act; past and present differ, and the time allowed varies.

sentences.zh: 愚謂皇太子妃祔廟之後，便可臨軒作樂及鼓吹。

translations.literal: In my humble view, after the crown prince's consort is enshrined in the temple, one may ascend the hall and perform music and drum signals.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that once the consort is enshrined, the court may resume hall audiences, music, and drum signals.

sentences.zh: 」右丞徐爰議：「皇太子妃雖未山塋，臨軒拜官，舊不為礙。

translations.literal: The Right Assistant Director Xu Yuan submitted a discussion: "Although the crown prince's consort has not yet been buried in the mountain tomb, ascending the hall to confer offices was not formerly an obstacle.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan replied: "Even before mountain burial, conferring offices at hall audience was never barred.

sentences.zh: 樟棺在殯，應縣而不作。

translations.literal: While the camphor coffin remains in the mourning hall, music should be suspended but not performed.
translations.idiomatic: While the camphor coffin lies in the mourning hall, instruments should hang but not sound.

sentences.zh: 祔後三御樂，宜使學官擬禮上。

translations.literal: After enshrinement, music for the three consorts should be arranged by the ritual scholars for submission.
translations.idiomatic: After enshrinement, music for the three consorts should be drafted by the ritual scholars and submitted.

sentences.zh: 」興之又議：「案禮，大功至則辟琴瑟，誠無自奏之理。

translations.literal: Xingzhi again submitted a discussion: "According to the rites, when da gong mourning arrives one sets aside zithers and se; truly there is no principle of performing music oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhi argued again: "The rites require setting zithers and se aside in da gong mourning; the mourner plainly should not play music himself.

sentences.zh: 但王者體大，理絕凡庶。

translations.literal: But the king's person is great, and principle cuts him off from commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the king's station is vast and stands apart from ordinary people.

sentences.zh: 故漢文既葬，悉皆復吉，唯縣而不樂，以此表哀。

translations.literal: Therefore after Emperor Wen of Han was buried, all alike resumed auspicious dress; only music was suspended but not played—by this mourning was shown.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen of Han's burial, all resumed festive dress, but music hung silent—mourning shown by suspension alone.

sentences.zh: 今准其輕重，侔其降殺，則下流大功，不容撤樂以終服。

translations.literal: Now, matching the weight and lightening the reduction, then for those below in da gong mourning one cannot withdraw music to the end of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Applied by analogy, lesser ranks in da gong mourning cannot keep music suspended for the full mourning term.

sentences.zh: 夫金石賓饗之禮，簫管警塗之衞，實人君之盛典，當陽之威飾，固亦不可久廢於朝。

translations.literal: Metal and stone for guest rites, pipes and flutes guarding the road—these are truly the great ceremonies of the ruler, the majesty displayed at the yang position; they also cannot long be abandoned at court.
translations.idiomatic: Bronze bells and stone chimes for guests, pipes guarding the imperial progress—these are a ruler's great ceremonies and the display of majesty; they cannot long be absent from court.

sentences.zh: 又禮無天王服嫡婦之文，直後學推貴嫡之義耳。

translations.literal: Again, the rites contain no text on the Son of Heaven wearing mourning for a principal wife; it is only later scholars extending the meaning of honoring the principal wife.
translations.idiomatic: The classics also contain no rule for a Son of Heaven mourning a principal consort; later scholars merely extended the honor due a principal wife.

sentences.zh: 既已制服成喪，虛懸終窆，亦足以甄崇冢正，標明禮歸矣。

translations.literal: Since mourning garments have already been completed and mourning suspended until final burial, this too is enough to exalt the head of the household and mark where ritual obligation lies.
translations.idiomatic: Once formal mourning is complete and only final burial remains outstanding, that is enough to honor the head of the house and mark ritual obligation.

sentences.zh: 」爰參議，皇太子朞服內，不合作樂及鼓吹。

translations.literal: Yuan joined in discussion: within the crown prince's one-year mourning, drum music and ordinary music should not be performed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan concurred: while the crown prince remains in one-year mourning, drum music and ordinary music should not be performed.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始中，陳貴妃父金寶卒。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era of Emperor Ming, the father of the Honored Consort Chen, Jin Bao, died.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Ming's Taishi reign, Jin Bao, father of Honored Consort Chen, died.

sentences.zh: 貴妃制服三十日滿，公除。

translations.literal: The consort completed mourning garments for thirty days, then underwent public removal.
translations.idiomatic: The consort wore mourning for thirty days, then underwent public removal.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝時，東海國言哀王薨踰年，嗣王乃來繼，不復追服，羣臣皆已反吉，國妃亦宜同除。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Mudi of Jin, the principality of Donghai reported that the Lamented King had died more than a year before the successor king came to succeed, and did not again put on mourning; the ministers had all returned to auspicious dress, and the princess of the state should likewise be released together.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mudi of Jin, Donghai reported that the lamented prince had been dead more than a year before the heir succeeded without renewing mourning; ministers had resumed normal dress, and the princess should do the same.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朝廷所以從權制者，以王事奪之，非為變禮也。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The reason the court follows expedient regulation is that royal affairs override mourning—not to alter the rites."
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied: "The court's expedient rule exists because state business overrides mourning—not to change ritual itself."

sentences.zh: 婦人傳重義大，若從權制，義將安託。

translations.literal: For a woman, the meaning of transmitting the patriline is great; if one follows expedient regulation, where will that meaning be lodged?
translations.idiomatic: For a woman, carrying on the patriline matters deeply; if expedient rule is applied to her, what becomes of that obligation?

sentences.zh: 」於是國妃終三年之制。

translations.literal: Thereupon the princess of the state completed the three-year regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The princess therefore completed the full three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：「廢三年之禮，開偷薄之源，漢、魏失之大者也。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng said: "To abolish the three-year mourning, opening a source of shallow conduct—Han and Wei erred greatly in this."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng wrote: "Abolishing three-year mourning opened the way to shallow conduct—a grave error of Han and Wei."

sentences.zh: 今若以丈夫宜奪以王事，婦人可終本服，是為吉凶之儀，雜陳於宮寢，綵素之制，乖異於內外，無乃情禮俱違，哀樂失所乎。

translations.literal: Now if men may be deprived for royal affairs but women may complete their proper mourning, then rites of auspice and mourning are mixed in the inner quarters, and regulations of colored and plain dress differ inside and outside—will not feeling and rite both be violated, and mourning and music lose their proper places?
translations.idiomatic: If men may be cut short for state business but women must finish full mourning, auspicious and mourning observances mingle in the inner quarters and colored and plain dress diverge within and without—feeling and rite are both breached, and grief and joy lose their places.

sentences.zh: 蕃國寡務，宜如聖典，可無疑矣。」

translations.literal: A feudal state has few affairs; it should follow the sage canon—there can be no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: A feudal domain has few state duties; it should follow the sage canon without question.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉四年八月，太傅長沙景王神主隨子南兗州刺史義欣鎮廣陵，備所加殊禮下船。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, the spirit tablet of the Grand Tutor, Prince Jing of Changsha, followed his son, the Inspector of Southern Yanzhou Yixin, who was stationed at Guangling, with all the special honors added to him, and went down to the ship.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 4, the spirit tablet of Grand Tutor Prince Jing of Changsha accompanied his son Yixin, inspector of Southern Yanzhou at Guangling, with all special honors, down to the ship.

sentences.zh: 及至鎮，入行廟。

translations.literal: On reaching the post, he entered the traveling temple.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he entered the traveling temple.

sentences.zh: 大司馬臨川烈武王神主隨子荊州刺史義慶江陵，亦如之。

translations.literal: The spirit tablet of the Grand Marshal, the Martial King of Linchuan, followed his son, the Inspector of Jingzhou Yiqing at Jiangling, in the same way.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit tablet of Grand Marshal the Martial King of Linchuan likewise followed his son Yiqing, inspector of Jingzhou at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十三年七月，白衣領御史中丞何承天奏：

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year of Yuanjia, He Chengtian, in plain dress acting as Imperial Censor, memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 23, He Chengtian, acting censor in plain dress, submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 尚書刺：「海鹽公主所生母蔣美人喪。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing impeached: "The birth mother of Princess Haiyan, Lady Jiang the Beauty, has died.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing reported: "Lady Jiang the Beauty, birth mother of Princess Haiyan, has died.

sentences.zh: 海鹽公主先離婚，今應成服，撰儀注參詳，宜下二學禮官博士議公主所服輕重。

translations.literal: Princess Haiyan had previously divorced; she should now complete mourning; ritual officers have been ordered to consult and examine—princesses' mourning grades light and heavy should be decided by discussion among the erudites of the two schools and ritual officers.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Haiyan had divorced; she must now mourn. Ritual officers were to determine the grade of mourning after consultation among university and ritual erudites.

sentences.zh: 太學博士顧雅議：『今既咸用士禮，便宜同齊衰削杖，布帶疏履，朞，禮畢，心喪三年。

translations.literal: Erudite Gu Ya of the National University submitted a discussion: "Now that commoners' rites are fully used, it is fitting to use qi mourning with staff, cloth belt, and loose shoes alike; when the one-year period is finished, heart-mourning for three years.
translations.idiomatic: National University erudite Gu Ya argued: "Since commoners' rites now apply, the princess should wear qi mourning with staff, cloth belt, and loose shoes for one year, then heart-mourn for three years.

sentences.zh: 』博士周野王議又云：『今諸王公主咸用士禮。

translations.literal: Erudite Zhou Yewang again said: "Now all princes and princesses fully use commoners' rites.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Zhou Yewang added: "All princes and princesses now follow commoners' rites.

sentences.zh: 譙王、衡陽王為所生太妃皆居重服，則公主情禮，亦宜家中朞服為允。

translations.literal: Prince Qiao and Prince Hengyang both wore heavy mourning for the birth mothers who were grand imperial consorts; then for a princess, feeling and rite alike should allow household one-year mourning as acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Qiao and Hengyang wore heavy mourning for birth mothers who were grand consorts; a princess's feeling and duty should likewise allow household one-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 』其博士庾邃之、顏測、殷明、王淵之四人同雅議；

translations.literal: The four erudites Yu Suizhi, Yan Ce, Yin Ming, and Wang Yuanzhi agreed with Ya's discussion;
translations.idiomatic: Erudites Yu Suizhi, Yan Ce, Yin Ming, and Wang Yuanzhi agreed with Gu Ya;

sentences.zh: 何惔、王羅雲二人同野王議。

translations.literal: He Tan and Wang Luoyun, two men, agreed with Yewang's discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He Tan and Wang Luoyun sided with Zhou Yewang.

sentences.zh: 」如所上臺案。

translations.literal: As submitted in the case above.
translations.idiomatic: As set forth in the memorial above.

sentences.zh: 今之諸王，雖行士禮，是施於傍親及自己以下。

translations.literal: Today's princes, though they practice commoners' rites, apply them to collateral kin and to those below themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Today's princes apply commoners' rites only to collateral kin and to those beneath themselves.

sentences.zh: 至於為帝王所厭，猶一依古典。

translations.literal: As for those whom the emperor disdains, they still follow the old canon entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Those whom the emperor's station disdains still follow the ancient canon in full.

sentences.zh: 又永初三年九月，符修儀亡，廣德三主以餘尊所厭，猶服大功。

translations.literal: Again, in the ninth month of the third year of Yongchu, when Lady Fu the Cultivated Consort died, the three princesses of Guangde, being disdained as residual honor, still wore da gong.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu 3, when Cultivated Consort Fu died, the three Guangde princesses, though disdained as residual honor, still wore da gong.

sentences.zh: 海鹽公主體自宸極，當上厭至尊，豈得遂服。

translations.literal: Princess Haiyan by status comes from the imperial apex; she should be disdained by the Son of Heaven's utmost station—how can she straightway wear mourning?
translations.idiomatic: Princess Haiyan springs from the imperial apex and should be subject to the emperor's utmost disdain—how can she simply wear mourning?

sentences.zh: 臺據經、傳正文，并引事例，依源責失。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing, relying on canonical texts of the classics and commentaries and citing precedents, traced the source and assigned the error.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing cited canonical texts and precedents, traced the source, and found the erudites in error.

sentences.zh: 而博士顧雅、周野王等捍不肯怗，方稱「自有宋以來，皇子蕃王，皆無厭降，同之士禮，著於故事。

translations.literal: Yet the erudites Gu Ya, Zhou Yewang, and others stubbornly refused to submit, still claiming that "since Song began, imperial sons and feudal princes have all had no disdain-reduction and alike used commoners' rites, recorded in precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gu Ya, Zhou Yewang, and others refused to yield, insisting that "since Song began, imperial sons and feudal princes have known no disdain-reduction and have followed commoners' rites by precedent.

sentences.zh: 緦功之服，不廢於末戚，顧獨貶於所生，是申其所輕，奪其所重。

translations.literal: Si and gong mourning is not abandoned for the most distant kin—yet Gu alone is demoted for the one who bore him; this asserts what is light and seizes what is heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Si and gong mourning is not dropped even for distant kin—yet Gu alone would demote mourning for one's birth mother, asserting the light and seizing the heavy.

sentences.zh: 奪其所重，豈緣情之謂。

translations.literal: To seize what is heavy—can this be called acting according to feeling?
translations.idiomatic: To seize what is heavy—can that be called following feeling?

sentences.zh: 」臺伏尋聖朝受終于晉，凡所施行，莫不上稽禮文，兼用晉事。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing humbly examined: our sage dynasty received the mandate from Jin; in all it has enacted, nothing fails to look up to ritual texts while also using Jin precedents.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing noted humbly: our dynasty received the mandate from Jin and in all enactments looks to ritual texts while also following Jin precedent.

sentences.zh: 又太元中，晉恭帝時為皇子，服其所生陳氏，練冠縓緣，此則前代施行故事，謹依禮文者也。

translations.literal: Again, in the Taiyuan era, when Emperor Gong of Jin was still a prince, he wore mourning for the Chen who bore him: a practice cap with hemp edging—this is a former dynasty's enacted precedent, strictly following ritual texts.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiyuan era, when Emperor Gong of Jin was still a prince, he mourned his birth mother Chen in a practice cap with hemp edging—a Jin precedent strictly following the classics.

sentences.zh: 又廣德三公主為所生母符修儀服大功，此先君餘尊之所厭者也。

translations.literal: Again, the three princesses of Guangde wore da gong for their birth mother, Cultivated Consort Fu—this is disdain by the former ruler's residual honor.
translations.idiomatic: The three Guangde princesses wore da gong for Cultivated Consort Fu, their birth mother—disdain under the former ruler's residual honor.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十三年，第七皇子不服曹婕妤，止於麻衣，此厭乎至尊者也。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanjia, the seventh prince did not wear mourning for Lady Cao the Excellent Lady; he stopped at hemp garments—this is disdain by the Son of Heaven's utmost station.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 13, the seventh prince did not mourn Excellent Lady Cao but stopped at hemp garments—disdain under the emperor's utmost station.

sentences.zh: 博士既不據古，又不依今，背違施行見事，而多作浮辭自衞。

translations.literal: The erudites neither relied on antiquity nor followed the present, going against enacted precedents now in force while making many floating phrases to defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The erudites cited neither antiquity nor current practice, defied precedents now in force, and defended themselves with empty rhetoric.

sentences.zh: 乃云五帝之時，三王之季。

translations.literal: They then said, "the age of the Five Emperors, the end of the Three Kings."
translations.idiomatic: They went on to invoke "the age of the Five Emperors" and "the twilight of the Three Kings."

sentences.zh: 又言長子去斬衰，除禫杖，皆是古禮，不少今世。

translations.literal: They also said that the eldest son removes the zhan-cui and doffs the chan staff—all are ancient rites, not at all inferior to the present age.
translations.idiomatic: They also claimed that when the eldest son sheds the hemmed mourning and lays aside the chan staff, these are all ancient rites and in no way inferior to current practice.

sentences.zh: 博士雖復引此諸條，無救於失。
