translations.literal: Though the doctors again cited these various provisions, it did not remedy the error.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the doctors cited these passages again, it could not save their position from error.

sentences.zh: 又詰臺云：「蕃國得遂其私情，此義出何經記？

translations.literal: He also questioned the Secretariat, saying: "That feudatory states may fulfill their private filial sentiments—from what classic or record does this principle come?
translations.idiomatic: He also pressed the Secretariat: "If feudatory princes may act on private filial feeling, in which classic or record is that principle found?

sentences.zh: 」臣案南譙、衡陽太妃並受朝命，為國小君，是以二王得遂其服，豈可為美人比例。

translations.literal: " The minister replies: The consorts-dowager of Nanqiao and Hengyang both received court appointments as petty sovereigns of their states; therefore the two princes were able to fulfill their mourning—how can one take this as a parallel for a meiren?
translations.idiomatic: " The memorialist replies: The consorts-dowager of Nanqiao and Hengyang both held court appointments as petty sovereigns of their states, which is why those two princes could complete their mourning—how can that be compared with a palace lady?

sentences.zh: 尋蕃王得遂者，聖朝之所許也。

translations.literal: In investigating cases where feudatory princes were allowed to fulfill mourning—the dynastic court permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: As for feudatory princes who were allowed to complete mourning, that was something our dynasty expressly permitted.

sentences.zh: 皇子公主不得申者，由有厭而然也。

translations.literal: That princes and princesses could not express mourning was because there was honor-suppression.
translations.idiomatic: That imperial princes and princesses could not press their mourning was due to honor-suppression.

sentences.zh: 臺登重更責失制不得過十日，而復不酬答。

translations.literal: The Secretariat again held them responsible for exceeding the ten-day limit on procedural failures, yet they still did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat again charged them with violating the rule that procedural failures must not exceed ten days, yet they still gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 既被催攝二三日，甫輸怗辭。

translations.literal: Having been pressed to respond for two or three days, they finally submitted compliant words.
translations.idiomatic: After being pressed to answer for two or three days, they finally submitted a compliant reply.

sentences.zh: 雖理屈事窮，猶聞義恥服。

translations.literal: Though their reasoning was defeated and their case exhausted, they still knew shame at yielding on principle.
translations.idiomatic: Though their argument was defeated and their case exhausted, they still felt shame at yielding on principle.

sentences.zh: 臣聞喪紀有制，禮之大經；

translations.literal: I have heard that mourning observances have fixed regulations—the great constant of ritual;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that mourning has fixed regulations—the great constant of ritual;

sentences.zh: 降殺攸宜，家國舊典。

translations.literal: grading and reduction as appropriate is the old canon of family and state.
translations.idiomatic: graded reduction as appropriate is the long-standing canon of family and state.

sentences.zh: 古之諸侯眾子，猶以尊厭；

translations.literal: In antiquity even the many sons of feudal lords were still subject to honor-suppression;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity even the many sons of feudal lords were still subject to honor-suppression;

sentences.zh: 況在王室，而欲同之士庶。

translations.literal: how much more in the imperial house—yet they wish to be equated with scholar-gentry and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: how much more within the imperial house—and yet they wish to be treated like common scholars and commoners.

sentences.zh: 此之僻謬，不俟言而顯。

translations.literal: This perversity needs no words to make plain.
translations.idiomatic: This perversity is obvious without need of further argument.

sentences.zh: 太常統寺，曾不研却，所謂同乎失者，亦未得之。

translations.literal: The Director of Ceremonies overseeing the bureau never examined and rejected this—what is called "being alike in error"—they have not grasped it either.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Ceremonies, who oversees the ritual bureau, never examined and rejected this; as for what is called "sharing the same error," they too have not understood it.

sentences.zh: 宜加裁正，弘明國典。

translations.literal: They should be corrected and the national statutes clarified and proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: They should be corrected so that the national statutes may be clarified and upheld.

sentences.zh: 謹案太學博士顧雅、國子助教周野王、博士王羅雲、顏測、殷明、何惔、王淵之、前博士遷員外散騎侍郎庾邃之等，咸蒙抽飾，備位前疑，既不謹守舊文，又不審據前准，遂上背經典，下違故事，率意妄作，自造禮章。

translations.literal: Respectfully reviewing: University Doctors Gu Ya, Imperial University assistant instructor Zhou Yewang, Doctors Wang Luoyun, Yan Ce, Yin Ming, He Tan, Wang Yuanzhi, former Doctor promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat Yuan Suizhi, and others—all were selected and adorned, filling the advisory posts; neither carefully observing old texts nor properly judging prior precedents, they thus turned their backs on the classics above and violated precedent below, following their whims to fabricate ritual chapters on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully reported: University Doctor Gu Ya, Imperial University assistant instructor Zhou Yewang, Doctors Wang Luoyun, Yan Ce, Yin Ming, He Tan, and Wang Yuanzhi, and former Doctor, now Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat Yuan Suizhi—all had been selected and elevated to advisory posts; yet they neither carefully upheld the old texts nor properly applied prior precedents, and so turned their backs on the classics above while violating established practice below, following whim to invent ritual provisions on their own.

sentences.zh: 太常臣敬叔位居宗伯，問禮所司，騰述往反，了無研却，混同茲失，亦宜及咎。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Jingshu holds the position of lineage elder, the office that handles ritual inquiries; in drafting replies back and forth he did not examine and reject at all, mingling this error—he too should bear blame.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Jingshu holds the post of ritual elder and heads the office charged with ritual questions; in drafting exchanges back and forth he never examined and rejected the error, and by mingling himself in the same mistake he too should bear blame.

sentences.zh: 請以見事並免今所居官，解野王領國子助教。

translations.literal: Request that according to current facts they all be removed from their present offices, and Zhou Yewang be dismissed from his concurrent post as Imperial University assistant instructor.
translations.idiomatic: It is requested that, on the basis of the facts now before the court, they all be removed from their present offices, and that Zhou Yewang be relieved of his concurrent post as Imperial University assistant instructor.

sentences.zh: 雅、野王初立議乖舛，中執捍愆失，未違十日之限，雖起一事，合成三愆，羅雲掌押捍失，三人加禁固五年。

translations.literal: Ya and Yewang in first proposing the errant opinion, in the middle persisting in resistance to admitted faults, not exceeding the ten-day limit—though arising from one matter, together they make three offenses; Luoyun supervised the drafting and resistance to fault; the three men are to receive five years of banishment confinement.
translations.idiomatic: Ya and Yewang first proposed the mistaken opinion and then persisted in resisting admitted faults, without exceeding the ten-day limit; though the matter arose once, together it constitutes three offenses. Luoyun supervised the drafting and resistance to fault. The three men are to be placed under banishment confinement for five years.

sentences.zh: 詔敬叔白衣領職。

translations.literal: An edict had Jingshu lead his office in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Jingshu to carry out his duties in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 餘如奏。

translations.literal: The rest as memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder as memorialized.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十九年，南平王鑠所生母吳淑儀薨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia, the birth mother of Prince Shuo of Nanping, Lady Wu the Fair Cultivator, died.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 29, the birth mother of Prince Shuo of Nanping, Lady Wu Shuyi, died.

sentences.zh: 依禮無服，麻衣練冠，既葬而除。

translations.literal: According to ritual there was no formal mourning garment; hemp clothes and white-trimmed cap, removed after burial.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual there was no full mourning garment; they wore hemp clothes and a white-trimmed cap, which were removed after burial.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「古者與尊者為體，不得服其私親。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: "In antiquity one formed a ritual body with one of higher rank and could not wear mourning for one's private kin.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices memorialized: "In antiquity one formed one's ritual body with a superior and therefore could not wear mourning for private kin.

sentences.zh: 而比世諸侯咸用士禮，五服之內，悉皆成服，於其所生，反不得遂。

translations.literal: Yet in recent generations all feudal lords use commoner ritual; within the five degrees of mourning all complete full mourning, yet toward their birth mothers they cannot fulfill it."
translations.idiomatic: Yet in recent times feudal lords have all used commoner ritual: within the five degrees of mourning everyone completes full mourning, while toward their birth mothers they are not allowed to do so."

sentences.zh: 」於是皇子皆申母服。

translations.literal: Thereupon all imperial princes expressed mourning for their mothers.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all imperial princes were allowed to observe mourning for their mothers.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝孝建元年六月己巳，有司奏：「故第十六皇弟休倩薨夭，年始及殤，追贈諡東平沖王。

translations.literal: On the jisi day of the sixth month in the first year of Xiaojian of Emperor Xiaowu, the relevant offices memorialized: "The late sixteenth imperial younger brother Xiujian died young, his years just reaching the shang boundary; posthumously enfeoffed and titled Prince Chong of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day of the sixth month in Xiaojian 1 of Emperor Xiaowu, the relevant offices memorialized: "The late sixteenth imperial younger brother Xiujian died young, having just reached the age of shang mourning; he was posthumously enfeoffed and given the posthumous title Prince Chong of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 服制未有成准，輙下禮官詳議。

translations.literal: Mourning regulations have no fixed precedent—urgently sent down to ritual officers for detailed deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: There is no established standard for mourning dress, and the matter was urgently referred to the ritual officers for detailed deliberation."

sentences.zh: 」太學博士陸澄議：「案禮有成人道，則不為殤。

translations.literal: University Doctor Lu Cheng argued: "Examining ritual, if one has the way of adulthood, then one is not treated as shang."
translations.idiomatic: University Doctor Lu Cheng argued: "According to ritual, if one has attained the way of adulthood, one is not treated under the shang rules."

sentences.zh: 今既追胙土宇，遠崇封秩，圭黻備典，成孰大焉。

translations.literal: Now having been granted sacrificial territory and enfeoffment rank raised far, regalia and emblems complete in canon—how much greater is full maturity.
translations.idiomatic: Now that sacrificial territory has been granted and enfeoffment rank has been raised to a high level, with regalia and emblems complete according to canon, how much greater is full maturity?

sentences.zh: 典文式昭，殤名去矣。

translations.literal: When canonical texts and forms are manifest, the name "shang" is removed.
translations.idiomatic: When canonical texts and forms are made manifest, the designation of shang is set aside.

sentences.zh: 夫典文垂式，元服表身，猶以免孺子之制，全丈夫之義。

translations.literal: Canonical texts hang as models; capping ceremony shows the person—even so they escape infant regulations and complete the meaning of the full adult.
translations.idiomatic: Canonical texts provide enduring models, and the capping ceremony marks the person; even so, infant regulations are set aside and the status of a full adult is completed.

sentences.zh: 安有名頒爵首，而可服以殤禮。

translations.literal: How can one have a title conferring feudal rank and yet wear the shang mourning?
translations.idiomatic: How can one receive a title conferring feudal rank and still be mourned under the shang rules?

sentences.zh: 」有司尋澄議無明證，却使秉正更上。

translations.literal: The offices found Cheng's argument without clear proof, rejected it, and had Bing Zheng submit again.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices found that Cheng's argument lacked clear precedent, rejected it, and had Bing Zheng submit a further opinion.

sentences.zh: 澄重議：「竊謂贈之為義，所以追加名器。

translations.literal: Cheng re-argued: "I venture that the meaning of posthumous enfeoffment is to add name and regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng argued again: "I venture that the meaning of posthumous enfeoffment is to add title and regalia.

sentences.zh: 故贈公者便成公，贈卿者便成卿。

translations.literal: Thus one posthumously made duke is thereby a duke; posthumously made minister is thereby a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one who is posthumously made a duke thereby becomes a duke, and one posthumously made a minister thereby becomes a minister.

sentences.zh: 贈之以王，得不為王乎？

translations.literal: Posthumously made a king—can he not be a king?
translations.idiomatic: If one is posthumously made a king, can he not be treated as a king?

sentences.zh: 然則有在生而封，或既沒而爵，俱受帝命，不為吉凶殊典；

translations.literal: Then there is enfeoffment in life or ennoblement after death—both receive imperial command, not different canonical treatment for auspicious vs. inauspicious;
translations.idiomatic: There are cases of enfeoffment in life and cases of ennoblement after death, but both receive the imperial command and are not given different canonical treatment according to whether the event is auspicious or inauspicious;

sentences.zh: 同備文物，豈以存亡異數。

translations.literal: both complete regalia and ritual objects—how use alive vs. dead to make different numbers?
translations.idiomatic: both are fully equipped with regalia and ritual objects—how can living and dead be treated by different standards?

sentences.zh: 今璽策咸秩，是成人之禮；

translations.literal: Now seals and patent all in due order—this is the ritual of the full adult;
translations.idiomatic: Now that seals and patent are all in due order, this is the ritual of a full adult;

sentences.zh: 羣后臨哀，非下殤之制。

translations.literal: the hosts of nobles attending mourning is not the regulation for lower shang.
translations.idiomatic: the assembly of nobles attending the mourning is not the regulation for lower shang.

sentences.zh: 若喪用成人，親以殤服，末學含疑，未之或辨。

translations.literal: If for the funeral one uses adult ritual but relatives wear shang garments—later scholars harbor doubt, and none may have distinguished it.
translations.idiomatic: If the funeral follows adult ritual while relatives wear shang mourning, later scholars may harbor doubt, but none has clearly distinguished the point.

sentences.zh: 敢求詳衷如所稱。

translations.literal: I dare request detailed consideration as stated."
translations.idiomatic: I dare request detailed deliberation along the lines stated."

sentences.zh: 」左丞臣羊希參議：「尋澄議，既無畫然前例，不合准據。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Minister Yang Xi joined discussion: "Examining Cheng's argument, there is neither clear-cut prior precedent nor basis for approval.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Minister Yang Xi submitted a joint opinion: "Examining Cheng's argument, there is neither a clear prior precedent nor a basis on which to approve it.

sentences.zh: 案禮，子不殤父，臣不殤君。

translations.literal: Examining ritual: a son does not treat a father as shang; a minister does not treat a lord as shang.
translations.idiomatic: According to ritual, a son does not mourn a father under the shang rules, and a minister does not mourn a lord under the shang rules.

sentences.zh: 君父至尊，臣子恩重，不得以幼年而降。

translations.literal: Lord and father are supremely honored; minister-son obligation is weighty—one cannot lower it because of youth.
translations.idiomatic: Lord and father are supremely honored, and the obligation of minister or son is weighty; one cannot reduce mourning because of youth.

sentences.zh: 又曰，『尊同則服其親服』，推此文旨，旁親自宜服殤，所不殤者唯施臣子而已。

translations.literal: It also says, "when rank is the same, one wears the relative's mourning"—extending this text's intent, collateral kin should naturally wear shang mourning; only toward lord and father does the non-shang rule apply."
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "when rank is the same, one wears mourning for the relative"—extending the meaning of this passage, collateral kin should naturally wear shang mourning; only toward lord and father does the rule against shang mourning apply."

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年六月，湘東國刺稱「國太妃以去三十年閏六月二十八日薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Xiaojian 1, a memorial from Xiangdong principality stated: "The state consort-dowager died on the intercalary sixth month, twenty-eighth day, thirty years ago.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Xiaojian 1, a memorial from the principality of Xiangdong stated: "The state consort-dowager died on the twenty-eighth day of the intercalary sixth month thirty years ago.

sentences.zh: 未詳周忌當在六月？

translations.literal: It is unclear whether the annual mourning anniversary should fall in the sixth month?
translations.idiomatic: It is unclear whether the annual mourning anniversary should fall in the sixth month,

sentences.zh: 為取七月？

translations.literal: or should the seventh month be taken?
translations.idiomatic: or whether the seventh month should be taken?

sentences.zh: 勒禮官議正」。

translations.literal: Ordered ritual officers to deliberate and decide."
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officers were ordered to deliberate and decide."

sentences.zh: 博士丘邁之議：「案吳商議，閏月亡者，應以本正之月為忌。

translations.literal: Doctor Qiu Maizhi argued: "Per Wu Shang's discussion, one who dies in an intercalary month should use the corresponding regular month for the anniversary taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Doctor Qiu Maizhi argued: "According to Wu Shang's discussion, when someone dies in an intercalary month, the mourning anniversary should be observed in the corresponding regular month.

sentences.zh: 謂正閏論雖各有所執，商議為允。

translations.literal: Though proponents of regular vs. intercalary month differ, Shang's discussion is sound.
translations.idiomatic: Although advocates of the regular month and of the intercalary month each have their own position, Shang's discussion is sound.

sentences.zh: 宜以今六月為忌。

translations.literal: The present sixth month should be the taboo day."
translations.idiomatic: The present sixth month should be taken as the anniversary."

sentences.zh: 」左僕射建平王宏謂：「邁之議不可准據。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Prince Hong of Pingping said: "Maizhi's discussion cannot be approved.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Prince Hong of Pingping said: "Maizhi's discussion cannot be approved.

sentences.zh: 案晉世及皇代以來，閏月亡者，以閏之後月祥。

translations.literal: Examining from Jin times and our dynasty, those who died in intercalary months use the month after the intercalary for the xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Jin times and our own dynasty, when someone died in an intercalary month the xiang was observed in the month following the intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 宜以來七月為祥忌。

translations.literal: The coming seventh month should be taken for xiang and taboo."
translations.idiomatic: The coming seventh month should be taken for the xiang and the anniversary."

sentences.zh: 」及大明元年二月，有司又奏：「太常鄱陽哀王去年閏三月十八日薨。

translations.literal: And in the second month of Daming 1, the offices memorialized: "Director of Ceremonies Prince Ai of Poyang died on intercalary third month, eighteenth day, last year.
translations.idiomatic: Then in the second month of Daming 1, the relevant offices memorialized: "Prince Ai of Poyang, Director of Ceremonies, died on the eighteenth day of the intercalary third month last year.

sentences.zh: 今為何月末祥除？

translations.literal: In which month-end should the xiang removal fall now?
translations.idiomatic: In which month-end should the xiang removal now fall?

sentences.zh: 」下禮官議正。

translations.literal: Sent down to ritual officers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was sent down to the ritual officers for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 博士傅休議：「尋三禮，喪遇閏，月數者數閏，歲數者沒閏，閏在朞內故也。

translations.literal: Doctor Fu Xiu argued: "Examining the Three Rites, when mourning meets an intercalary month—if counting months one counts the intercalary; if counting years one omits the intercalary, because the intercalary is within the period.
translations.idiomatic: Doctor Fu Xiu argued: "According to the Three Rites, when mourning encounters an intercalary month, if one counts by months one counts the intercalary month, but if one counts by years one omits it, because the intercalary month falls within the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽哀王去年閏三月薨，月次節物，則定是四月之分，應以今年四月末為祥。

translations.literal: Prince Ai of Poyang died in the intercalary third month last year; by month sequence and seasonal markers it is definitely the division of the fourth month—this year's fourth month-end should be xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ai of Poyang died in the intercalary third month last year; by month sequence and seasonal markers it clearly belongs to the fourth month, and the xiang should therefore fall at the end of the fourth month this year.

sentences.zh: 晉元、明二帝，並以閏二月崩，以閏後月祥，先代成准，則是今比。

translations.literal: Emperors Yuan and Ming of Jin both died in intercalary second month and took the month after intercalary for xiang—precedent for our day.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Yuan and Ming of Jin both died in the intercalary second month and observed the xiang in the month after the intercalary month; that established precedent applies to the present case.

sentences.zh: 」太常丞庾蔚之議：「禮，正月存親，故有忌日之感。

translations.literal: Director of Ceremonies Assistant Yu Weizhi argued: "In ritual, the first month preserves the kin, hence the feeling of the taboo day.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Ceremonies Assistant Yu Weizhi argued: "In ritual, the first month preserves the kin, and therefore gives rise to the feeling associated with the anniversary.

sentences.zh: 四時既已變，人情亦已衰，故有二祥之殺。

translations.literal: The four seasons having changed, human feeling has also waned, hence the reduction of the two xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Once the four seasons have changed, human feeling has also waned, and therefore the two xiang observances are reduced.

sentences.zh: 是則祥忌皆以同月為議，而閏亡者，明年必無其月，不可以無其月而不祥忌，故必宜用閏所附之月。

translations.literal: Thus xiang and taboo are both deliberated in the same month; but one who dies in intercalary has no such month next year—one cannot omit xiang and taboo for lack of the month, so one must use the month to which the intercalary is attached.
translations.idiomatic: Thus both xiang and anniversary are normally observed in the same month; but one who dies in an intercalary month will have no such month in the following year, and one cannot omit the xiang and anniversary merely because that month is absent. Therefore one must use the regular month to which the intercalary month is attached.

sentences.zh: 閏月附正，公羊明議，故班固以閏九月為後九月，月名既不殊，天時亦不異。

translations.literal: Intercalary month attaches to the regular—Gongyang's clear discussion; hence Ban Gu treats intercalary ninth as the latter ninth month; the month name is not different, nor is the season.
translations.idiomatic: The intercalary month is attached to the regular month, as the Gongyang commentary clearly states; hence Ban Gu treats the intercalary ninth month as the latter ninth month. The month name is not different, nor is the season.

sentences.zh: 若用閏之後月，則春夏永革，節候亦舛。

translations.literal: If one uses the month after intercalary, spring and summer are forever altered, and seasonal markers are also wrong.
translations.idiomatic: If one uses the month after the intercalary month, spring and summer would be permanently displaced and the seasonal markers would also be wrong.

sentences.zh: 設有人以閏臘月亡者，若用閏後月為祥忌，則祥忌應在後年正月。

translations.literal: Suppose someone dies in intercalary twelfth month—if the month after intercalary is used for xiang and taboo, xiang and taboo would fall in the first month of the year after next.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose someone dies in the intercalary twelfth month: if the month after the intercalary month were used for the xiang and anniversary, those observances would fall in the first month of the year after next.

sentences.zh: 祥涉三載，既失周朞之義，冬亡而春忌，又乖致感之本。

translations.literal: Xiang would span three years—violating the Zhou period meaning; winter death with spring taboo also violates the root of evoking feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The xiang would then span three years, violating the meaning of the Zhou mourning period; a death in winter with an anniversary in spring would also violate the root principle of evoking feeling.

sentences.zh: 譬今年末三十日亡，明年末月小，若以去年二十九日親尚存，則應用後年正朝為忌，此必不然。

translations.literal: For example one dies on the thirtieth day of the year's end; next year the last month is short—if on the twenty-ninth of last year the kin was still alive, one would use the New Year of the year after next for taboo—this surely cannot be so.
translations.idiomatic: For example, if someone dies on the thirtieth day at the end of the year and the last month of the following year is short, one could not say that because the kin was still alive on the twenty-ninth of last year, the anniversary should be observed on New Year's Day of the year after next—that surely cannot be right.

sentences.zh: 則閏亡可知也。

translations.literal: Then intercalary-month death is knowable.
translations.idiomatic: From this the rule for intercalary-month death becomes clear.

sentences.zh: 」通關並同蔚之議，三月末祥。

translations.literal: The organs through-hall all agreed with Weizhi; third month-end for xiang.
translations.idiomatic: The offices through the Secretariat all agreed with Weizhi: the xiang should fall at the end of the third month.

sentences.zh: 大明五年七月，有司奏：「故永陽縣開國侯劉叔子夭喪，年始四歲，傍親服制有疑。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Daming 5, the offices memorialized: "The former Marquis Who Founded Yongyang County, Liu Shuzi, died young at the age of four; there is doubt about collateral mourning regulations."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Daming 5, the relevant offices memorialized: "The former founding marquis of Yongyang County, Liu Shuzi, died young at the age of four, and there is doubt about the mourning dress of collateral kin."

sentences.zh: 」太學博士虞龢、領軍長史周景遠、司馬朱膺之、前太常丞庾蔚之等議，並云「宜同成人之服。

translations.literal: University Doctor Yu He, Chief Clerk of the Army of the Palace Guard Zhou Jingyuan, Marshal Zhu Yingzhi, former Director of Ceremonies Assistant Yu Weizhi, and others deliberated, all saying "they should wear the same mourning as adults."
translations.idiomatic: University Doctor Yu He, Chief Clerk of the Army of the Palace Guard Zhou Jingyuan, Marshal Zhu Yingzhi, former Director of Ceremonies Assistant Yu Weizhi, and others all argued that "they should wear the same mourning as adults."

sentences.zh: 東平沖王服殤，實由追贈，異於已受茅土」。

translations.literal: Prince Chong of Dongping wore shang mourning only because of posthumous enfeoffment, which differs from one who had already received a fief of soil."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chong of Dongping wore shang mourning only because of posthumous enfeoffment, which differs from one who had already received a territorial fief."

sentences.zh: 博士司馬興之議：「應同東平殤服。

translations.literal: Doctor Sima Xingzhi argued: "They should follow the shang mourning of Dongping."
translations.idiomatic: Doctor Sima Xingzhi argued: "They should follow the shang mourning used for Dongping."

sentences.zh: 」左丞荀萬秋等參議：「南面君國，繼體承家，雖則佩觿，未闕成德，君父名正，臣子不容服殤，故云『臣不殤君，子不殤父』。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Minister Xun Wanqiu and others joined discussion: "Facing south to rule a state and succeeding to the patrimony, though they may wear the girdle pendant, they have not yet lacked full virtue; lord and father names are correct, and as minister or son one may not wear shang mourning—hence it is said, "a minister does not mourn a lord under shang rules, a son does not mourn a father under shang rules."
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Minister Xun Wanqiu and others submitted a joint opinion: "One who faces south to rule a state and succeeds to the patrimony, though still wearing the girdle pendant of youth, has not yet failed in full virtue; the names of lord and father are established, and as minister or son one may not wear shang mourning—hence the saying, "a minister does not mourn a lord under shang rules, a son does not mourn a father under shang rules."

sentences.zh: 推此，則知傍親故依殤制。

translations.literal: Extending this, one knows that collateral kin should follow the shang regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Extending this principle, one sees that collateral kin should follow the shang regulations.

sentences.zh: 東平沖王已經前議。

translations.literal: Prince Chong of Dongping was already decided by the earlier deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chong of Dongping had already been decided by the earlier deliberation.

sentences.zh: 若升仕朝列，則為大成，故鄱陽哀王追贈太常，親戚不降。

translations.literal: If one rises to court office, then one is fully mature; therefore when Prince Ai of Poyang was posthumously made Director of Ceremonies, collateral kin did not reduce mourning.
translations.idiomatic: If one rises to court office, one is treated as fully mature; therefore when Prince Ai of Poyang was posthumously made Director of Ceremonies, collateral kin did not reduce mourning.

sentences.zh: 愚謂下殤以上，身居封爵，宜同成人。

translations.literal: In my humble view, from lower shang upward, if one holds a feudal title in person, one should be treated like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, from lower shang upward, if one personally holds a feudal title, one should be treated like an adult.

sentences.zh: 年在無服之殤，以登官為斷。

translations.literal: For ages within shang for which there is no mourning garment, office-holding should be the dividing line.
translations.idiomatic: For ages within shang mourning for which no garment is prescribed, holding office should be the dividing line.

sentences.zh: 今永陽國臣，自應全服，至於傍親，宜從殤禮。

translations.literal: Now the subjects of Yongyang should wear full mourning, but for collateral kin shang ritual should be followed."
translations.idiomatic: In the present case, the subjects of Yongyang should wear full mourning, but collateral kin should follow shang ritual."

sentences.zh: 」詔「景遠議為允」。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Jingyuan's discussion is approved."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Jingyuan's discussion is approved."

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽二年七月，有司奏：「第七皇弟訓養母鄭修容喪。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Yuanhui 2 of the Deposed Emperor, the offices memorialized: "The seventh imperial younger brother's foster mother, Lady Zheng Xiurong, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Yuanhui 2 under the Deposed Emperor, the relevant offices memorialized: "The foster mother of the seventh imperial younger brother, Lady Zheng Xiurong, has died.

sentences.zh: 未詳服制，下禮官正議。

translations.literal: Mourning regulations are unclear; sent down to ritual officers for correct deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: The mourning regulations are unclear, and the matter was sent down to the ritual officers for correct deliberation."

sentences.zh: 」太學博士周山文議：「案庶母慈己者，小功五月。

translations.literal: University Doctor Zhou Shanwen argued: "According to ritual, for a concubine mother who has shown affection, one wears xiao-gong for five months."
translations.idiomatic: University Doctor Zhou Shanwen argued: "According to ritual, for a concubine mother who has shown affection to the child, one wears xiao-gong mourning for five months."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云：『其使養之不命為母子，亦服庶母慈己之服。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: "If she was made to rear the child but was not appointed mother and son, one still wears mourning for a concubine mother who has shown affection."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says: "If she was made to rear the child but was not formally appointed mother and son, one still wears mourning for a concubine mother who has shown affection."

sentences.zh: 』愚謂第七皇弟宜從小功之制。

translations.literal: In my humble view the seventh imperial younger brother should follow the xiao-gong regulation."
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view the seventh imperial younger brother should follow the xiao-gong regulation."

sentences.zh: 」參議並同。

translations.literal: The joint deliberators all agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The joint deliberators all agreed.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏廢帝喪親三年之制，而魏世或為舊君服三年者。

translations.literal: Under Han and Wei, deposed emperors observed three-year mourning for kin; in Wei times some still wore three years for a former lord.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han and Wei, deposed emperors observed the three-year mourning for kin, and in Wei times some still wore three years of mourning for a former lord.

sentences.zh: 至晉泰始四年，尚書何楨奏：「故辟舉綱紀吏，不計違適，皆反服舊君齊衰三月。

translations.literal: By the fourth year of Taishi of Jin, Minister of the Secretariat He Zhen memorialized: "Former officials raised through recommendation and registry, regardless of whether they had left office properly or improperly, all returned to wear qi-sackcloth for three months for their former lord."
translations.idiomatic: By Taishi 4 of Jin, Minister of the Secretariat He Zhen memorialized: "Former officials raised through recommendation and registry, regardless of whether they had left office properly or improperly, all returned to wear qi-sackcloth mourning for three months for their former lord."

sentences.zh: 」於是詔書下其奏，所適無貴賤，悉同依古典。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict transmitted his memorial; wherever they had gone, high or low, all alike followed the ancient canon.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict transmitted his memorial, and wherever they had gone, high or low alike followed the ancient canon.

sentences.zh: 魏武以正月崩，魏文以其年七月設伎樂百戲，是魏不以喪廢樂也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei died in the first month; Emperor Wen of Wei in that same year, in the seventh month, established a hundred kinds of music and entertainments—thus Wei did not suspend music because of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Wei died in the first month, and in the seventh month of that same year Emperor Wen of Wei established a hundred kinds of music and entertainments—thus Wei did not suspend music because of mourning.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝以來，國有大喪未除，正會亦廢樂。

translations.literal: From Emperor Wu of Jin onward, when the state had a great mourning not yet ended, the regular court assembly also suspended music.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Wu of Jin onward, when the state was in great mourning that had not yet ended, the regular court assembly also suspended music.

sentences.zh: 太安元年，太子喪未除，正會亦廢樂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taian, when the crown prince's mourning had not yet ended, the regular assembly also suspended music.
translations.idiomatic: In Taian 1, when the crown prince's mourning had not yet ended, the regular assembly also suspended music.

sentences.zh: 穆帝永和中，為中原山陵未修復，頻年會，輒廢樂。

translations.literal: In the Yonghe era of Emperor Mu, because the imperial tombs in the Central Plains had not yet been restored, at successive annual assemblies music was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Mu's Yonghe reign, the tombs of the Central Plains still unrestored, and at each year's grand assembly music was set aside.

sentences.zh: 是時太后臨朝，后父褚裒薨，元會又廢樂。

translations.literal: At that time the empress dowager held court; when the empress's father Chu Pou died, the New Year's assembly again suspended music.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was regent at the time; when the empress's father Chu Pou died, music was again suspended at the New Year's assembly.

sentences.zh: 晉世孝武太元六年，為皇后王氏喪，亦廢樂。

translations.literal: In Jin, in the sixth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu, for the mourning of Empress Wang music was also suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin's Emperor Xiaowu, in the sixth year of Taiyuan, music was likewise suspended for the mourning of Empress Wang.

sentences.zh: 宋大喪則廢樂。

translations.literal: Under Song, at a great state mourning music was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In the Song, a great imperial mourning also meant suspending music.

sentences.zh: 漢獻帝建安末，魏武帝作終令曰：「古之葬者，必在瘠薄之地，其規西原上為壽陵。

translations.literal: At the end of Jian'an under Emperor Xian of Han, Emperor Wu of Wei made his final instructions, saying: "In antiquity those who buried the dead chose necessarily barren and thin ground; he planned Shouling on the western plateau.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jian'an, Emperor Xian of Han's reign, Cao Cao issued his final instructions: "Ancient burials were placed on lean, poor soil; he planned Shouling on the western heights.

sentences.zh: 因高為基，不封不樹。

translations.literal: Taking the height as the foundation, no mound was raised and no trees planted.
translations.idiomatic: The grave took the hill itself as its form—no mound, no planted trees.

sentences.zh: 周禮，冢人掌公墓之地，凡諸侯居左右以前，卿大夫居後。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, the tomb-keeper supervised the land of the public tombs; feudal lords were placed to left and right and forward, ministers and grandees behind.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou assign the tomb-keeper charge of the royal cemetery: feudal lords to the sides and front, ministers and grandees to the rear.

sentences.zh: 漢制亦謂之陪陵。

translations.literal: Under Han institutions this was also called accompanying the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Han usage called this "accompanying the tomb."

sentences.zh: 其公卿大臣列將有功者，宜陪壽陵。

translations.literal: Those among the high ministers, great officials, and ranked generals who had merit should accompany Shouling.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious ministers, great officials, and ranked generals were to be buried beside Shouling.

sentences.zh: 其廣為兆域，使足相容。

translations.literal: The burial precinct should be made broad enough to hold them all.
translations.idiomatic: The burial precinct was to be widened until all could be accommodated.

sentences.zh: 」魏武以送終制衣服四篋，題識其上，春秋冬夏日有不諱，隨時以斂。

translations.literal: " Cao Wu, for his funeral arrangements, prepared four boxes of garments, marked on each; for spring, summer, autumn, and winter there was no taboo—he was to be enshrouded according to the season.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao set out four boxes of burial garments, each labeled; with no seasonal taboo, he was to be dressed according to the time of year.

sentences.zh: 金珥珠玉銅鐵之物，一不得送。

translations.literal: Objects of gold, ear ornaments, pearls, jade, bronze, and iron were not to be sent to the grave at all.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing of gold, jade, pearls, bronze, or iron was to go into the tomb.

sentences.zh: 文帝遵奉，無所增加。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen followed and observed this, adding nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen followed the instructions without addition.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，刻金璽，追加尊號。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, a golden seal was carved and an additional honorific title appended.
translations.idiomatic: After accepting the throne, a golden seal was carved and further honorific titles added.

sentences.zh: 不敢開埏，乃為石室，藏璽埏首，示陵中無金銀諸物也。

translations.literal: He dared not open the tomb passage; therefore he made a stone chamber and stored the seal at the head of the passage, to show that the tomb held no gold, silver, or other valuables.
translations.idiomatic: He would not open the tomb passage; instead a stone chamber was built and the seal placed at the passage head, showing the mound held no gold or silver.

sentences.zh: 漢禮明器甚多，自是皆省矣。

translations.literal: Under Han ritual there were many mingqi grave goods; from this time onward all were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Han funeral rites had required many mingqi; from this point they were largely cut away.

sentences.zh: 文帝黃初三年，又自作終制：「禮，國君即位，為椑，存不忘亡也。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangchu, Emperor Wen again made his own final instructions: "In ritual, when a feudal lord takes the throne he prepares his coffin, keeping the living mindful that the dead are not forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangchu year three, Cao Pi issued his own final instructions: "Ritual requires a ruler, on accession, to prepare his coffin—so the living do not forget the dead.

sentences.zh: 壽陵因山為體，無封無樹，無立寢殿，造園邑，通神道。

translations.literal: Shouling takes the mountain as its body: no mound, no trees, no sleeping hall erected, no park-settlement built, no spirit-way opened.
translations.idiomatic: Shouling was to take the mountain as its form—no mound, no trees, no sleeping hall, no park-settlement, no spirit-way.

sentences.zh: 夫葬者，藏也。

translations.literal: Burial means concealment.
translations.idiomatic: To bury is to hide away.

sentences.zh: 欲人之不能見也。

translations.literal: The wish is that people cannot see it.
translations.idiomatic: The aim is that none may see the dead.

sentences.zh: 禮不墓祭，欲存亡之不黷也。

translations.literal: Ritual does not permit sacrifice at the mound, wishing that the living and dead not be profaned together.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual forbids sacrifice at the mound, lest the living profane the dead.

sentences.zh: 皇后及貴人以下，不隨王之國者，有終沒，皆葬澗西，前又已表其處矣。

translations.literal: The empress and honored ladies below her who did not follow the king to his fief, when their lives ended, were all buried west of the Jian River; their places had already been set forth before.
translations.idiomatic: The empress and consorts who did not follow the king to his fief were, at death, buried west of the Jian; the sites had already been designated.

sentences.zh: 」此詔藏之宗廟，副在尚書、祕書三府，明帝亦遵奉之。

translations.literal: " This edict was stored in the ancestral temple, with copies in the three offices of the Masters of Writing and the Secretariat; Emperor Ming also followed and observed it.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict was kept in the ancestral temple, with copies in the Masters of Writing and Secretariat offices; Emperor Ming likewise obeyed it.

sentences.zh: 明帝性雖崇奢，然未遽營陵墓也。

translations.literal: Though Emperor Ming's nature inclined to luxury, he did not hasten to build his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming loved display, yet he did not rush to build his tomb.

sentences.zh: 晉宣帝豫自於首陽山為土藏，不墳不樹，作顧命終制，斂以時服，不設明器。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Jin prepared in advance an earthen burial on Mount Shouyang, with no mound and no trees; he made a testamentary final instruction, enshrouding in seasonal dress and setting out no mingqi.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's Emperor Xuan prepared ahead of time an earthen burial on Mount Shouyang—no mound, no trees—with a testament ordering seasonal dress and no mingqi.

sentences.zh: 文、景皆謹奉成命，無所加焉。

translations.literal: Emperors Wen and Jing both reverently followed the completed command, adding nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Wen and Jing both strictly kept the command without addition.

sentences.zh: 景帝崩，喪事制度，又依宣帝故事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing died, the mourning regulations again followed Emperor Xuan's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Jing's death, funeral arrangements again followed Emperor Xuan's precedent.

sentences.zh: 武帝泰始四年，文明王皇后崩，將合葬，開崇陽陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi, Empress Wang of the Civilized era died; they were to be buried together, and Chongyang Tomb was opened.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi year four, Empress Wang of the Civilized era died; for joint burial Chongyang Tomb was opened.

sentences.zh: 使太尉司馬望奉祭，進皇帝蜜璽綬於便房神坐。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant Sima Wang was sent to perform the sacrifice and present the imperial honey seal and cord at the spirit seat in the side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Sima Wang was sent to sacrifice and present the imperial honey seal and cord at the spirit seat in the side chamber.

sentences.zh: 魏氏金璽，此又儉矣。

translations.literal: The golden seal of Wei—this was frugality again.
translations.idiomatic: Even Wei's golden seal—here was austerity once more.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年，詔曰：「昔舜葬蒼梧，農不易畝；

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi an edict said: "In antiquity Shun was buried at Cangwu, yet farmers did not change their fields;
translations.idiomatic: A Taishi year two edict read: "When Shun was buried at Cangwu, farmers did not change their fields;

sentences.zh: 禹葬會稽，巿不改肆。

translations.literal: Yu was buried at Kuaiji, yet markets did not alter their stalls.
translations.idiomatic: when Yu was buried at Kuaiji, markets did not move their stalls.

sentences.zh: 上惟祖考清簡之旨，外欲移陵十里內居人，一切停之。

translations.literal: Inwardly I follow my ancestors' aim of simplicity; outwardly I wish to move the inhabitants within ten li of the tombs—all of this is stopped."
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly I honor my forebears' simplicity; outwardly I had wished to relocate residents within ten li of the tombs—all of that is halted."

sentences.zh: 」江左元、明崇儉，且百度草創，山陵奉終，省約備矣。

translations.literal: East of the Yangtze, Emperors Yuan and Ming honored frugality, and with a hundred offices still being founded, funeral and tomb arrangements were spare and complete.
translations.idiomatic: In the south, Yuan and Ming prized austerity; with institutions still being formed, tombs and funerals were kept spare.

sentences.zh: 成帝咸康七年，杜后崩。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng, Empress Du died.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiankang year seven under Emperor Cheng, Empress Du died.

sentences.zh: 詔外官五日一入臨，內官旦一入而已。

translations.literal: An edict ordered outer officials to attend mourning once every five days, inner officials only once each morning.
translations.idiomatic: Outer officials were to mourn once every five days; inner officials only once each morning.

sentences.zh: 過葬虞祭禮畢止。

translations.literal: After the burial, the yu sacrifice, and completion of the rites, this stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Attendance ceased once burial, the yu sacrifice, and the rites were complete.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「大行皇后陵所作凶門栢歷，門號顯陽端門。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: "For the late empress's tomb a mourning gate and cypress frame are being made, with the gate named Xianyang Duangate."
translations.idiomatic: Offices reported: "For the late empress's tomb a mourning gate and cypress frame are under construction, the gate to be named Xianyang Duangate."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「門如所處，凶門栢歷，大為煩費，停之。

translations.literal: The edict said: "The gate may stand where proposed; the mourning gate and cypress frame are greatly wasteful—stop them."
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "Let the gate stand as proposed; the mourning gate and cypress frame are far too costly—halt them."

sentences.zh: 」案蔡謨說，以二瓦器盛死者之祭，繫於木表，裹以葦席，置於庭中近南，名為重。

translations.literal: According to Cai Mo's account, two earthenware vessels holding offerings for the dead were tied to a wooden pole, wrapped in reed matting,
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo explained that two pottery vessels of offerings for the dead were tied to a wooden pole, wrapped in reed matting,

sentences.zh: 今之凶門，是其遺象也。

translations.literal: placed in the courtyard near the south, and called a chong; today's mourning gate is the surviving form of this.
translations.idiomatic: and set in the courtyard toward the south—called a chong; today's mourning gate preserves that image.

sentences.zh: 禮，既虞而作主。

translations.literal: In ritual, after the yu sacrifice one makes a spirit tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual requires making a spirit tablet after the yu sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 今未葬，未有主，故以重當之。

translations.literal: Now, before burial, there is as yet no tablet; therefore the chong stands in its place.
translations.idiomatic: Before burial there is no tablet yet; hence the chong serves in its stead.

sentences.zh: 禮稱為主道，此其義也。

translations.literal: Ritual calls this "the way of the lord"—that is the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual terms this "the way of the lord"—that is the point.

sentences.zh: 范堅又曰：「凶門非古。

translations.literal: Fan Jian also said: "The mourning gate is not ancient.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Jian added: "The mourning gate is not ancient.

sentences.zh: 古有懸重，形似凶門。

translations.literal: In antiquity there was a suspended chong, resembling a mourning gate.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity had a suspended chong, which looked like a mourning gate.

sentences.zh: 後人出之門外以表喪，俗遂行之。

translations.literal: Later men moved it outside the gate to mark mourning, and custom carried it on.
translations.idiomatic: Later people set it outside the gate to mark mourning, and custom kept the practice.

sentences.zh: 薄帳，即古弔幕之類也。

translations.literal: The thin canopy is of the same kind as the ancient mourning screen."
translations.idiomatic: The thin mourning canopy belongs to the same class as the ancient mourning screen."

sentences.zh: 」是時又詔曰：「重壤之下，豈宜崇飾無用。

translations.literal: At that time another edict said: "Beneath the heavy earth, how can useless ornament be piled up?
translations.idiomatic: Another edict of the time said: "Beneath the heavy earth, how can useless ornament be heaped up?

sentences.zh: 陵中唯潔掃而已。

translations.literal: Within the tomb let there be only clean sweeping."
translations.idiomatic: Within the tomb let there be only clean sweeping."

sentences.zh: 」有司又奏依舊選公卿以下六品子弟六十人為挽郎。

translations.literal: The relevant offices again memorialized that, according to old practice, sixty youths of the sixth rank and below from among the sons of dukes and ministers should be chosen as pallbearers.
translations.idiomatic: Offices again proposed, per old custom, choosing sixty youths of sixth rank and below from officials' families as pallbearers.

sentences.zh: 詔又停之。

translations.literal: The edict again stopped this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict again halted it.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝太元四年九月，皇后王氏崩。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu, Empress Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Taiyuan year four under Emperor Xiaowu, Empress Wang died.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「終事唯從儉速。

translations.literal: The edict said: "The funeral should be only frugal and swift."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: "The funeral should be frugal and swift."

sentences.zh: 」又詔：「遠近不得遣山陵使。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Near and far must not dispatch tomb envoys."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict forbade dispatching tomb envoys from near or far.

sentences.zh: 」有司奏選挽郎二十四人。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized selecting twenty-four pallbearers.
translations.idiomatic: Offices proposed selecting twenty-four pallbearers.

sentences.zh: 詔停。

translations.literal: The edict stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict halted it.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉十七年，元皇后崩，詔亦停選挽郎。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen of Song, when the primary empress died, the edict likewise stopped selecting pallbearers.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year seventeen, when the primary empress of Song's Emperor Wen died, pallbearers were likewise not chosen.

sentences.zh: 漢儀五供畢則上陵，歲歲以為常。

translations.literal: Under Han ritual, when the five offerings were complete one ascended to the tomb; year by year this became constant.
translations.idiomatic: Han practice made ascending to the tomb after the five offerings an annual constant.

sentences.zh: 魏則無定禮。

translations.literal: Under Wei there was no fixed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had no fixed rule for it.

sentences.zh: 齊王在位九載，始一謁高平陵，而曹爽誅。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi, in nine years on the throne, visited Gaoping Tomb only once—and then Cao Shuang was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi, in nine years on the throne, visited Gaoping Tomb only once—then Cao Shuang was put to death.

sentences.zh: 其後遂廢，終魏世。

translations.literal: Thereafter it was abandoned, through the end of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: After that the practice lapsed for the rest of Wei.

sentences.zh: 晉宣帝遺詔：「子弟羣官，皆不得謁陵。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Jin left in his testament: "Sons, younger brothers, and officials—all must not visit the tombs."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Jin's testament ordered: "Sons, younger brothers, and officials must not visit the tombs."

sentences.zh: 」於是景、文遵旨。

translations.literal: Thereupon Emperors Jing and Wen followed the command.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Jing and Wen obeyed.

sentences.zh: 至武帝猶再謁崇陽陵，一謁峻平陵，然遂不敢謁高原陵。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wu there were still two visits to Chongyang Tomb and one to Junping Tomb, yet he did not dare visit Gaoyuan Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu still visited Chongyang Tomb twice and Junping Tomb once, but did not dare visit Gaoyuan Tomb.

sentences.zh: 至惠帝復止也。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Hui it stopped again.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Hui it ceased again.

sentences.zh: 逮江左初，元帝崩後，諸公始有謁陵辭陵之事，蓋由眷同友執，率情而舉，非洛京之舊也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the east-of-the-Yangtze court, after Emperor Yuan's death the great officials first had the practice of visiting and taking leave at the tombs—likely from affection like that between friends, undertaken from feeling rather than from the old Luoyang custom.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the southern court, after Emperor Yuan's death officials began tomb visits and leave-taking—born of personal affection, not Luoyang precedent.

sentences.zh: 成帝時，中宮亦年年拜陵，議者以為非禮，於是遂止，以為永制。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Cheng the inner palace also paid annual tomb visits; critics held this unritual, and so it was stopped as a permanent rule.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng the inner palace too visited tombs yearly; critics called it unritual, and it was stopped as permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 至穆帝時，褚太后臨朝，又拜陵，帝幼故也。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Mu, when Empress Dowager Chu held court, tomb visits resumed—the emperor was young.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mu, Empress Dowager Chu as regent resumed tomb visits—the emperor was still a child.

sentences.zh: 至孝武崩，驃騎將軍司馬道子命曰：「今雖權制釋服，至於朔望諸節，自應展情陵所，以一周為斷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu died, the General of Agile Cavalry Sima Daozi ordered: "Though the provisional rule now releases mourning dress, for the new and full moon and the seasonal festivals feeling should still be shown at the tombs, with one week as the limit."
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Xiaowu's death, Sima Daozi ordered: "Though provisional rule ends mourning dress, new and full moons and festivals should still be observed at the tombs, for one week at a time."

sentences.zh: 」於是至陵變服單衣𢂿，煩瀆無準，非禮意也。

translations.literal: Thereupon at the tomb they changed dress to plain single garments and mourning trousers, with repeated profanation and no standard—contrary to ritual intent.
translations.idiomatic: At the tombs they then wore plain single garments and mourning trousers, with repeated visits and no standard—contrary to ritual.

sentences.zh: 至安帝元興元年，尚書左僕射桓謙奏曰：「百僚拜陵，起於中興，非晉舊典。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxing under Emperor An, the Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Huan Qian memorialized: "Officials' tomb visits began in the Restoration—this is not Jin's old canon.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanxing year one under Emperor An, Huan Qian memorialized: "Officials' tomb visits began in the Restoration—not Jin's old canon.

sentences.zh: 積習生常，遂為近法。

translations.literal: Long habit became custom and turned into recent law.
translations.idiomatic: Long habit became custom and passed for recent law.

sentences.zh: 尋武皇帝詔，乃不使人主諸王拜陵，豈唯百僚。

translations.literal: Search the edict of Emperor Wu: he would not have the ruler, princes, and kings visit tombs—how much less the hundred officials alone.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's edict forbade the ruler and imperial princes from visiting tombs—how much less the hundred officials alone.

sentences.zh: 謂宜遵奉。

translations.literal: I hold that we should follow and observe this."
translations.idiomatic: We should follow and observe it."

sentences.zh: 」於是施行。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon it was enforced.

sentences.zh: 及義熙初，又復江左之舊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yixi the old east-of-the-Yangtze practice was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yixi the old southern practice returned.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝又斷羣臣初拜謁陵，而辭如故。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song again cut officials' initial tomb visits and leave-taking, while farewell visits remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Song again barred officials' initial tomb visits, while farewell visits remained.

sentences.zh: 自元嘉以來，每歲正月，輿駕必謁初寧陵，復漢儀也。

translations.literal: From Yuanjia onward, every first month the imperial carriage necessarily visited Chuning Tomb—restoring Han practice.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuanjia on, each first month the imperial carriage visited Chuning Tomb—restoring Han practice.

sentences.zh: 世祖、太宗亦每歲拜初寧、長寧陵。

translations.literal: Emperors Shizu and Taizong also visited Chuning and Changning tombs every year.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Shizu and Taizong likewise visited Chuning and Changning tombs yearly.

sentences.zh: 漢以後，天下送死奢靡，多作石室石獸碑銘等物。

translations.literal: From Han onward, funeral display across the realm grew extravagant; many made stone chambers, stone beasts, steles, and inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: After Han, funerary display grew extravagant—stone chambers, stone beasts, steles, and inscriptions multiplied.

sentences.zh: 建安十年，魏武帝以天下雕弊，下令不得厚葬，又禁立碑。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jian'an, Emperor Wu of Wei, because the realm was worn and impoverished, ordered that thick burial not be permitted and also forbade erecting steles.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an year ten, with the realm exhausted, Cao Cao forbade lavish burial and the erection of steles.

sentences.zh: 魏高貴鄉公甘露二年，大將軍參軍太原王倫卒，倫兄俊作表德論，以述倫遺美，云「祗畏王典，不得為銘，乃撰錄行事，就刊於墓之陰云爾」。

translations.literal: In the second year of Ganlu under the Noble Village Duke of Wei, Wang Lun, a staff officer of the Grand General from Taiyuan, died; Lun's elder brother Jun composed a eulogy of virtue to recount Lun's fine deeds, saying, "In reverent awe of the royal canon I may not make an inscription; I have therefore compiled his conduct and will publish it on the yin side of the tomb—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: In Ganlu year two of Wei, staff officer Wang Lun of Taiyuan died; his brother Jun wrote a virtue eulogy, saying he dared not make an inscription per the royal ban but would record Lun's conduct on the tomb's shaded side.

sentences.zh: 此則碑禁尚嚴也。

translations.literal: This shows the stele ban was still strict.
translations.idiomatic: This shows the stele ban was still strict.

sentences.zh: 此後復弛替。

translations.literal: Thereafter it lapsed again.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter it slackened again.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝咸寧四年，又詔曰：「此石獸碑表，既私褒美，興長虛偽，傷財害人，莫大於此。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianning under Emperor Wu of Jin, another edict said: "These stone beasts and stele tables, being private praise, foster vain falsehood, harm goods and injure people—nothing is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianning year four, Emperor Wu of Jin edicted: "Stone beasts and stele tables, as private praise, breed vanity, waste wealth, and harm people—nothing worse.

sentences.zh: 一禁斷之。

translations.literal: Let them be wholly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Let them be wholly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 其犯者雖會赦令，皆當毀壞。

translations.literal: Even if an offender is covered by an amnesty, the objects must still be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: Even offenders covered by amnesty must have them destroyed."

sentences.zh: 」至元帝太興元年，有司奏：「故驃騎府主簿故恩營葬舊君顧榮，求立碑。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan, the relevant offices memorialized: "The former chief clerk of the General of Agile Cavalry's bureau, in gratitude for his former lord Gu Rong, seeks to erect a stele for his burial."
translations.idiomatic: In Taixing year one, offices reported: "The former chief clerk of the General of Agile Cavalry, burying his lord Gu Rong, seeks leave to erect a stele."

sentences.zh: 」詔特聽立。

translations.literal: The edict specially permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict specially allowed it.

sentences.zh: 自是後，禁又漸頹。

translations.literal: From this time onward the ban gradually collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: From then the ban gradually collapsed.

sentences.zh: 大臣長吏，人皆私立。

translations.literal: Great ministers and chief local officers all set up private ones.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers and chief local officers all erected private steles.

sentences.zh: 義熙中，尚書祠部郎中裴松之又議禁斷，於是至今。

translations.literal: In the Yixi period, Pei Songzhi of the Masters of Writing's Sacrificial Affairs Bureau again proposed forbidding them; from then to the present.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi, Pei Songzhi of the Sacrificial Affairs Bureau again proposed a ban—and it has held since.

sentences.zh: 順帝昇明三年四月壬辰，御臨軒，遣使奉璽綬禪位於齊王，懸而不樂。

translations.literal: On the renchen day of the fourth month of the third year of Shengming under Emperor Shun, he faced the hall, sent envoys to present the seal and cord and abdicate to the Prince of Qi, and suspended music without performing it.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen of the fourth month, Shengming year three, Emperor Shun faced the hall, sent envoys with seal and cord to abdicate to the Prince of Qi, and hung up music unperformed.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝泰始二年九月，有司奏：「皇太子所生陳貴妃禮秩既同儲宮，未詳宮臣及朝臣並有敬不？

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Taishi under Emperor Ming of Song, the relevant offices memorialized: "The birth mother of the crown prince, Honored Consort Chen, now shares the crown prince's ritual rank; it is unclear whether palace officials and court officials should all show respect?"
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi year two, month nine, offices asked: "Honored Consort Chen, the crown prince's birth mother, now ranks with the heir—should palace and court officials all show respect?"

sentences.zh: 妃主在內相見，又應何儀？

translations.literal: When the consort and the mistress of the inner quarters meet within, what ceremony should apply?"
translations.idiomatic: When consort and palace mistress meet within, what ceremony applies?"

sentences.zh: 」博士王慶緒議：「百僚內外禮敬貴妃，應與皇太子同。

translations.literal: " The Erudite Wang Qingxu proposed: "Within and without, officials should show ritual respect to the honored consort as to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: " Erudite Wang Qingxu held: "Officials inside and out should respect the honored consort as they do the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 其東朝臣隸，理歸臣節。

translations.literal: The eastern-palace retainers, by principle, belong to the subject's station."
translations.idiomatic: Eastern-palace retainers, by principle, stand in subject relation."

sentences.zh: 」太常丞虞愿等同慶緒。

translations.literal: " The Assistant Director of the Grand Impartial Sacrifices Yu Yuan and others agreed with Qingxu.
translations.idiomatic: " Assistant Director Yu Yuan and others agreed with Qingxu.

sentences.zh: 尚書令建安王休仁議稱：「禮云，妾既不得體君，班秩視子為序。

translations.literal: The Director of the Masters of Writing, the Prince of Jian'an Wang Xiuren, argued, saying: "Ritual says a concubine cannot embody the lord; rank and precedence follow the son in order.
translations.idiomatic: Director Wang Xiuren of Jian'an argued: "Ritual says a concubine cannot embody the lord; rank and precedence follow the son in order.

sentences.zh: 母以子貴，經著明文。

translations.literal: The mother is ennobled through the son—this is set forth plainly in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: When a mother is ennobled through her son, the canonical texts state it in plain terms.

sentences.zh: 內外致敬貴妃，誠如慶緒議。

translations.literal: That inner and outer circles should show reverence to the Honored Consort is indeed as Qingxu argued.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer officials ought to pay homage to the Honored Consort, just as Wang Qingxu proposed.

sentences.zh: 天子姬嬪，不容通音介於外，雖義可致虔，不應有牋表。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's consorts may not exchange messages with the outside; though reverence may be shown in principle, they should not submit memorials or letters.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial consorts must not communicate with the outside world; even where devotion might warrant contact, they should not send memorials or formal letters.

sentences.zh: 」參詳休仁議為允。

translations.literal: On full review, Xiu Ren's opinion was approved.
translations.idiomatic: After joint review, Xiu Ren's opinion was adopted.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 泰豫元年，後廢帝即位，崇所生陳貴妃為皇太妃。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiyu, when the deposed emperor succeeded, he honored his birth mother, Honored Consort Chen, as Imperial Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiyu (473), the deposed emperor took the throne and elevated his birth mother, Honored Consort Chen, to Imperial Grand Consort.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「皇太妃位亞尊極，未詳國親舉哀格當一同皇太后？

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: "The Imperial Grand Consort's rank is next below the supreme dignity; it is unclear whether imperial kin should observe mourning for her on the same scale as for the Empress Dowager—
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices submitted: "The Imperial Grand Consort stands just below the highest dignity. Should imperial relatives mourn her on the same footing as the Empress Dowager?

sentences.zh: 為有降異？

translations.literal: —or should there be a reduced grade?
translations.idiomatic: Or should mourning be scaled down?

sentences.zh: 又於本親朞以下，當猶服與不？

translations.literal: Moreover, for her own kin within one-year mourning, should she still wear mourning or not?"
translations.idiomatic: And for her own relatives within the one-year mourning circle, should she still wear mourning dress?"

sentences.zh: 」前曹郎王燮之議：「案喪服傳，『妾服君之黨，得與女君同』。

translations.literal: Former Bureau of Appointments clerk Wang Xiezhi argued: "According to the Mourning Dress Commentary, 'A concubine wears mourning for the lord's kin group and may do so on the same footing as the principal wife.'"
translations.idiomatic: Former Bureau of Appointments clerk Wang Xiezhi argued: "The Mourning Dress Commentary says, 'A concubine mourns the lord's kin group and may match the principal wife.'"

sentences.zh: 如此，皇太妃服宗與太后無異。

translations.literal: On this basis, the Grand Consort's mourning for the imperial clan would be no different from the Empress Dowager's.
translations.idiomatic: On that reading, the Grand Consort's mourning obligations toward the imperial clan would match the Empress Dowager's.

sentences.zh: 但太后既以尊降無服，太妃儀不應殊，故悉不服也。

translations.literal: But the Empress Dowager, because her rank was supreme, was exempt from mourning; the Grand Consort's rites should not differ; therefore she wore none at all.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because the Empress Dowager's supreme rank released her from mourning obligation, the Grand Consort's protocol should not differ—so she wore no mourning at all.

sentences.zh: 計本情舉哀，其禮不異。

translations.literal: As for performing mourning from genuine feeling, the rite would be the same.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to expressing grief from genuine feeling, the ritual would not differ.

sentences.zh: 又禮，『諸侯絕朞』。

translations.literal: Moreover, in ritual, "Feudal lords cut off one-year mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Ritual also states that "feudal lords terminate one-year mourning."

sentences.zh: 皇太妃雖云不居尊極，不容輕於諸侯。

translations.literal: Though the Imperial Grand Consort does not occupy the supreme pole, she cannot be treated more lightly than a feudal lord.
translations.idiomatic: Although the Imperial Grand Consort does not hold the highest dignity, she cannot be ranked below a feudal lord.

sentences.zh: 謂本親朞以下，一無所服。

translations.literal: It follows that for her own kin within one-year mourning, she wore nothing at all.
translations.idiomatic: For her own kin within the one-year mourning circle, she would wear no mourning dress at all.

sentences.zh: 有慘自宜舉哀。

translations.literal: When grief struck, she should still perform mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When personal bereavement struck, she should still express mourning.

sentences.zh: 親疏二儀，準之太后。

translations.literal: The two protocols for close and distant kin should follow the Empress Dowager's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The two protocols—close kin and distant kin—should follow the Empress Dowager's model.

sentences.zh: 」兼太常丞司馬燮之議：「禮，『妾服君之庶子及女君之黨』。

translations.literal: Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies aide Sima Xiezhi argued: "In ritual, 'A concubine wears mourning for the lord's sons by other women and for the principal wife's kin.'"
translations.idiomatic: Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies aide Sima Xiezhi argued: "Ritual states, 'A concubine mourns the lord's sons by other women and the principal wife's kin.'"

sentences.zh: 皆謂大夫士耳。

translations.literal: This refers only to grand masters and officers.
translations.idiomatic: This applies only to grand masters and officers.

sentences.zh: 妾名雖總，而班有貴賤。

translations.literal: Though the name "concubine" is general, ranks divide noble from base.
translations.idiomatic: Though all are called "concubines," their ranks divide high from low.

sentences.zh: 三夫人九嬪，位視公卿。

translations.literal: The Three Ladies and Nine Concubines rank with dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Ladies and Nine Concubines held ranks comparable to dukes and ministers.

sentences.zh: 大夫猶有貴妾，而況天子。

translations.literal: Even a grand master may have a honored concubine—how much more the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Even grand masters could have honored concubines—how much more the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 諸侯之妾為他妾之子無服，既不服他妾之子，豈容服君及女君餘親。

translations.literal: A feudal lord's concubine wears no mourning for another concubine's son; having no mourning for another concubine's son, how could she wear mourning for the lord and the principal wife's remaining kin?
translations.idiomatic: A feudal lord's concubine did not mourn another concubine's son; if she did not mourn another concubine's son, how could she mourn the lord or the principal wife's other kin?

sentences.zh: 況皇太后妃貴亞相極，禮絕羣后，崇輝盛典，有踰東儲，尚不服朞，太妃豈應有異。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Empress Dowager and Honored Consort stand next to the supreme pole; ritual cuts them off from the empresses; their splendid ceremony even surpasses the Eastern Heir—yet they still do not wear one-year mourning; how could the Grand Consort differ?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Empress Dowager and Honored Consort stood next to the throne; ritual set them apart from other consorts; their splendid rites even outranked the Eastern Heir—yet they still wore no one-year mourning. How could the Grand Consort be treated differently?

sentences.zh: 若本親有慘，舉哀之儀，宜仰則太后。

translations.literal: If her own kin suffered bereavement, the mourning rite should follow the Empress Dowager's example.
translations.idiomatic: When her own kin suffered bereavement, the mourning rite should follow the Empress Dowager's precedent.

sentences.zh: 」參議以燮之議為允。

translations.literal: On joint review, Xiezhi's opinion was approved.
translations.idiomatic: After joint deliberation, Xiezhi's opinion was adopted.

sentences.zh: 太妃於國親無服，故宜緣情為諸王公主於至尊是朞服者反，其太妃王妃三夫人九嬪各舉哀。

translations.literal: The Grand Consort wore no mourning for imperial kin; accordingly, on grounds of feeling, princes and princesses who would wear one-year mourning for the Sovereign should be excused, while the Grand Consort, princess consorts, the Three Ladies, and the Nine Concubines should each perform mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Grand Consort owed no mourning dress to imperial kin, the court should let affection govern the case: princes and princesses who would ordinarily mourn the emperor for a year should be released from that duty, while the Grand Consort, royal consorts, the Three Ladies, and the Nine Concubines should each perform mourning as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武帝孝建三年八月戊子，有司奏：「雲杜國解稱國子檀和之所生親王，求除太夫人。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, eighth month of the third year of Xiaojian of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, the relevant offices memorialized: "The state of Yundu reports that the birth mother of the state heir Tan Hezhi, a royal consort, seeks appointment as Grand Lady."
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day in the eighth month of the third year of Xiaojian (456), the relevant offices reported that the state of Yundu asked to ennoble the birth mother of its heir, Tan Hezhi, as Grand Lady.

sentences.zh: 檢無國子除太夫人先例，法又無科。

translations.literal: No precedent was found for a state heir ennobling his mother as Grand Lady, nor is there a statute for it.
translations.idiomatic: No precedent could be found for a state heir elevating his mother to Grand Lady, and no statute covered the case.

sentences.zh: 下禮官議正。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the ritual officers for decision.
translations.idiomatic: The case was sent to the ritual officers for a ruling.

sentences.zh: 」太學博士孫豁之議：「春秋，『母以子貴』。

translations.literal: Grand Academy erudite Sun Huozhi argued: "In the Spring and Autumn Annals, 'The mother is ennobled through the son.'"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Academy erudite Sun Huozhi argued: "The Spring and Autumn Annals says, 'The mother is ennobled through the son.'"

sentences.zh: 王雖為妾，是和之所生。

translations.literal: Though the prince was born of a concubine, he was born of Hezhi.
translations.idiomatic: Though the prince's mother was a concubine, she was Hezhi's birth mother.

sentences.zh: 案五等之例，鄭伯許男同號夫人，國子體例，王合如國所生。

translations.literal: By the precedent of the five ranks, the Earl of Zheng and the Baron of Xu alike styled their wives "Lady"; by the protocol for a state heir, a prince should match a state's birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: Under the five-rank precedent, the Earl of Zheng and Baron of Xu alike called their wives "Lady"; by the protocol for state heirs, a prince should follow the same rule as a feudatory state's birth mother.

sentences.zh: 」太常丞庾蔚之議：「『母以子貴』，雖春秋明義，古今異制，因革不同。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies aide Yu Weizhi argued: "'The mother is ennobled through the son' is a clear principle of the Spring and Autumn, but ancient and modern institutions differ and reforms are not the same."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Ceremonies aide Yu Weizhi argued: "'The mother is ennobled through the son' is clear Spring and Autumn doctrine, but institutions differ across ages and reforms do not match."

sentences.zh: 自頃代以來，所生蒙榮，唯有諸王。

translations.literal: In recent generations, birth mothers honored with glory have been only those of princes.
translations.idiomatic: In recent generations, only princes' birth mothers had been honored in this way.

sentences.zh: 既是王者之嬪御，故宜見尊於蕃國。

translations.literal: Since they were consorts of a king, they should receive honor in the feudatory state.
translations.idiomatic: As consorts of a prince, they ought to be honored within the feudatory domain.

sentences.zh: 若功高勳重，列為公侯，亦有拜太夫人之禮。

translations.literal: If merit was high and achievement weighty, and one was enfeoffed as duke or marquis, there was also the rite of appointing a Grand Lady.
translations.idiomatic: When merit was great enough to merit enfeoffment as duke or marquis, there was also the rite of appointing a Grand Lady.

sentences.zh: 凡此皆朝恩曲降，非國之所求。

translations.literal: All these were gracious reductions from the court, not requests of the state itself.
translations.idiomatic: All such cases were gracious favors from the court, not requests initiated by the feudatory state.

sentences.zh: 子男妾母，未有前比。

translations.literal: For the concubine-mother of a viscount or baron, there was no earlier parallel.
translations.idiomatic: No earlier parallel existed for ennobling the concubine-mother of a viscount or baron.

sentences.zh: 」祠部郎中朱膺之議以為：「子不得爵父母，而春秋有『母以子貴』。

translations.literal: Director of the Sacrificial Affairs Bureau Zhu Yingzhi argued: "A son may not ennoble his parents, yet the Spring and Autumn has 'The mother is ennobled through the son.'"
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Sacrificial Affairs Bureau Zhu Yingzhi argued: "Sons may not ennoble their parents, yet the Spring and Autumn says, 'The mother is ennobled through the son.'"

sentences.zh: 當謂傳國嗣君母，本先公嬪媵，所因藉有由故也。

translations.literal: This must mean the mother of the heir who receives the state succession, who was originally a concubine or attendant of the former lord—there is a reason rooted in the succession.
translations.idiomatic: This must refer to the mother of the heir who receives state succession—originally a concubine or attendant of the former lord—where the succession itself supplies the grounds.

sentences.zh: 始封之身，所不得同。

translations.literal: One who is first enfeoffed cannot be treated the same.
translations.idiomatic: Someone receiving a first enfeoffment could not be treated the same way.

sentences.zh: 若殊績重勳，恩所特錫，時或有之，不由司存。

translations.literal: If achievement was exceptional and merit weighty, the grace might be specially bestowed; this happened at times and did not come from the relevant office.
translations.idiomatic: When achievement was extraordinary, the court might grant the honor as a special favor; this occurred from time to time and was not a matter for the ritual offices to decide on their own.

sentences.zh: 」所議參議，以蔚之為允。

translations.literal: On joint review of the opinions, Weizhi's was approved.
translations.idiomatic: After joint review, Weizhi's opinion was adopted.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 大明二年六月，有司奏：「凡侯伯子男世子喪，無嗣，求進次息為世子。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Daming, the relevant offices memorialized: "Whenever a marquis, earl, viscount, or baron's heir apparent dies without issue, they seek to advance the second son as heir apparent."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Daming (458), the relevant offices reported that whenever a feudal heir died without issue, the family sought to advance the second son as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 檢無其例，下禮官議正。

translations.literal: No precedent was found; the matter was referred to the ritual officers for decision.
translations.idiomatic: No precedent could be found, and the case was sent to the ritual officers for a ruling.

sentences.zh: 」博士孫武議：「案晉濟北侯荀勗長子連卒，以次子輯拜世子。

translations.literal: Erudite Sun Wu argued: "According to the Jin case, when Lian, eldest son of Marquis Xun of Jibei, died, the second son Ji was appointed heir apparent."
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Sun Wu argued: "In Jin, when Lian, eldest son of Marquis Xun of Jibei, died, the second son Ji was appointed heir apparent."

sentences.zh: 先代成準，宜為今例。
