translations.literal: A precedent of the previous age—fit to serve as today's rule.
translations.idiomatic: That earlier precedent should serve as the rule for today.

sentences.zh: 」博士傅郁議：「禮記，微子立衍，商禮斯行。

translations.literal: Erudite Fu Yu argued: "In the Record of Rites, Weizi established Yan and the ritual of Shang was carried out."
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Fu Yu argued: "The Record of Rites says that when Weizi established Yan, the ritual of Shang was carried out."

sentences.zh: 仲子舍孫，姬典攸貶。

translations.literal: When Zhongzi set aside his grandson, the Zhou canon censured it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzi passed over his grandson, the Zhou canon condemned it.

sentences.zh: 歷代遵循，靡替于舊。

translations.literal: Successive generations followed this without change from old custom.
translations.idiomatic: Successive generations had followed this without departing from ancient custom.

sentences.zh: 今胙土之君在而世子卒，厥嗣未育，非捨孫之謂。

translations.literal: Now the lord who holds enfeoffed land is alive while the heir apparent dies and his line has not yet produced a son—this is not a case of setting aside a grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Today the enfeoffed lord still lives while the heir apparent dies without a son of his own—this is not the case of setting aside a grandson.

sentences.zh: 愚以為次子有子，自宜紹為世孫。

translations.literal: I hold that if the second son has a son, that son should naturally succeed as heir grandson.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that if the second son already has a son, that grandson should naturally succeed as heir grandson.

sentences.zh: 若其未也，無容遠搜輕屬，承綱繼體，傳之有由。

translations.literal: If he has not yet, one cannot far-seek a light kinship to receive the succession and continue the line—transmission must have a proper basis.
translations.idiomatic: If he has no son yet, one cannot search far among remote kin to carry on the succession; transmission must have a proper basis.

sentences.zh: 父在立子，允稱情典。

translations.literal: Establishing a son while the father lives aptly matches the emotional norm.
translations.idiomatic: Appointing an heir while the father still lives aptly matches ritual feeling.

sentences.zh: 」曹郎諸葛雅之議：「案春秋傳云，『世子死，有母弟則立之，無則立長，年均擇賢，義均則卜』。

translations.literal: Bureau clerk Zhuge Yazhi argued: "The Zuo Commentary says, 'When the heir apparent dies, if there is a younger brother by the same mother, establish him; if not, establish the eldest; if ages are equal, choose the worthy; if worth is equal, divine.'"
translations.idiomatic: Bureau clerk Zhuge Yazhi argued: "The Zuo Commentary says, 'When the heir apparent dies, if there is a younger brother of the same mother, establish him; if not, establish the eldest; if ages are equal, choose the worthy; if worth is equal, divine.'"

sentences.zh: 古之制也。

translations.literal: This was the ancient rule.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the ancient institution.

sentences.zh: 今長子早卒，無嗣，進立次息以為世子，取諸左氏，理義無違。

translations.literal: Now the eldest son died early without issue; advancing the second son as heir apparent, taking this from the Zuo Commentary, accords with reason and right.
translations.idiomatic: Now the eldest son died young without issue; advancing the second son as heir apparent, following the Zuo Commentary, accords with reason and right.

sentences.zh: 又孫武所據晉濟北侯荀勗長子卒，立次子，亦近代成例。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Jin case Sun Wu cited—when the eldest son of Marquis Xun of Jibei died, the second son was established—is also a recent precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wu also cited the recent Jin precedent in which, when Marquis Xun of Jibei's eldest son died, the second son was established.

sentences.zh: 依文採比，竊所允安。

translations.literal: Comparing texts and weighing them, I privately find it acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing the texts, I find the solution acceptable.

sentences.zh: 謂宜開許，以為永制。

translations.literal: It should be opened and permitted, to serve as a permanent rule.
translations.idiomatic: The practice should be authorized and made a permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 」參議為允。

translations.literal: On joint review, approval was given.
translations.idiomatic: After joint review, the proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 大明十二年十一月，有司奏：「興平國解稱國子袁愍孫母王氏，應除太夫人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the twelfth year of Daming, the relevant offices memorialized: "The state of Xingping reports that the mother of the state heir Yuan Minsun, Lady Wang, should be appointed Grand Lady."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the twelfth year of Daming (468), the relevant offices reported that the state of Xingping asked to appoint the mother of its heir, Yuan Minsun, Lady Wang, as Grand Lady.

sentences.zh: 檢無國子除太夫人例。

translations.literal: No precedent was found for a state heir appointing a Grand Lady.
translations.idiomatic: No precedent could be found for a state heir elevating his mother to Grand Lady.

sentences.zh: 下禮官議正。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the ritual officers for decision.
translations.idiomatic: The case was sent to the ritual officers for a ruling.

sentences.zh: 」太學博士司馬興之議：「案禮，下國卿大夫之妻，皆命天子。

translations.literal: Grand Academy erudite Sima Xingzhi argued: "According to ritual, the wives of ministers in subordinate states were all appointed by the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Academy erudite Sima Xingzhi argued: "Ritual holds that the wives of ministers in subordinate states were all appointed by the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 以斯而推，則子男之母，不容獨異。

translations.literal: By this reasoning, the mother of a viscount or baron cannot be treated as a separate exception.
translations.idiomatic: By that reasoning, the mother of a viscount or baron could not be treated as a separate exception.

sentences.zh: 」博士程彥議以為：「五等雖差，而承家事等。

translations.literal: Erudite Cheng Yan argued: "Though the five ranks differ, they equally inherit the family charge."
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Cheng Yan argued: "Though the five ranks differed, they equally bore the family charge."

sentences.zh: 公侯之母，崇號得從，子男於親，尊秩宜顯。

translations.literal: The mothers of dukes and marquises could receive honored titles; for viscounts and barons, kinship rank should also be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and marquises could honor their mothers with exalted titles; for viscounts and barons, kinship rank should likewise be displayed.

sentences.zh: 故春秋之義，『母以子貴』。

translations.literal: Hence the meaning of the Spring and Autumn: "The mother is ennobled through the son."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Spring and Autumn principle: "The mother is ennobled through the son."

sentences.zh: 固知從子尊與國均也。

translations.literal: One clearly knows that honor through the son equals honor of the state.
translations.idiomatic: From this it is clear that honor gained through the son equals honor of the state itself.

sentences.zh: 彥參議，以興之議為允。

translations.literal: Yan, on joint review, approved Xingzhi's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: On joint review, Yan adopted Xingzhi's opinion.

sentences.zh: 除王氏為興平縣開國子太夫人。

translations.literal: Lady Wang was appointed Grand Lady of the Baron of Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang was appointed Grand Lady of the Baron of Xingping county.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 大明四年九月，有司奏：「陳留國王曹虔秀長兄虔嗣早卒，秀襲封之後，生子銑以繼虔嗣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Daming, the relevant offices memorialized: "King Cao Qianxiu of Chenliu's elder brother Qian Si died early; after Qianxiu succeeded to the fief, he bore a son Miao to continue Qian Si's line."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Daming (460), the relevant offices reported that King Cao Qianxiu of Chenliu's elder brother Qian Si had died early; after Qianxiu inherited the fief, he fathered a son Miao to continue Qian Si's line.

sentences.zh: 今依例應拜世子，未詳應以銑為世子？

translations.literal: Now, by rule, an heir apparent should be appointed; it is unclear whether Miao should be made heir apparent—
translations.idiomatic: By statute an heir apparent should now be appointed; it was unclear whether Miao should be named heir apparent—

sentences.zh: 為應立次子鍇？

translations.literal: —or whether the second son Kai should be established?
translations.idiomatic: —or whether the second son Kai should be established instead?

sentences.zh: 」太學博士王溫之、江長議，並為應以銑為正嗣。

translations.literal: Grand Academy erudites Wang Wenzhi and Jiang Chang both held that Miao should be the legitimate successor.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Academy erudites Wang Wenzhi and Jiang Chang both held that Miao should be the legitimate heir.

sentences.zh: 太常陸澄議立鍇。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Ceremonies Lu Cheng argued for establishing Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Ceremonies Lu Cheng argued for establishing Kai.

sentences.zh: 右丞徐爰議謂：「禮後大宗，以其不可乏祀。

translations.literal: Right Assistant Director Xu Yuan argued: "Ritual honors the great descent line because sacrifice cannot be left without a recipient."
translations.idiomatic: Right Assistant Director Xu Yuan argued: "Ritual honors the great descent line because sacrifice cannot be left without a recipient."

sentences.zh: 諸侯世及，春秋成義。

translations.literal: Feudal lords succeed by generation—this is the established meaning of the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal succession by generation was the established meaning of the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 虔嗣承家傳爵，身為國王，雖薨沒無子，猶列昭穆。

translations.literal: Qian Si inherited the family and transmitted the fief; he was king in his own person; though he died without a son, he still stands in the ancestral tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Si inherited the house and transmitted the fief; he had been king in his own person; though he died without a son, he still stood in the ancestral tablets.

sentences.zh: 立後之日，便應即纂國統。

translations.literal: On the day an heir was established, he should at once have succeeded to the state line.
translations.idiomatic: On the day an heir was established, he should at once have succeeded to the state line.

sentences.zh: 于時既無承繼，虔秀以次襲紹。

translations.literal: At that time there was no successor; Qianxiu succeeded in order of seniority.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was no successor, so Qianxiu succeeded by order of seniority.

sentences.zh: 虔嗣既列廟饗，故自與世數而遷。

translations.literal: Since Qian Si was already enrolled in ancestral offerings, he naturally shifted with the generational count.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qian Si was already enrolled in ancestral offerings, he naturally shifted with the generational sequence.

sentences.zh: 豈容蒸嘗無闕，橫取他子為嗣。

translations.literal: How could seasonal sacrifices be left without a recipient while another man's son was seized as successor?
translations.idiomatic: How could seasonal sacrifices be left without a recipient while another man's son was seized as heir?

sentences.zh: 為人胤嗣，又應恭祀先父。

translations.literal: As someone's adopted heir, he should also respectfully sacrifice to his natural father.
translations.idiomatic: As an adopted heir, he should also respectfully sacrifice to his natural father.

sentences.zh: 案禮文，公子不得禰諸侯。

translations.literal: According to the ritual texts, a lord's son may not treat his father as an enfeoffed lord in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: According to ritual texts, a lord's son may not treat his father as an enfeoffed lord in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 虔嗣無緣降廟就寢。

translations.literal: Qian Si had no grounds to descend in the temple and take the lower place.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Si had no grounds to descend in the temple and take the lower place.

sentences.zh: 銑本長息，宜還為虔秀世子。

translations.literal: Miao was originally the eldest son; he should be restored as Qianxiu's heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Miao was originally the eldest son; he should be restored as Qianxiu's heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 」詔如爰議。

translations.literal: The edict followed Yuan's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed Xu Yuan's opinion.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉十三年七月，有司奏：「御史中丞劉式之議，『每至出行，未知制與何官分道，應有舊科。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the thirteenth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, the relevant offices memorialized: "Censor-in-Chief Liu Shizhi argued, 'Whenever the emperor goes out, it is unclear by regulation which officials should have separate roadways; there ought to be an old statute."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the thirteenth year of Yuanjia (436), the relevant offices reported Censor-in-Chief Liu Shizhi's argument: "Whenever the emperor goes abroad, regulations do not clearly state which officials should have separate roadways; there ought to be an old statute."

sentences.zh: 法唯稱中丞專道，傳詔荷信，詔喚眾官，應詔者行，得制令無分別他官之文，既無畫然定則，準承有疑。

translations.literal: The law only speaks of the censor's exclusive roadway; imperial messengers bearing credentials, and summoning the host of officials—those who answer the summons proceed—but the regulations contain no text distinguishing other officials; since there is no clearly fixed rule, following precedent is doubtful."
translations.idiomatic: The law speaks only of the censor's exclusive roadway; imperial messengers bearing credentials summon officials, and those summoned proceed—but the regulations contain no text distinguishing other officials; with no clearly fixed rule, following precedent is doubtful."

sentences.zh: 謂皇太子正議東儲，不宜與眾同例，中丞應與分道。

translations.literal: He held that the Crown Prince, as the proper Eastern Heir, should not be treated like the multitude; the censor should have a separate roadway.
translations.idiomatic: He held that the Crown Prince, as the proper Eastern Heir, should not be treated like ordinary officials; the censor should have a separate roadway from him.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史、丹陽尹、建康令，並是京輦土地之主，或檢校非違，或赴救水火，事應神速，不宜稽駐，亦合分道。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Yangzhou, the Governor of Danyang, and the Magistrate of Jiankang are all masters of the capital region's territory; whether inspecting violations or rushing to fire and flood, affairs demand speed and should not be delayed—they too should have separate roadways.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspector of Yangzhou, Governor of Danyang, and Magistrate of Jiankang were all masters of the capital region; whether inspecting violations or rushing to fires and floods, their business required speed and should not be delayed—they too should have separate roadways.

sentences.zh: 又尋六門則為行馬之內，且禁衞非違，並由二衞及領軍，未詳京尹、建康令門內之徒及公事，亦得與中丞分道與不？

translations.literal: Moreover, within the six gates lies the area of the imperial escort; violations of the guard are handled by the Two Guards and the Commander-in-Chief—it is unclear whether the capital governor, magistrate, their subordinates within the gates, and official business may also have separate roadways from the censor or not."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, within the six gates lay the imperial escort zone; guard violations were handled by the Two Guards and the Commander-in-Chief—it was unclear whether the capital governor, magistrate, their subordinates within the gates, and official business might also have separate roadways from the censor.

sentences.zh: 其准參舊儀，告報參詳所宜分道』。

translations.literal: Let the old protocol be taken as standard, reported and jointly reviewed for who should have separate roadways.'"
translations.idiomatic: Let the old protocol serve as standard, reported and jointly reviewed to determine who should have separate roadways.'"

sentences.zh: 聽如臺所上，其六門內，既非州郡縣部界，則不合依門外。

translations.literal: Approval was given as the Secretariat proposed; within the six gates, since this was not the territory of a province, prefecture, or county, the rule for outside the gates did not apply.
translations.idiomatic: Approval was given as the Secretariat proposed: within the six gates, since the area was not the territory of a province, prefecture, or county, the rule for outside the gates did not apply.

sentences.zh: 其尚書令、二僕射所應分道，亦悉與中丞同。」

translations.literal: Those who should have separate roadways—the Director of the Department of State Affairs and the two Vice Directors—were all the same as for the censor."
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Department of State Affairs and the two Vice Directors who should have separate roadways were all treated the same as the censor."

sentences.zh: 孝武帝大明六年五月，詔立凌室藏冰。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixth year of Daming of Emperor Xiaowu, an edict ordered the establishment of an ice house for storing ice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixth year of Daming (462), Emperor Xiaowu ordered an ice house built for storing ice.

sentences.zh: 有司奏，季冬之月，冰壯之時，凌室長率山虞及輿隸取冰於深山窮谷涸陰沍寒之處，以納于凌陰。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: In the last month of winter, when ice is firm, the ice-house chief leads foresters and carriage attendants to take ice from deep mountains and remote valleys where shade is thick and cold penetrating, and store it in the ice vault;
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices reported: In the last month of winter, when ice had hardened, the ice-house chief would lead foresters and carriage attendants to gather ice from deep mountains and remote valleys where shade was thick and cold penetrating, and store it in the ice vault.

sentences.zh: 務令周密，無泄其氣。

translations.literal: they must make it tight and sealed, letting none of its cold escape.
translations.idiomatic: The vault had to be sealed tight so none of the cold escaped.

sentences.zh: 先以黑牡秬黍祭司寒於凌室之北。

translations.literal: First, with a black bull and black millet they sacrifice to the Cold Lord north of the ice house.
translations.idiomatic: First a black bull and black millet were offered to the Cold Lord north of the ice house.

sentences.zh: 仲春之月，春分之日，以黑羔秬黍祭司寒。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring, on the day of the spring equinox, with a black lamb and black millet they sacrifice to the Cold Lord.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring, on the day of the spring equinox, a black lamb and black millet were offered to the Cold Lord.

sentences.zh: 啟冰室，先薦寢廟。

translations.literal: The ice house is opened; offerings are first presented at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The ice house was opened, and ice was first presented at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 二廟夏祠用鑑盛冰，室一鑑，以禦溫氣蠅蚋。

translations.literal: For summer sacrifices at the two temples, mirrors hold the ice—one mirror per chamber—to ward off warm air, flies, and gnats.
translations.idiomatic: For summer sacrifices at the two temples, ice was held in mirrors—one per chamber—to ward off warm air, flies, and gnats.

sentences.zh: 三御殿及太官膳羞，並以鑑供冰。

translations.literal: The three imperial halls and the Grand Steward's prepared delicacies all received ice in mirrors.
translations.idiomatic: The three imperial halls and the Grand Steward's prepared delicacies all received ice in mirrors.

sentences.zh: 自春分至立秋，有臣妾喪，詔贈祕器。

translations.literal: From the spring equinox to the beginning of autumn, when a minister or concubine died, the court granted secret coffins by edict.
translations.idiomatic: From the spring equinox to the beginning of autumn, when a minister or concubine died, the court granted secret coffins by edict.

sentences.zh: 自立夏至立秋，不限稱數以周喪事。

translations.literal: From the establishment of summer to the beginning of autumn, the number of grants was not limited, to cover funeral needs.
translations.idiomatic: From the establishment of summer to the beginning of autumn, the number of grants was not limited, to cover funeral needs.

sentences.zh: 繕制夷盤，隨冰借給。

translations.literal: Flat trays were made and lent out with the ice as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Flat trays were prepared and lent out with the ice as needed.

sentences.zh: 凌室在樂游苑內，置長一人，保舉吏二人。

translations.literal: The ice house stood within the Leyou Park; one chief was appointed and two clerks recommended for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: The ice house stood within Leyou Park; one chief was appointed and two clerks were recommended for promotion.

sentences.zh: 三公黃閤，前史無其義。

translations.literal: The yellow doors of the Three Excellencies—earlier histories give no explanation for them.
translations.idiomatic: The yellow doors of the Three Excellencies—earlier histories give no explanation for the practice.

sentences.zh: 史臣按，禮記「士韠與天子同，公侯大夫則異」。

translations.literal: The historian comments: The Record of Rites says, "Officers' knee-covers are the same as the Son of Heaven's; dukes, marquises, and grand masters differ."
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: The Record of Rites says, "Officers' knee-covers match the Son of Heaven's; dukes, marquises, and grand masters differ."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注：「士賤，與君同，不嫌也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan annotates: "Officers are base; sharing with the ruler is not offensive."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan annotates: "Officers are lowly; sharing with the ruler is not offensive."

sentences.zh: 」夫朱門洞啟，當陽之正色也。

translations.literal: Vermilion gates open wide—the correct color facing the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion gates open wide—that is the correct color facing the sun.

sentences.zh: 三公之與天子，禮秩相亞，故黃其閤，以示謙不敢斥天子，蓋是漢來制也。

translations.literal: The Three Excellencies and the Son of Heaven are close in ritual rank; therefore their doors are yellow, to show humility and not presume upon the Son of Heaven—this is likely a Han institution.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Excellencies stood close to the Son of Heaven in ritual rank; therefore their doors were painted yellow, to show humility and not presume upon the emperor—likely a Han institution.

sentences.zh: 張超與陳公箋，「拜黃閤將有日月」是也。

translations.literal: In Zhang Chao's letter to the Duke of Chen, "bowing at the yellow doors will take days yet" refers to this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao's letter to the Duke of Chen, "bowing at the yellow doors will take days yet," refers to this practice.

sentences.zh: 史臣按：今朝士詣三公，尚書丞、郎詣令、僕射、尚書，並門外下車，履，度門閫乃納屐。

translations.literal: The historian comments: Today when court gentlemen visit the Three Excellencies, and Directors and Gentlemen of the Secretariat visit the Director, Vice Directors, and Ministers of the Secretariat, they all dismount outside the gate, walk in shoes, and only at the threshold put on slippers.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Today when court gentlemen visit the Three Excellencies, and Secretariat directors and gentlemen visit the Director, Vice Directors, and Ministers, they all dismount outside the gate, walk in shoes, and only at the threshold put on slippers.

sentences.zh: 漢世朝臣見三公，並拜。

translations.literal: In Han times court ministers seeing the Three Excellencies all bowed.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times court ministers seeing the Three Excellencies all bowed.

sentences.zh: 丞、郎見八座，皆持板揖，事在漢儀及漢舊儀，然則並有敬也。

translations.literal: Directors and gentlemen seeing the Eight Seats all held their tablets and bowed with joined hands—the matter is in the Han Protocol and Old Han Protocol; thus both involved reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Directors and gentlemen seeing the Eight Seats all held their tablets and bowed with joined hands—this appears in the Han Protocol and Old Han Protocol; both involved reverence.

sentences.zh: 陳蕃為光祿勳，范滂為主事，以公儀詣蕃，執板入閤，至坐，蕃不奪滂板，滂投板振衣而去。

translations.literal: When Chen Fan was Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Fan Pang was chief clerk, Pang came to Fan by official protocol, holding his tablet as he entered the inner door; reaching the seat, Fan did not take Pang's tablet; Pang threw down the tablet, shook his robes, and left.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Fan was Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Fan Pang chief clerk, Pang came to Fan by official protocol, tablet in hand, through the inner door; reaching the seat, Fan did not take Pang's tablet; Pang threw down the tablet, shook his robes, and left.

sentences.zh: 郭泰責蕃曰：「以階級言之，滂宜有敬；

translations.literal: Guo Tai reproached Fan, saying: "By rank, Pang owed reverence;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai reproached Fan, saying: "By rank, Pang owed reverence;

sentences.zh: 以類數推之，至閤宜省。

translations.literal: by category and number, reaching the inner door reverence should be reduced."
translations.idiomatic: by category and protocol, reaching the inner door reverence should be reduced."

sentences.zh: 」然後敬止在門，其來久矣。

translations.literal: After that, reverence stopped at the gate—the practice has been long established.
translations.idiomatic: After that, reverence stopped at the gate—a practice long established.
